decisions.why: Each is named by file or pattern, so the set is reproducible, and a record quoting a path does not run it.

decisions.summary: research/ is listed among the records.
decisions.why: FR-001's phase list places every Python file in the repository and places none under research/; a *.sh hit there still keeps the file by the test's second sentence.

decisions.summary: pool/ is listed among the records whose hits are no run, with no reason given and no 'of a feature' qualifier.
decisions.why: FR-001 places live Python under pool/ (the Mode A sheets' generators, 6, phase 4), and the block's earlier text counted pool/*.py as a caller that keeps a file; this revision moved it to the records without a word. A generator that names a harness is 'something still runs' it, and FR-001 says such a file is 'ported like any other'. Searching pool/*.py is not impossible, not implied by the GM's words, and does not defeat the amendment, whose purpose is to drop only what is not still used. Non-code under pool/ may stay excluded; pool/*.py (and the route survey, which also omits pool/) must count.

decisions.summary: tests/hooks/fixtures/, the recorded command corpus, is no run.
decisions.why: Implied by the round arbiter's ask:449-T052-inline-census carried in FR-001: a string fed to a guard as its input is no run. A rule that counted it would keep files on a use that does not exist, against 'if those are not still used'.

decisions.summary: tests/tooling/fixtures/brief_load/ holds briefs parsed as text and never executed.
decisions.why: One named directory, with its reader and test named; parsed text is not a run, the same class as the guard-input corpus.

decisions.summary: A hit in a plan-review.json quotes the file as history and is no run.
decisions.why: A named file, a review record; a quotation in it runs nothing.

decisions.summary: A hit in 'a *.md research note' is no run.
decisions.why: Sentence one keeps any file hit outside the records NAMED; research.md is already named, so this is a further, unnamed class of .md, and nothing separates it from the 'live doc' that item 9 says must not hit. The census's deletions cannot be reproduced from the stated rule, and a hit put in this class deletes a file by a judgment no one can check. It must be named by path or pattern.

decisions.summary: A hit in 'a recorded result file' is no run.
decisions.why: The principle is sound, a stored result runs nothing, but the class has no pattern or list. The block's own correction (14 files came back when a measurement's other fields had been missed) shows hand-classified hits are where this census erred. Open-ended, it widens deletion by an unmeasured amount against FR-001's 'a file something still runs is ported'. It must be named by path or pattern.

decisions.summary: Routes that never spell a path (globs and finds over specs) walk feature directories for records; none collects or runs a .py under specs/, and testpaths holds pytest to tests/.
decisions.why: A one-shot labeled premise supporting the text search, carving nothing out. Its method list omits pool/, which falls under excl-pool-dir's correction.

decisions.summary: 222 files: 140 deleted, 82 kept, each ported or ruled on at its own phase-3 task or deleted there if it no longer runs.
decisions.why: FR-001 places these files in phase 3 and the GM asked for the unused ones to go. The figures carry a one-shot date and method; 154-14=140 and 68+14=82 agree. The 140 is owed a re-count once the exclusions are corrected.

decisions.summary: The task's census is git ls-files 'specs/*.py'.
decisions.why: FR-001's first census is of Python files; the shell scripts under specs/ are in the second census at phase 3, so nothing is dropped.

decisions.summary: No spec.md, plan.md, tasks.md or measurements.json is changed; prose may still name a deleted file as history.
decisions.why: The GM asked for no record to be rewritten, and FR-001's rewrite duty covers measurement commands, which by the test name no deleted file.

decisions.summary: Census then deletion in one landing; green when the gate passes with the files gone; red recorded and ruled through make arbiter-ask; done when each deleted path's search returns no command, shell script, measurement or live doc.
decisions.why: Procedure, narrowing nothing asked. Item 9's exit is looser than the test (a .yml or other .json hit keeps a file under the test but passes the exit); that is a defect in the check, not a narrowing, and it should restate the test.

decisions.summary: figures.py, probe.py, ratchet.py, gatecost.py and gate_costs.py become l7r-gate measure in one landing; the Makefile's three call sites, its inline class_count and the guard measure_hooks ask the gate.
decisions.why: FR-001 replaces every tracked Python file and places scripts/measure/ in phase 2 and the Makefile's gate recipes in the second census; the request is that the Python all be ported. The caller list states its two search commands. Those greps match the .py filename only, so an import or a python3 -m form would not appear; the block's item 9 (git ls-files) and the replayed tests are what would catch one. Not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: RATCHETS becomes data in dev/ratchets.json with every pinned baseline and reason verbatim; run-plausible reads the same row.
decisions.why: A Python table must leave Python under FR-001, and the baselines and reasons are carried verbatim, so nothing asked for is reduced. The output consequence of the move is ruled separately under THREE PATH DIFFERENCES.

decisions.summary: The floor-net-of-load loop runs 300,000,000 iterations in Rust and calibration_s becomes 0.116 s.
decisions.why: FR-002 asks for the same verdicts and outputs, and this changes a constant the Python held, so it is ruled rather than waved through. The rule cannot be followed literally: calibration_s is the duration of one specific loop, and a Rust loop at the Python's iteration count is a different duration by the block's own reason, so at least one of iteration count or calibration_s must move or the net-of-load floor compares a Rust run against a Python time and defeats what FR-002 protects. The ruling rests on that alone, not on the block's statement that the GM's ceiling and baseline are unchanged, which the bundle cannot confirm. Two limits on the record: checklist item 10 of this same block says 'Before moving a constant. None moved.' while this decision moves one, and the block should say so; and the block does not say the 63-case differential reached this loop, which runs only at or over a ceiling, so equivalence here rests on the test_ratchets.py cases the block says are replayed.

decisions.summary: Three of the six differential differences: a named class filters the done reference warm and cold medians, and the usage line.
decisions.why: These are exactly the differences FR-002's ruled case ask:449-T75-gatecost-class names: the warm and cold medians and the usage line.

decisions.summary: The other three differential differences, which the block says differ only in naming dev/ratchets.json for the moved baseline.
decisions.why: FR-002 requires the same outputs and no ruled case in the spec covers these three. It is implied by the GM's own request as FR-001 carries it: the request ports all the Python, FR-001 and this block's item 9 require the Python file gone, so an identical string would direct the reader to a file that does not exist. Any location for the table would force a changed path, so the choice of dev/ratchets.json does not create the difference. The ruling is limited to what the block states, that the difference is confined to the path; any other changed word in those messages is not covered.

decisions.id: PROBE AND FULL FIGURES OUTSIDE THE DIFFERENTIAL
decisions.summary: probe and the figures commands that re-run measurements are held by their tests, not the differential.
decisions.why: FR-002's standard is every case the tests and suites hold, and the block says those tests are replayed. The differential is beyond what FR-002 requires. Item 6's exit, 'each tool's verdicts the Python's, by a differential', is worded wider than this decision; that is an internal inconsistency in the block, not a departure from the request.

decisions.summary: A class median over its ceiling is printed and does not refuse, tested.
decisions.why: FR-002's ruled case ask:449-T75-gatecost-class says this in the same words.

decisions.summary: Every case of test_ratchets.py, test_gate_costs.py, test_figures_deleted_engine.py, test_make_figures.py and test_probe.py is in measure/*/tests.rs, the Makefile recipe cases included.
decisions.why: FR-001 moves each tests/ file with the piece it tests, and FR-002 is held on every case those tests hold.

decisions.summary: The six measurement tools become l7r-gate measure in one landing.
decisions.why: FR-001 puts scripts/measure/ in phase 2 and the ruling ask:449-T68-scope slices it; the 'phase 3 with importers' set is removed from this slice. The stated census requires the '.py' suffix so it finds paths, not imports; that is a limit on the census, not a change to what was asked.

decisions.summary: event_log, feature_report, turn_time, fix_yield, task_phases and where_time go to phase 3 with their importers, named as expected remainders carrying the T065 clause.
decisions.why: FR-001 carries this verbatim (ask:449-T76-scope, 'no door', expected remainders, T065 clause). The widened grep now covers the importers and the shell and Rust entry points, which answers the clause.

decisions.summary: tool_yield.py also goes to phase 3, the seventh, because fix_yield.py still imports it.
decisions.why: FR-001's ruling names six; a seventh leaves phase 2. The rule cannot be followed here: a Python module cannot be replaced by Rust while a Python importer survives, and keeping both is what FR-003 forbids. It is deferred, not excused: T065 clause, named in the phase-2 close, and SC-005's census still closes on it. The premise that fix_yield.py imports it is stated with no method and could not be checked from this bundle.

decisions.summary: A usage line names the new command instead of the Python's.
decisions.why: FR-002 says same outputs. Matching would print the name of a deleted file as the way to run the tool, which defeats what a usage line is for. No verdict or exit status moves.

decisions.summary: guard-log lists firings of the same second in file order where the Python's glob gave the file system's.
decisions.why: The Python's tie order is whatever the file system returns, so it has no one value across clones and no test can hold it; FR-002 binds every case the tests and suites hold, and those are replayed. Only the order of ties moves, not which firings are listed.

decisions.summary: fresh-tally lists causes tied on a count in name order where the Python iterated a set.
decisions.why: The Python's order changes from run to run, so it disagrees with itself and 'the same output' has no referent. Physically impossible to match; a fixed order is the only faithful port.

decisions.summary: shared_text, contract_part, contract_shared and their _lines move into tests/tooling/test_bundle_shared_text.py rather than being ported with subagent_cache.py.
decisions.why: Their stated only caller is a Python test, and a Python test cannot import a Rust function, so FR-001's 'each tests/ file with the piece it tests' carries them with it. The bodies are unchanged and remain in both censuses until that file goes, so FR-002 replaces nothing here and nothing leaves the port. The grep is now named and sees imports, but its pathspec omits specs/, which FR-001 counts; a harness there would break at the deletion, a correctness risk for the landing and not a fidelity ruling.

decisions.summary: The listed cases of the slice's test files are replayed in measure/*/tests.rs.
decisions.why: This is FR-002's requirement and FR-008's test home, applied to the slice.

decisions.summary: test_runstats.py keeps the cases of tests/_gate_failures.py and of the Makefile's wiring, in Python.
decisions.why: A test of a ported tool's file outlives the tool, which on its face departs from porting it. FR-001's own words place it: each tests/ file goes with the piece it tests, and _gate_failures.py stays Python with pytest, which FR-001 ends in phase 4. The file stays in the census and SC-005 closes on it.

decisions.summary: Every specs/*/measurements*.json command running a file this task ports or deletes is rewritten in the same commit to the port and re-run.
decisions.why: FR-001 requires exactly this.

decisions.summary: The five measure tools become l7r-gate measure subcommands in one landing; the Makefile and three figure files are rewritten, and docs/spec-kit-and-reviews.md's model_trial step and rust/phases/src/driver/CLAUDE.md's pointer with them.
decisions.why: FR-001 places these files through ask:449-T068-scope, model_trial.py, popup_rounds.py and push_check_times.py in the last slice, and names the docs step. Changed since last judged: the two documents are now rewritten with the port. The search spaces are stated.

decisions.id: THE DELETION WAITS ON THE GM
decisions.summary: The ports land first; the removal of the five tools and two tests was refused by the built-in safety check, so the task stays open until the GM runs it; the two tests that import the tools stay and pass until then.
decisions.why: Nothing asked for is dropped: the exits and item 9 still require the files gone and the task cannot close without it. FR-002 binds the port before the deletion. On FR-003's 'no piece runs both': recipes, hooks and figures run only the port, and the Python's only remaining run is its own two tests, which test it and do not serve the piece. Changed since last judged: 'nothing invokes the Python' is replaced by this exact statement.

decisions.summary: replay_owing.py and depiction_replay.py go to phase 3 with modal_owed, modal_triage and claims; the other deferred tools as FR-001 and T070's row place them.
decisions.why: FR-001 carries ask:449-T77-replays and ask:449-T77-scope. Each file is still ported or deleted under the request's own terms; only its phase moves.

decisions.summary: model_trial.rs holds a Rust fold_usage, and agent_census.py's phase-3 port calls that one.
decisions.why: FR-003's unit is the piece: model-trial usage runs the Rust fold and agent_census.py, unported until phase 3, runs its Python one; neither runs both. The 40-transcript differential is the plan's stated proof. The spec's record of ask:449-T77-replays does not name fold_usage, so this rests on FR-003, not on that record.

decisions.summary: One-shot differentials of each command through the Python and the binary over the real repository.
decisions.why: FR-002's reach is every case the tests and suites hold, carried by WHAT THE TESTS REPLAY. The differentials are proof beyond that reach and take nothing from it; that run and run-all are not among them, and that usage is a seeded sample of 40, does not lower it.

decisions.id: DIFFERENCE: run in a process group
decisions.summary: run starts each session in its own process group, not its own session.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds verdicts and outputs, the line the spec's own ask:449-T77-bad-since draws. Which process session a launched child sits in is neither, and the plan states the only effect is the controlling terminal. This ground stands alone: the plan's remark about the standard library is a cost argument and is not relied on.

decisions.summary: A bad --since to popup-rounds exits 1 with empty stdout and one stderr line naming the value; which values parse, and the local-time conversion, stay the Python's.
decisions.why: Exactly FR-002's ruled case ask:449-T77-bad-since. Changed since last judged: 'refused where the Python raised' is replaced by the ruled shape, with a labeled one-shot differential over 13,876 forms showing which values parse.

decisions.summary: run-all's progress times read the local zone, as the Python's did.
decisions.why: Sameness with the Python, which FR-002 asks. Changed since last judged: the earlier block's UTC difference is gone.

decisions.summary: The Rust rows are the Rust push's CHECKS table plus the one-process run; the proof is m:push-checks-rust.
decisions.why: FR-001 names it an FR-002 ruled case under ask:449-T77-scope with that proof over the Rust push's table, and the commands the Python listed are of a shell line already removed, so the tool still measures the push as it now is.

decisions.summary: Every case of test_maps_moved.py and test_model_trial.py is in measure/*/tests.rs.
decisions.why: This is FR-002's own requirement carried out.

decisions.summary: git ls-files names none of the slice's files; every measurements command running a ported or deleted file is rewritten in the same commit and re-run.
decisions.why: FR-001's census and recorded-measurement clauses, stated without reduction.

decisions.summary: the gate's inline Python becomes l7r-gate log run/bypass/gate-bypass/land-tooling, ruff-toml and json-field in rust/gate/src/logs.rs
decisions.why: FR-001's second census puts the Makefile's gate recipes, scripts/gates/*.sh, sync-with-main.sh and land-tooling.sh in phase 2; unchanged since last judged.

decisions.summary: python3 -m pip show -q pytest-xdist replaces the import probe, the serial arm stays, and it goes with the pytest line in phase 4, named at the phase-2 close by its own search
decisions.why: FR-001 carries ask:449-T069-xdist in these terms, so placement is not reopened. Both arms measured 2026-11-09, method: the two probes run under python3 and python3 -s, -s hiding the user-site xdist with the system pip still visible. Present: both exit 0. Absent, the real package name: both exit 1, so the probe forks as the import did and 'the same question' holds on both arms. The two differ only on an interpreter without pip (the import can succeed, pip show cannot), which falls to the serial arm: a slower run, same verdict.

decisions.id: XDIST PROBE: the T065 clause's last limb
decisions.summary: the probe holds the clause on a plain Bash call, a plain Edit, Makefile parse time and an already-verified make done, but still runs on every other make done, including one picking no Python test, until T071 and phase 4
decisions.why: FR-001 says the probe carries the T065 clause and the block concedes one limb, so this is a narrowing whether or not it is labeled one. Limb by limb: Bash call, Edit, parse time and already-verified are held and excepted from nothing. The make-done limb cannot be held inside the ruled form: the ruling fixes a probe that is itself a Python start on the pytest line, and that line runs on every make done that passes already-verified, so while the line runs the probe runs. The exception is the physically-impossible case, not an awkward one, and it does not gut the clause's purpose, since the same recipe starts python3 -m l7r.diagram.ci incremental and pytest on that make done regardless. It ends where the block says, at T071 and phase 4. The premise that done always reaches test-full is the block's one-shot reading of the Makefile dated 2026-11-09; the bundle bars re-reading the repository, so it was weighed as labeled and not re-measured.

decisions.summary: test-cohort-gate, test-land-tooling and test-claims-gate's index edit use jq; test-entry-gate's edit is a literal shell replacement
decisions.why: ask:449-T052-inline-census moves these four suites to phase 2, and removing their inline Python is what that asks; unchanged since last judged.

decisions.summary: make audit's four recipes, buildspec/run.sh until T73, and the two fixtures over claims.py and record_owed.py remain after T069
decisions.why: Each is placed by the accepted spec: FR-001's ask:449-T069-suites names the two fixtures and make audit's four recipes with their phases, and FR-001a deletes buildspec. Unchanged since last judged.

decisions.summary: a record's bytes are the Python's, numbers included: logs.rs's dumps writes json.dumps's form and a float as repr writes it, each form pinned by a test, no exception
decisions.why: FR-002 held whole. The earlier text excepted serde's exponent form on a one-shot grep of existing logs; that exception is gone and the block says so. The rule governs every form, not only the parenthetical's examples. Python 3.14 measured 2026-11-09, method: json.dumps on each value: 5e-05, 1e+16, 1e+22, 0.0001, 1.0, -0.0, 1.2345678901234568e+17, DEL escaped as backslash-u007f, non-BMP as a surrogate pair, NaN and Infinity written bare, and an integer past 64 bits written whole. The tests should pin those too.

decisions.summary: the census's phase-2 share prints only What stays' sites; measurement commands running a ported or deleted file are rewritten and re-run in the same commit
decisions.why: FR-001's second census over the phase-2 set and the four suites, and FR-001's rule on recorded measurements; unchanged since last judged. The probe is outside this pattern, which does not match -m, and the XDIST block assigns it its own search.

decisions.summary: T071 is preflight.py alone; the test planner's files are out of it (goal, exits and Done rewritten to that).
decisions.why: FR-001's ask:449-T071-scope replaces T067's placement: selection, incremental, cover_changed and the rest go in phase 4, preflight.py is ported in T071. The earlier block's planner exit and its no-.py-under-ci measure are gone.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate preflight holds the derived files, the record, the quick tier, the stray-probe refusal, the snapshot, the check, what the gate rolled and the gate-write guard's question; the Makefile's four calls and gate_write_hooks.rs call it.
decisions.why: This is the port FR-001 orders in phase 2 for preflight.py, called once a process per FR-006.

decisions.summary: scripts/gates/preflight.py stays at its path, cut to --cover (changed lines' coverage), asked only by make preflight, gone in phase 4 with pytest.
decisions.why: FR-001: 'preflight.py is ported in T071, its pytest-reading checks behind one named door until phase 4'. --cover reads coverage.py's data and is the only thing left behind the door; the earlier block's Python-reading --same-py is no longer in it.

decisions.summary: make done passes --no-coverage, as the Python's make done did (feature 405 T47, D25), so no make done starts the door.
decisions.why: Stated as preserving existing behavior, which FR-002 requires; that premise is the plan's and cannot be measured from this bundle. If the Python's make done did not already skip it, this is a behavior change owing its own FR-002 case. It starts less Python than FR-001 permits, not more.

decisions.summary: The two-version question (does a .py file's two versions differ only where the gate does not look) is a new verb --same-program on codeid.py, one batch, at most once a run, only when a .py file outside the byte-hashed areas changed.
decisions.why: Classed narrowing because FR-001 lets only preflight.py's pytest-reading checks stay Python and this check is not one; the spec names --debug-free-equal on codeid.py and does not name this verb. Against the request ('should probably all be ported to Rust ... making this a Rust codebase'): nothing leaves the port's scope, the question is about Python source, codeid.py goes in phase 4 and SC-005's censuses must return nothing, so it ends with the last .py. FR-002 binds the answer to the Python's, and the reference is CPython's own parser, the class FR-001 already settled for codeid.py (ask:449-T062-py-id, its .py id is Python's own ast.dump, asked by the Rust gate by path; --debug-free-equal the same). Purpose: the request came from measured Python cost on hooks and a one-line Rust edit's make done; a Rust edit moves no .py file, so the SC-002 case starts none.

decisions.summary: The verb may start from the gate-write guard, on an Edit while a gate is running and such a file changed.
decisions.why: Adjudicated apart from the make done branch. FR-001 forbids codeid.py on a plain Bash call or a plain Edit; the spec's own engine_edit.py clause reads plain Edit as one 'with none live', and ask:449-phase1-tools-by-path allows a rare branch. With no gate running the block starts nothing, so a plain Edit starts no Python.

decisions.summary: The verb may start on the tree check of a make done whose tree moved such a file.
decisions.why: Adjudicated apart from the guard branch. It matches the FR-001 T065 clause's shape (no Python on a make done whose change holds no file it reads) and is one process for the run; a Rust-only change never reaches it, which is the case the request's cost complaint and SC-002 name.

decisions.summary: hamlet_path's import of l7r.diagram.tools.claims stays inside --cover, reached only by make preflight, Python by path until phase 3, never on a make done.
decisions.why: Under FR-001's ask:449-T067-scope ceiling ('staying Python by path until phase 3 and only on a make done whose change holds a file claims reads'); never on a make done is stricter than that ceiling and narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: raw_areas asks the stamp's --raw-match as the Python did, so a page_browser docstring edit is called as before; any correction goes through its own case.
decisions.why: FR-002: same verdicts by default, with the correction route it names.

decisions.summary: --cover's JSON answer is new, between the Rust and Python halves; each line the phase prints is the Python's.
decisions.why: An internal interface that exists only because of the door FR-001 orders; FR-002 binds the printed output, which is held.

decisions.summary: The phase's and tree's cases move to preflight/tests.rs; the door's stay in test_preflight.py, with one new case for --cover and one for --same-program.
decisions.why: FR-001 'each tests/ file with the piece it tests'; the two new cases only test what this task changes.

decisions.summary: Done is the differential over the real repository with no mismatch, preflight.py holding only --cover and what it calls, and every recorded measurement command naming a ported or deleted file rewritten and re-run in the same commit.
decisions.why: FR-002's same-verdicts requirement and FR-001's recorded-measurement clause, nearly word for word.

decisions.summary: Leaf first by imports, callers reach the binary once a process or in a batch; a red exit goes to make arbiter-ask; no work budget.
decisions.why: ask:449-T062-order, FR-006, SC-002 and the arbiter's standing role; the budget line settles nothing the request addressed.

decisions.summary: Under tests/ only ten named test files, the six modules they and pytest load, and the non-Python directories stay; every other Python test is deleted.
decisions.why: The GM said 'delete everything except that group', and FR-001b records the group by subject (the sweep of the hand-drawn sheets and the checks of agent files, CLAUDE.md files and other documents) and delegates naming it to this plan. Each of the ten is one of those by name; the six helpers are what makes them loadable. The bundle does not hold the group as it was shown to the GM, so membership is checked against FR-001b's record of it, not against that text.

decisions.summary: selection.py, gate_plugin.py, incremental.py, pool_readers.py, gate_config.py's two readers, scripts/gates/pool-readers.py, cover_changed.py, refresh_baseline.py and preflight.py are deleted here rather than in the commit removing pytest; the kept suite runs whole with no selection and no coverage.
decisions.why: FR-001b settles it: the planner and the coverage floor over Python go with the tests, in place of ask:449-T071-scope's commit. With them gone a whole run of the kept group is the only remaining form, and the GM exempted that group from the deletion.

decisions.summary: check-function-cap.py, check-duplicate-defs.py, ruff format, pyrefly and check stale-dirs are deleted.
decisions.why: The GM asked which static checks on the Python can go away and approved the answer ('Sounds good, please proceed with that'); FR-001b carries it. Nothing here retains or adds a check. The approved list itself is not in the bundle.

decisions.summary: The .py arm of check file-scale's line bar goes; the .rs bar and the per-directory file count stay.
decisions.why: The only text changed since the BLOCKED round. The earlier block kept the bar whole by calling the list's 'Python-file size bar' a mislabel, which completed the GM's thought against what was approved. This block deletes the part the approved list named. The .rs bar and the directory count are not checks on the Python, so keeping them narrows nothing the GM asked about.

decisions.summary: ruff check stays, narrowed to E9, F63, F7 and F82.
decisions.why: Taken against the request and not only the spec: the GM's words were a question, 'which of our static checks ... can also go away now?', so a list leaving one standing does not contradict them, and FR-001b records 'ruff check stays, narrowed to outright errors' under the GM's approval of that answer. The plan's four rule families only spell out 'outright errors'. It keeps no behavior the GM asked to change, and it does reduce what the check reports. Item 1's goal sentence reads more broadly than this and is loosely worded; the decision is the operative text.

decisions.summary: The commit before the removal is tagged python-tests-before-removal so a port can read the cases it replays; new Rust still owes 100% line coverage.
decisions.why: The tag removes nothing and preserves nothing in the tree: the deletion the GM asked for still happens. It is how FR-002's 'on every case its tests and its suites hold' stays reachable after the tests are gone. The coverage clause restates FR-004.

decisions.summary: Tag, then delete the tests and Python-only tooling in one commit with the Makefile, land.py, the guards and the crates edited to stop reading them.

Whether reason_ok's swap to shared::escape::enough changes behavior rests on the differential (48 check-bundle cases, escapes given, none differing but the ruled one). The plan claims nothing beyond that, and this review does not either.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate rust learns nested crates: transitive path-dependency verdict keys, nearest-directory ownership, uncovered and dead over the nested crates, and one shared cover-gate build.
decisions.why: Without it, a nested crate's checks would never run again, so the tooling has to follow the split. The shared coverage build serves the GM's 'reuse things which have already been compiled'.

decisions.summary: Checks and scripts that read the gate's files by path name the new locations. Not repointed: three historical 'moved from' comments, a doc naming a file deleted before T92, and two scratch-fixture paths. The five push.rs selftest messages are corrected under ask:449-T92-messages.
decisions.why: The message changes are exactly what ask:449-T92-messages rules. The mentions left alone are history, a file already gone, and synthetic fixtures, and no clause asks for any of them to change. Enumeration defect: the '118 rust/gate/src/ mentions outside specs/' figure and 'a grep of the split tree finds no other' name no command, so their search space cannot be checked (for example, whether Makefiles and shell scripts were covered).

decisions.summary: In the 102-invocation behavior comparison on the pre-split fixture clone, one verdict differs. check research-pointers' fixture list now names the crate paths, so on the pre-split tree it reads the moved files' fixtures as unexempted. The exits call this 'the ruled path difference'.
decisions.why: The plan's 'ruled' label is wrong, so this ruling is mine. ask:449-T92-messages covers only a path in a message the Rust itself writes, and it binds every other verdict byte for byte. A fixture or exemption list is data the check reads, and what differs here is a verdict, so the ask does not reach it. It is still legitimate on physical grounds. The split the GM asked for moves the files. A check that finds fixtures by path cannot exempt them at a path that no longer exists. Keeping the old list would make the check refuse correct work on the split tree, which is the case FR-002 itself carves out (constitution XIV). The difference shows up only when the new binary runs on the old tree. On the tree each binary is built for, the verdict is unchanged. The exits line should say 'the path difference ruled in this plan review', not cite the ask.

decisions.summary: No build jobs cap is set: a cold build peaked at 3,791 MB, under the 10 GB cap.
decisions.why: This is a measured resource decision and touches no requested behavior.

decisions.summary: The guard suite's real-build case runs the clone's own wrapper on the clone's own tree into the wrapper's own target (the one make hooks-test's l7r-guard.sh trace/deps calls build), no longer deletes the kept binary to force a build, and judges that the kept binary answers; build/self-check/keep paths stay covered by cases 1-6 on the fake cargo.
decisions.why: FR-011's T94 clause and SC-006 ask that the landing's hook suites reuse what make done has already built rather than build it again; the GM 2026-11-11: 'being able to reuse things which have already been compiled ... is exactly what we should be doing'. This resolves the earlier BLOCKED text, which kept a forced rebuild (deleting the kept binary) of what the hooks-test wrapper call had already built and rested that on the premise 'make done builds no release guard binary'; the new block retracts the premise and names the shared target. Dropping the forced build is the very behavior SC-006 removes, not a narrowing of test coverage; a changed guard crate still gets its one real build.

decisions.summary: The case's last check no longer pipes from sleep 30 (which the suite waited on every run) and judges in the suite's own shell, so its ok/bad reaches the counts (30 cases became 31).
decisions.why: Removes 30 s of waiting from every landing (the GM's 'the iteration loops do indeed need to be faster'); counting the check is enforcement of a check that already existed, not new scope.

decisions.summary: The sync-with-main suite is left as it is: 19.3 s alone, parts already parallel, builds no crate; its landing time is shared CPU, and phase scheduling is deferred to the measurement after T93.
decisions.why: FR-011's T94 clause is about suites rebuilding what make done built; the trace shows this suite builds nothing, so nothing in that clause is left undone. Deferring the scheduling question matches the GM's 'then we will stop and measure again ... what the next most low-hanging fruit is'.

decisions.summary: A warm-tree make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 run of all 53 suites wrote no build output and made no new target directory; the suites reach cargo only through the named wrappers and shims (search space: git grep over tests/hooks), the guard suite's real-build case having been the one second target.
decisions.why: SC-006 covers all of make done's hook suites, not only the two slowest; this is the verification that the requested property holds across them, with both a name search and a mechanism census stated. Enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: The Rust checks' runner becomes its own crate rust/gate/crates/rustc (over core and tree only) with its own binary l7r-rust, built and run by l7r-gate.sh rust <cmd>, stale only over core, tree, rustc, rust/guard and the workspace manifests; the wrapper's staleness scan gains rust/guard and touches the binary after a build.
decisions.why: The before-figures (labeled, observed 2026-11-11) attribute 40 s of a core edit's 49 s to the wrapper rebuilding the full release binary before any test ran. Splitting the runner off is the GM's 'splitting the gate crate into several crates' and FR-011's 'an edit recompiles one crate and what depends on it'; adding rust/guard to the staleness scan fixes a stale-binary hole. Nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: A crate's test, cover, lint and dead rerun only when its key moves: its sources, path dependencies (followed against every crate), workspace manifests, and the tree paths its tests read at run time as declared in [package.metadata.l7r] reads; a crate whose sources name the tree and declare nothing is refused with the fix named.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 'reuse ... the results of tests which have already run' and FR-011's reuse of a passed result. Keying on declared runtime reads makes a crate rerun when its tests' inputs change, which keeps a reused green truthful rather than narrowing reuse. The refusal of an undeclared reader is behavior, but its only reach is the soundness of the requested reuse: delete the reuse and it has nothing to check, so it enforces the request. (The incidental '1,105 lines' in this bullet carries no observation label; it narrates why a file was split and no decision rests on it.)

decisions.summary: When the first key moved, test and test-counters consult a second key: the crate's compiled test binaries plus every non-source input; a binary that already passed runs nothing, and the counting build shares the plain build's verdict where the binary is byte-identical (every crate but core and phases, observed 2026-11-11).
decisions.why: This is FR-011's literal 'run only the crates whose compiled test binary changed since their last green run'.

decisions.summary: Content ids are git blob ids whether a file is edited, staged or committed, and the last eight green keys are kept.
decisions.why: Implementation detail of the reuse so a commit, or an edit taken back, does not re-run what already passed; serves the request's reuse and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The only ways to run every crate fresh: FRESH=1 REASON="..." on make rust-test, make static or make counters-inert (refused without a two-word reason, logged through LOGESCAPE/guard_log), or make done FULL=1, which sets L7R_RUST_FRESH and runs bypass-audit first (asks for a reason at a terminal, cancels on empty, refuses with no terminal or from a backgrounded call, records the reason or the refusal via l7r-gate log bypass). FULL on the three targets and INCREMENTAL=0 anywhere no longer turn reuse off; the idle run's make done INCREMENTAL=0 keeps reuse for the Rust checks; no new guard.
decisions.why: FR-011: 'every crate at once only through an escape that states a reason and is recorded', and the GM's 'our tooling must enforce this'. Both named escapes now state a reason and are recorded (the previous round's text left make done FULL=1 as 'its own logged path' without saying it states a reason; the block now spells that out), and the block names no third unlogged route. Retiring FULL and INCREMENTAL=0 as reuse switches closes unrecorded escapes, which is enforcement of the request. The idle run keeping reuse extends reuse to a path the request does not mention rather than narrowing anything asked ('reuse ... results of tests which have already run ... is exactly what we should be doing'). Enforcement by making the slow run unreachable without a recorded reason satisfies FR-011's stated mechanism, so 'no new guard' narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The l7r-gate rust verbs answer byte for byte as before except the kept-result line (now also for test, a named crate and a second-key hit) and the new undeclared-reader refusal.
decisions.why: The only output changes are the reuse report and the refusal, both parts of the requested reuse. FR-002 binds ports and T93 is not one, so its citation is loose, but that is not a fidelity finding.

decisions.summary: T93 is not a straight port under FR-001c and keeps its review; ordered after T92 and T94; exits and done-measures are the after-figures, make static, make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1, make done green, and FRESH=1 refused without a reason and logged with one; FR-004 coverage holds for the new crate.
decisions.why: Keeping the review applies FR-001c correctly (no Python is replaced). The order and exits follow FR-011's T92-T94 and SC-006's re-measurement. The FR-003 to FR-004 citation fix corrects the coverage constraint to the requirement that carries it.

decisions.summary: The gate binary builds in a new [profile.tool] (inherits release, incremental on) instead of release; [profile.release] left at cargo's default so the hamlet engine's cargo run --release is untouched.
decisions.why: This is the means of cutting the exact cost FR-012 names for T95 (the full l7r-gate release binary rebuilt after any gate crate edit). Leaving release alone keeps the engine's build and output unchanged, which SC-007 and the plan's no-map-moved answer require.

decisions.id: T95-D2 guard and l7r-rust share the profile
decisions.summary: l7r-guard and l7r-rust move to the tool profile with l7r-gate; the guard wrapper, its self-check and kept copy read tool/l7r-guard.
decisions.why: This reaches past the one binary FR-012 names for T95. It is still inside the GM's 'performance efficiency of the Rust code that we already have' (the Rust tooling's own costs), and the wrappers share one build. The block measured that it holds outputs: identical stdout and exit codes on four hook inputs, median and p90 latency no worse. It changes how the guard is built, not what it decides.

decisions.summary: test-l7r-guard.sh's fake cargo refuses a build without --profile tool; one case each in test-make-only-hooks.sh and make_only_hooks/tests.rs pins a tool/l7r-gate path; make_only_hooks code unchanged (matches by name).
decisions.why: These tests fail only if the wrapper drifts back to release or the make-only guard stops covering the moved binaries (FR-005). They enforce the requested change, so they are not added scope.

decisions.summary: codegen-units=256, opt-level 1, lto=off and the dev profile rejected on the bench.
decisions.why: These are design choices among ways to cut the same cost. The ones rejected for slowing the verbs were rejected to keep FR-012's 'held to every output and verdict' and no-slower runs.

decisions.summary: The rust-lld linker (about 0.4 s more) is left out of this landing.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks that the cost be cut and measured lower (SC-007), not cut as far as it can go. The cost falls from tens of seconds to about 2 s without it, so leaving out a further optimization narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The hamlet engine's run and bench.rs's baseline build (an older commit whose manifest may not define the profile) stay on release; l7r-guard bench compares verdicts, not times.
decisions.why: Neither is the T95 cost. Keeping the engine on release protects generator output. The bench baseline builds an old manifest and compares verdicts only, so its profile does not touch anything FR-012 asks for.

decisions.summary: T95 goes first of T95-T99 because T96 touches the same profile settings.
decisions.why: The GM approved the five options together and gave no order, so sequencing them is inside the request.

decisions.id: T95-D8 make static remainder left to T96
decisions.summary: After an edit, make static still takes 103 s (core) or 65 s (claims). About 2 s of that is the gate rebuild; the rest (lint, coverage and dead-code reruns from T93's key) is left as T96's measurement.
decisions.why: T95's FR-012 cost is the gate binary rebuild only, and that is what T95 cuts. The remainder is not T95's to cut. Aside for the GM: T96's FR-012 remit is 'a test binary rebuilt after a one-line edit', and the lint and dead-code part of the remainder is not named in any of T95-T99. That belongs to the GM's 'stop and measure again' step, not to a T95 finding.

decisions.summary: The tool/ target is 485 MB against release's 141 MB, a cold tool build takes 34.1 s, and the first make rust-test after landing reruns every crate once (88 s).
decisions.why: FR-012 leaves a fresh worktree's cold build as it is, and the GM said 'I'm less concerned about the one-time ramp-up for a fresh clone'. Disk use and a one-time rerun are costs, not departures from what was asked.

decisions.summary: Exits: green on the guard suite, rust-test, static, identical verbs and land; red is set down and a cannot-be-done claim goes to make arbiter-ask. Budget is one landing. The generator perf tools are declared not applicable.
decisions.why: This is the procedure for carrying out the request. The generator tools do not apply because no engine code changes. Notes, which do not block: (1) the 'runs no slower and says the same' comparison names 8 verbs and gives no census of l7r-gate's verbs, so it may be a sample. SC-007's 'every check it touches' is also carried by the 19 crates of make rust-test, the 31-case guard suite, make static and make land, all green on the change. A later round may ask for the census. (2) The block's 'before' figures (core 38-45 s, owed 19-21 s, claims 8.0-8.6 s) differ from the figures the GM was shown ('claims 13.9 s, owed 8.4 s, core 10 s'), and the block does not explain the gap. FR-012's same-command rule is met because bench.py measured both sides, and the cost is lower against either baseline, but the GM may want the difference explained.

decisions.summary: The GM's 13.9 s for claims was a test rebuild after a core edit and its revert (rebuilt through core, tree, owed, plan); a claims-only one-line edit costs 3.8-3.9 s, split into compile and GNU ld link.
decisions.why: Answers the GM's own 'Tell me more about these numbers' and locates the cost FR-012 names (T96); it narrows nothing: the core-edit path is also measured after the change (make static after a core edit, links 27-61 s to 3.7-4.1 s).

decisions.summary: Every cargo build links with the toolchain's rust-lld via one repository-root .cargo/config.toml.
decisions.why: The means of cutting the cost FR-012 asks cut; outputs held (coverage reports identical, 19 crates green, guard suite 37/37, 8 l7r-gate verbs identical).

decisions.summary: The dev profile (inherited by test) keeps line tables only for debug info.
decisions.why: A means of cutting link time and output size; the plan records coverage reports unchanged, so FR-012's hold on outputs is kept.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate.sh, l7r-guard.sh and rustc.rs run cargo from the tree's root so every build (cover's show-env included) reads the same config; coverage build keeps lld.
decisions.why: Implementation needed for the change to apply uniformly and not split build flags; changes no verdict or output.

decisions.summary: The config names the 1.87.0 gcc-ld directory; a moved toolchain makes l7r-gate.sh refuse, l7r-guard.sh keep its last good binary, and a rust-test fail, each naming the fix.
decisions.why: The approach's own failure handling for the path it hard-codes, not a carve-out from the request: on the toolchain the tree is built with, no verdict or output changes; it turns what would be an obscure link failure into a named one. No reach beyond the builds T96 changes.

decisions.summary: .cargo/config.toml joins the kept-result key's workspace files and rustc's declared reads.
decisions.why: Keeps FR-011's result reuse correct under the new config file (a config change reruns every crate); serves the requested reuse rather than adding scope.

decisions.summary: Release and tool profiles do not inherit dev's debug setting; the hamlet engine's code generation is unchanged, its release build relinks once with lld.
decisions.why: Confines the change to the tooling build time FR-012 targets; no map or engine output moves.

decisions.summary: opt-level 0 (option c) rejected as buying less; instrumenting only our crates for coverage (option e), the '.' reads and the dead-code key left to T100.
decisions.why: Choice among means for T96's cost; the deferred items are make static's coverage and dead-code reruns, which the GM filed as T100 and FR-012 assigns there, so nothing asked is dropped.

decisions.summary: After figures by the same make rust-test command (3.8 s to about 1 s for a claims edit) and make static after core and claims edits (103.3 to ~75 s, 64.8 to ~56 s), outputs re-verified.
decisions.why: SC-007's re-measure by the same command and verdict hold; every figure carries a one-shot observed/method label.

decisions.summary: A new guard, scratch-sweep-hooks, starts at most one detached sweep a day from UserPromptSubmit; make scratch-sweep [DRY=1] runs one on demand.
decisions.why: The GM: 'Fix those leaks as well' of the session scratch under /tmp/claude-1000; FR-013 asks for a sweep of finished sessions' scratch. A recurring sweep, with make as the one entry point (FR-005), is how the leak is fixed and nothing beyond it.

decisions.summary: A session directory goes when its transcript AND everything inside it have been unchanged three days; a session directory with no transcript and a loose top-level entry go when nothing inside changed in three days.
decisions.why: FR-013: swept 'once its transcript has been idle for days, never a live session's'. Also reading the directory's own contents is how 'never a live session's' is kept when a subagent writes there without touching the session's transcript, so it carries the spec's own constraint. Directories with no transcript and loose entries are scratch under /tmp/claude-1000 too, part of the 38 GB leak the GM said to fix, and are judged by the same idle rule.

decisions.summary: Three days idle, swept once a day, as GUESS knobs (SCRATCH_SWEEP_DAYS) with seams for the tests.
decisions.why: FR-013 says 'idle for days' and gives no number. Three days fills that in and also meets the relay's 'don't touch dirs younger than a few hours'.

decisions.summary: Always kept: the prompting session's directory, every session registered as running in ~/.claude/sessions/<pid>.json whose pid still runs and whose procStart matches, and any entry a live process holds as its cwd, binary or open file.
decisions.why: This is FR-013's 'never a live session's' itself. A session paused over a weekend has an idle transcript but is still live, so the registry and /proc checks are what make that clause hold.

decisions.summary: Where the session registry cannot be read, no session directory is judged at all.
decisions.why: Without the registry the sweep cannot tell a live session paused past three days from a finished one. Sweeping anyway would break FR-013's 'never a live session's', which is the GM's own constraint, so the exception is implied by the request's own words. It covers session directories only, and loose entries are still swept. Checked 2026-11-11 with ls -la ~/.claude/sessions/ on this container: the registry is present and readable by uid 1000, and its records carry pid and procStart. So the fail-safe is not the default on the machine that has the leak.

decisions.summary: Nothing is removed where /proc cannot be read.
decisions.why: Without /proc the sweep cannot see which entries live processes hold, so removing would risk exactly what FR-013 forbids. The exception is implied by 'never a live session's'. On this Linux container /proc is readable, so the case is a fail-safe and does not hollow out the sweep.

decisions.summary: Any tree containing a directory the sweep cannot read is kept.
decisions.why: The sweep cannot establish that nothing inside changed in three days, or that no live process holds it, without reading the tree. Removing it would need the idle test that FR-013 sets as the condition for sweeping, and that test cannot be run here, so the rule cannot be applied as written. The case is per-tree and does not exempt the readable scratch the leak is made of.

decisions.summary: Links are never followed or descended: a link inside a removed tree is deleted as itself with its target untouched, and a link at the root or among a project's sessions is left.
decisions.why: The scope is scratch UNDER /tmp/claude-1000, and following a link could delete or judge something outside it. A link at the root or in a session slot holds no disk itself, and its idleness and liveness could only be judged by following it out of the root, which the request's scope forbids. Leaving it frees nothing less, so the leak fix's purpose is untouched. Links inside a removed tree are still removed, so no scratch survives through them.

decisions.summary: The hook reads only the stamp's age and starts the sweep with setsid -f; the sweep takes a lock, rechecks the stamp and writes it before walking. Cost recorded with labeled figures.
decisions.why: This is how the sweep runs (cost and concurrency) and settles nothing about what is or is not swept. All figures carry observed-date and method labels.

decisions.summary: Every removal and the day's total are written to the guard log with sizes.
decisions.why: It makes the requested sweep checkable and adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: A dry run on this machine would remove 110 entries, 11.0 MB; the large trees were already cleared by the laptop session.
decisions.why: This is a labeled measurement. It does not conflict with FR-013's 'the existing pile is left to the GM's laptop session': the plan does not do a separate cleanup of the pile, the laptop session has already cleared the large trees, and the forward sweep that FR-013 asks for applies its idle rule to whatever is there.

decisions.summary: A project directory left empty is kept.
decisions.why: A project directory is a container for many sessions, not a finished session's scratch, which is the subject of FR-013 and SC-008. Empty, it holds no meaningful disk.

decisions.summary: Checklist part A: goal, constraints, order after T96 beside T101 (T102 extends to the cargo cache), exits through make land and arbiter-ask, and a done measure (504 tests passed, the dry run).
decisions.why: It restates FR-013 and records process, and narrows nothing. Its figures are labeled.

decisions.summary: Every TempDir::new removes each l7r-{tag}-p{pid}-{seq} directory of its tag in its parent whose pid has no /proc entry, and hookrun.sh removes l7r-hooks-suite-<guard>-p<pid>.* of a gone pid before each run; neither sweep has any age condition.
decisions.why: Arbiter check 1: yes, the liveness test can remove a directory a live process still holds. The pid in the name is the CREATOR's, but the holders are mostly its descendants: under make rust-test the runner's TempDir is the TMPDIR of cargo and every test binary, and hookrun.sh's suite directory is held by the suite it runs. Kill the creator alone (SIGKILL, or a TERM aimed at its pid by a watchdog or timeout rather than at its group, which by the paragraph's own premise the Rust runner does not handle) and the children live on; the next run of the same tag or guard finds no /proc entry and deletes the directory under them. The plan calls pid reuse 'the safe way to be wrong' and never names this unsafe way. The request names exactly this risk and the rule against it: 'don't touch dirs younger than a few hours (a running gate may own them)'. The sweep deletes directories of any age, and the plan never mentions that clause. Substituting a pid test for the GM's age floor because it looks more precise is not a ground under MODE 1: an age floor is not impossible, nothing else the GM wrote contradicts it, and it does not defeat the purpose (the pile stays bounded). What the plan must carry: the GM's floor, so that neither sweep touches a directory younger than a few hours, whatever its pid.

decisions.summary: TempDir names directories l7r-{tag}-p{pid}-{seq} and sweeps only that form, so the pre-T101 l7r-{tag}-{pid}-{seq} pile (and mktemp-suffixed names) is never touched and stays the laptop session's to delete.
decisions.why: Arbiter check 2: yes, as long as the match is anchored. An exact tag, then '-p', digits, '-', digits, then end of name cannot match the old l7r-{tag}-{pid}-{seq} form (no 'p') or a mktemp XXXXXX suffix (no hyphen inside it). The bundle shows the NAME FORM, not the matcher, so this ruling assumes an anchored match. The unit test's old-form and other-tag fixtures pin that on the Rust side, and test-parts.sh's old-form fixture pins it on the shell side. Leaving the pile alone follows the request's 'leave that alone unless he asks you to' and FR-013's last sentence.

decisions.summary: A pid reused by a live process keeps the directory carrying that pid.
decisions.why: Arbiter check 3: yes, by construction. A /proc/<pid> entry that is present, a zombie's included, means the directory is kept, and the unit test's live-pid fixture and test-parts.sh's live-run fixture go through that same branch. The only cost is a leftover lasting until the pid is freed and a later run of that tag, which errs in the direction the request asks for.

decisions.summary: hookrun.sh stops the suite and exits through its EXIT trap on INT or TERM, and sweeps gone-pid suite directories; a unit test sweeps a fixture of gone-pid, live-pid, other-tag and old-form directories; tests/hooks/test-parts.sh runs hookrun.sh beside a gone run's, a live run's and an old-form directory and stops one with TERM, two of its cases red against the earlier hookrun.sh.
decisions.why: Arbiter check 4: they match, with two gaps in what is pinned. They are recorded here and do not block. (a) test-parts.sh sends only TERM, so the INT half of hookrun.sh's trap, which the plan claims, is pinned by nothing. (b) The unit test has an 'another tag's' fixture but the shell pin has no other-guard fixture, so whether hookrun.sh's sweep is confined to its own <guard> goes unchecked. 'Two of its cases red against the earlier hookrun.sh' is consistent: only the gone-run removal and the TERM exit could fail against a version that neither sweeps nor traps, while the live and old-form cases pin against a sweep that reaches too far. These tests enforce the request ('add a test that pins it') and are in scope.

decisions.summary: Left line, SIGKILL part: a process killed by SIGKILL leaves its directory until the next of its kind runs.
decisions.why: The request says 'remove it on exit, including failure and interrupt', and FR-013 says 'removed on exit, failure and panic included'. No code runs in a process on SIGKILL, so removing the directory at that exit cannot be done at all. Removing it on a later run is the most that is possible, and under make rust-test the runner's per-run TMPDIR already holds every test's scratch for that run.

decisions.summary: Left line, INT/TERM part: the paragraph treats SIGINT and SIGTERM 'as surely as SIGKILL', so a Rust process (the make rust-test runner, a test binary, a production command) stopped by an interrupt or a TERM leaves its directory until the next of its kind runs instead of removing it on exit.
decisions.why: MODE 1's rule on bundled cases: one argument stretched over two unlike things. SIGKILL cannot be caught. SIGINT and SIGTERM can, and only their DEFAULT handling skips Drop. The plan itself traps INT and TERM in hookrun.sh and parts.sh, stopping the children and then removing the directory, which shows the Rust runner's counterpart is possible. The request names this case word for word: 'remove it on exit, including failure and interrupt (trap / ...)'. Under FR-013 ('removed on exit') an interrupted process has exited and its directory has not been removed. Being harder to do in Rust, or the sweep already bounding the pile, does not make the exception legitimate. What the plan must carry: on an interrupt or a TERM, the Rust side removes what it made at exit, as the shell side already does, so that the Left line keeps only SIGKILL.

decisions.summary: The cargo target cache is pruned by extending T103's daily sweep (same lock, stamp, live-process check, log and make scratch-sweep [DRY=1]).
decisions.why: FR-013 and the GM's 'Fix those leaks as well' ask that the cache stop growing without bound and leave the mechanism open. A periodic prune is a direct means to that end and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Within a store, each crate's variants beyond its newest four are removed once idle three days.
decisions.why: This bounds growth from moved paths and changed flags, which serves SC-008. One caveat: the premise that cargo makes a new variant only on a path or flag change is stated, not measured, and the bundle does not show how variants are grouped. Per-run-named crates (l7r_fixture_broken_<n>) would escape a per-name cap. What covers the measured leak is the dry run, which reports the l7r_fixture variants removed, and the fact that the source is gone. The cap's adequacy therefore rests on the dry run, not on the rule as written. That is a design caveat, not a narrowing: nothing the GM asked for is excluded.

decisions.summary: A build directory named for no live tree is removed whole after three idle days. The mirror's and every clone's directories are never removed whole. Where the clones directory cannot be read, nothing is removed whole.
decisions.why: Live trees' directories are still variant-pruned, so growth stays bounded. The protections keep the guard's binary and live builds safe, in line with the relayed caution not to touch what a running gate may own. Nothing asked for is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Anything a live process holds is kept, as in T103.
decisions.why: A safety condition in line with the relayed 'don't touch dirs ... a running gate may own'. It does not limit the leak fix.

decisions.summary: The sweep's first run removes stale content already in the cache: about 2.4 GB, including six stale build directories.
decisions.why: FR-013's 'the existing pile is left to the GM's laptop session' comes from the relayed message, where 'the existing pile' is defined in the preceding sentence as the /tmp l7r-* scratch directories (T101). The GM's only words on the cargo cache are 'Fix those leaks as well', and a sweep that fixes a growth leak necessarily removes what is stale. T103 did the same for /tmp/claude-1000 and was cleared. The three-day idle threshold and the live-process check go beyond the 'younger than a few hours' caution.

decisions.summary: Four variants and three idle days are new constants, labeled GUESS knobs.
decisions.why: These are parameters of the requested mechanism, declared as guesses and not claimed as measurements. They narrow nothing.

decisions.summary: 'Done, measured' is the dry run, with the mechanism pinned by fixture tests.
decisions.why: The dry run shows what the sweep removes today, not SC-008's property that the cache's size stops growing with test runs. The fixture tests cover the mechanism that gives that property. This is a plan-quality point and narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate rust test-counters runs a crate's counting build only where the crate has a `counters` feature and passes over the rest by name
decisions.why: FR-012 asks for the counters-inert phase's cost to be cut with every verdict held. The phase exists to prove the counters change no result, and a crate with no counters has nothing for it to prove. On the plan's labeled census (only rust/phases has the feature; core's testkit is already on under cfg(any(test, ...)); no other crate has features), the counting build of the other 18 crates was the default test build run a second time. That makes this removal of duplicate work, which is what was asked, not a narrowing of what is proven. The ruling rests on one premise the plan states without a method label: that make static's cover runs those same default tests in the same make done. The implementation has to keep that true.

decisions.summary: the phase's output changes: a pass-over line per skipped crate replaces its test run
decisions.why: FR-012's 'every output and verdict' clause is there so that results do not move. A pass-over line reports work not repeated and is not a changed result. Every verdict still comes out the same: from cover for the skipped crates, and from the unchanged counting run for rust/phases.

decisions.summary: rustc crate tests give a crate a `counters` feature where they run the counting build and assert the pass-over line for one without
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested change: if the gating were deleted, the test would have nothing left to check. It is not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: measurement: before from two landings' make done counters-inert phase (113 s, 59 s); after from make counters-inert FRESH=1 (4.96 s) plus T97's own landing's counters-inert phase
decisions.why: FR-012 and SC-007 require the before and after figures to come from the same command. Item 9 (Done, measured), with a one-landing budget, makes the counters-inert phase of the landing that carries T97 a done condition, and that is the same command as the before figure. SC-007 is satisfied by that landing-phase figure, which must be recorded. The FRESH=1 timing does not satisfy it, because it is a different command and is only supplementary evidence. If the landing-phase figure were deferred past T97's landing, this would become a narrowing, and an illegitimate one.

decisions.summary: the gate is keyed on a feature literally named `counters`
decisions.why: The phase is the counters-inert phase, and today's labeled census finds the counters under exactly that feature name in the one crate that has them. No case that exists today is excluded.

decisions.summary: ordered after T101-T103; one landing; red exit via make arbiter-ask; no engine code or map change
decisions.why: Sequencing and procedure inside FR-012. None of it narrows the request or the spec.

decisions.summary: T99's arbiter-crate test time is attributed to one test (7.64 s of 8-11 s) and within it one bundle call (7.62 s) that reads all 8,696 subagent transcripts (8.0 GB) whole to take each first line.
decisions.why: A measured diagnosis of the arbiter crate's slow tests, which FR-012 (T99) names as a cost to be cut against FR-008's bar; it decides where to cut, not what is asked.

decisions.summary: first_prompt in rust/gate/crates/arbiter/src/arbiter/bundle/reviews.rs reads a transcript's first line through a buffered reader instead of reading the whole file.
decisions.why: A cut of a cost FR-012 lists (T99, the arbiter crate's tests), measured before and after by the same per-test run as FR-012 and SC-007 require (7.64 s to 0.30 s). That a real spec round's bundle also gets faster is the same function, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: Output held: the parsed first line is unchanged, and an unopenable path, a directory, an empty file and a non-JSON first line each still give an empty prompt; the crate's 32 tests pass unchanged.
decisions.why: FR-012 and SC-007 require every output and verdict held; the directory case only moves where the failure arises, and its result (an empty prompt) is the same. No case is excluded or changed.

decisions.summary: Six arbiter tests still take 0.14-0.43 s against FR-008's 0.1 s, left to T99 (owed-list computation, about 25 git calls each).
decisions.why: Nothing is exempted from FR-008 or FR-012: the remaining cost stays owed by T99, which this task was found under and lands ahead of. It records a remainder, it does not narrow T99's scope.

decisions.summary: Exits: green on make static and make land; red records the failure and sets the task down, any cannot-be-done claim ruled through make arbiter-ask. Budget one landing; no constant moved, no map moved.
decisions.why: Procedure only; no part of the request is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Coverage's three instrumentation flags move out of RUSTFLAGS into a RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER so only the workspace's crates are instrumented; third-party crates (fancy-regex, serde) build plain.
decisions.why: Cuts the coverage rerun cost FR-012 names for T100 without changing what is measured: the report only ever counted workspace lines, and the plan records identical `uncovered` reports for claims and core before and after (FR-004's floor and FR-012's held outputs). The one moved hit count (121 to 110 in units.rs) is a live-tree input, hit both times, not a changed verdict.

decisions.summary: plan, cohort, tree and the gate binary crates stop declaring the whole tree '.' and declare what a full traced run of their tests opened (whole scripts/ directory where a script was read, plus the plan template); checks keeps '.'.
decisions.why: Removes reruns of checks whose inputs did not move, the 'results of tests which have already run' reuse the GM asked for (FR-011, FR-012/T100), while keeping FR-011's rule that a kept result never stands over an input that moved; the narrowed sets come from a measured trace, not assumption, and the crate whose reads are tree-wide keeps the whole tree. No case of the request is excluded.

decisions.id: T100-D3 dead check keyed on its family
decisions.summary: The dead-code check's key widens from the crate and its build inputs to every file of rust/gate/, so a dependent dropping a pub fn's last caller invalidates the kept green result; pinned by a test.
decisions.why: Enforces that the dead-code rerun T100 names gives the verdict a fresh run would give (FR-012 'held to every output and verdict', FR-011 kept results never over moved inputs). It widens rather than narrows; a check whose only effect is that the requested caching stays correct serves the request.

decisions.summary: Before and after measured by the same make static runs, back to back on a scratch clone of the unchanged tree and this clone, with core, claims, a docs edit and reverts timed.
decisions.why: Exactly SC-007's requirement: re-measured by the same command, lower (core 68.7 to 54.0 s, claims 44.5 to 25.3 s, docs 34.2 to 13.5 s, each with an observed-date and method label).

decisions.summary: A core edit still builds 17 coverage binaries one after another (14.6 s of 54.0 s); sharing that build is filed apart if taken up.
decisions.why: FR-012 asks T100's reruns be cut and SC-007 asks the cost be lower, both met; neither asks every remaining second removed, and the GM's own procedure for this work is to land, re-measure and pick the next cost. The plan states the remainder openly with its measured size rather than excluding a case the request names, so nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Each slow suite timed alone against its full-run time to separate its own cost from contention (batching and idle-tests own time; sync-with-main and entry-gate mostly contention).
decisions.why: Measurement in service of FR-012's T98 cost; decides where to cut, narrows nothing. Figures carry one-shot labels (date and method).

decisions.summary: The batching guard takes its time from a file named by BATCH_CLOCK, honored only beside a fixture's own BATCH_STATE_DIR, unit-tested for the file, its absence and a session without a state directory; the suite moves it with tick instead of sleeping.
decisions.why: The means of cutting the batching suite's sleep cost, which FR-012 asks for. It stays inside FR-012's 'held to every output and verdict the tooling gives today' only because the clock is honored solely beside a fixture's BATCH_STATE_DIR and a unit test pins that a session without one never reads it; that gate is the load-bearing condition. The block reports all 56 checks passing.

decisions.summary: One clock per case (a shared one broke parallel parts) and polling for the guard log's notice record instead of sleeping.
decisions.why: Implementation detail of the same cut; keeps the suite's verdicts (SC-007).

decisions.summary: The idle-tests suite is left as it is.
decisions.why: Not a narrowing of the named cost: its time is waiting on the real timer processes it exists to test (shown by a bash -x trace, not asserted), so it does not contend for CPU and is not on the full run's critical path (36.3 s in the full run against sync-with-main's 62.7 s); and faking its clock would put FR-012's 'every verdict held' at risk.

decisions.summary: Starting suites longest-first by last time was tried, measured slower (74.8 s and 77.0 s), and reverted.
decisions.why: An experiment toward the requested cut, measured and dropped; changes nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The rest - sync-with-main's own time and the contention around it - is measured and left; the full run measured 71.2 s before and 63.8 s after by the same command, all 54 suites green.
decisions.why: FR-012 and SC-007 require the T98 cost cut, measured before and after by the same command, lower, verdicts held; neither they nor the GM's words set a target, a floor, or name individual suites, and the GM's method in this section is explicitly incremental ('stop and measure again ... next most low-hanging fruit'). The cut is made and measured by the same command, and the obvious contention lever was tried and measured worse. Noted, not a fidelity finding: the before/after rests on one run each on a shared host (the block says so), and the critical path - sync-with-main under contention, 56.5 s of 63.8 s - is where the remaining cost sits, its 25.6 s alone not broken down as idle-tests' was.

decisions.summary: A fixed git reader rather than a shared computed fixture or a pre-built record, because the fixture repository changes between a test's computations (measured: 140 git calls for the slowest test).
decisions.why: The ruling ask:set-down-449-efficiency-round-2 names all three mechanisms as acceptable. Picking one, with a measured reason for setting another aside, stays inside it.

decisions.summary: owed_units returns a list the test supplies (GIVEN, #[cfg(test)] only), and otherwise record::owed::unanswered. The five bundle tests get an empty list. The capped-round cause test gets an empty list and, for its unreadable case, an error.
decisions.why: This is the 'fixed git reader fed to the six tests' the ruling names. It exists only in the test build, so the binary's behavior is unchanged, and the plan reports every test passing as before.

decisions.summary: asks_reversals_red_gates_and_reviews reads an empty fixture folder (TRANSCRIPTS, test build only) instead of the machine's transcripts.
decisions.why: Same kind of seam as the one the ruling authorises. The plan says the test only ever checked that the folder exists, which an empty fixture folder still shows. No output or verdict of the tool changes.

decisions.summary: The real owed-list computation is tested once, in the_capped_round_cause_reads_the_record_s_owed_list (0.143 s), and that test is named as the remainder over FR-008's bar.
decisions.why: This is the ruling's own escape: a test that cannot reach the bar without changing what the arbiter does at its git boundary is landed with its measured cut and named as the remainder. A supplied list cannot test this computation, so the escape applies. It rests on the ruling, not on FR-008's end-to-end exemption, which this test does not fit (it runs real git on a fixture, not the real command).

decisions.summary: asks_reversals_red_gates_and_reviews measures 0.123 s by the plan's own per-test method (each test alone with --exact, best of three), but it is counted as meeting FR-008's bar. The overrun is put down to process start and the first use of its regexes, which a whole-crate run would share. Checklist step 1 claims every test is under the bar except the one remainder.
decisions.why: The ruling requires each of the six arbiter tests to run under FR-008's bar, with exactly one escape: a test that cannot get there without changing what the arbiter does at its git boundary. By the plan's own account, this test's overrun is process start and regex first use, not the git boundary, so the escape does not reach it, and the plan does not name it as a remainder anyway. Its claim to meet the bar switches how time is counted. Before and after were both measured per test in its own process, and by that method the test is over 0.1 s. The figure for a whole-crate run is inferred (0.123 s minus 0.064 s of timed bundle calls), and no command measured it. FR-012 and SC-007 require the same command before and after. To clear this, do one of three things: (a) bring the test under 0.1 s by the plan's own method; (b) measure every test's in-process time with a stated command and use that method for all six, before and after; or (c) take a second remainder to the round arbiter, because the current ruling does not allow one that is not at the git boundary.

decisions.summary: Runs after T104, which carries the transcript-scan cut, and before the set-down.
decisions.why: Sequencing only. Nothing in the request or spec is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The crates a core edit owes are built first in one `cargo test --no-run --lib -p <each>` per family, in the crate run's own environment (cover_env factored out); a failed build there is left to the crate's own run to report.
decisions.why: This is the GM's first candidate as filed (request.md 2026-11-11 'the next three time savings': 'build a core edit's 17 coverage binaries together'; FR-012 T105). Leaving a failed build to the crate's own run keeps the verdicts and outputs FR-012 holds; it does not narrow anything.

decisions.summary: A crate's run now deletes only the copies of its own library the build did not just write (going by cargo's JSON artifact list), not every copy. It moves other crates' test binaries aside while its tests and report run, then puts them back (cover_built).
decisions.why: Without this the together build is wasted: the old per-crate clearing deleted the binaries it had just made, and each run rebuilt them. The reason for the old deletion (stale library copies showing as unreached lines) is kept, because only copies the build did not write are removed. FR-012 asks for the cost cut with every output held. The coverage comparison in the next decision is the check that it is held.

decisions.summary: Coverage held: claims' 7,640 and core's 3,654 lines, with hit counts and the `uncovered` report identical to T100's, compared line by line.
decisions.why: FR-012 and SC-007 require every output and verdict to be held. This is that check, not added scope.

decisions.summary: Before and after by the same command (make static after a one-line core or claims edit, back to back, a scratch clone of main against this clone): core edit 65.0 s to 57.2 s, claims edit 26.0 s to 24.8 s. The together build gets its own log line.
decisions.why: SC-007 requires the cost re-measured by the same command, and lower. Both figures went down. They come from one run each on a loaded shared host, and the plan says so itself. The new log line reports the build's timing. It does not change any check's verdict or report, so it is not a departure from 'every output the tooling gives today' in substance.

decisions.summary: The coverage test runs (17.2 s of the core edit's run) stay one crate after another, recorded as what is left.
decisions.why: The GM's candidate was to build the coverage binaries together. Running the coverage tests side by side was never part of it, so leaving them alone narrows nothing that was asked. The plan states it openly as the next cost.

decisions.summary: Tests: owed crates go to one cargo call per family, and a family of one to none. The clearing test keeps a library the build wrote, removes one it did not, and finds another crate's binary put back. The coverage-step tests move to rustc/tests/cover.rs under the 1,000-line bar.
decisions.why: These tests only enforce the requested behavior and the held outputs, so they are enforcement of the request, not scope. The file move is housekeeping under an existing bar.
