decisions.summary: One Delta per computation asks git once for revisions, one name-status diff, one untracked listing, one ls-tree a revision and one cat-file --batch, handed to the four families (record, translation, entry-drift, modal), each filtering to its own paths; each family's own base fallback kept; a family whose paths show a possible rename or unusual status falls back to its own narrow diff so its answer is exact; no cache outlives the computation.
decisions.why: This is the mechanism of the requested cut to the record's owed list's git calls (FR-012, T107; the GM 2026-11-11 'the next three time savings'). The narrow-diff fallback serves FR-012's 'held to every output' and removes no case.

decisions.summary: listing() reuses its computed units rather than computing them twice; unanswered_of, left with no caller, is removed; the old entry points stay as thin wrappers for their other callers.
decisions.why: Removing the duplicate computation is part of the requested cost cut; deleting a function with no remaining caller changes no behavior; keeping wrappers preserves every caller's output as FR-012 requires.

decisions.summary: make record-owed, record-owed (no flags, --unanswered, --slugs, --between), modal-owed and translation-owed compared byte-for-byte (stdout, stderr, exit code) before and after on the fixture and on a real record delta; delta/tests.rs holds each shared diff to the narrow one it replaces, the rename case included.
decisions.why: Verification that enforces FR-012's 'held to every output and verdict the tooling gives today' and SC-007; enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope. The byte-identical verb set names the record, modal and translation verbs; entry-drift's output is held by delta/tests.rs (each shared diff against the narrow one it replaces) and by the landing's gate run, which the plan's green exit requires - a gap in the plan's wording, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Cost measured before and after by the same wrapper: 24 git calls and 519-599 ms to 9 calls and 208-257 ms a computation on the fixture; make record-owed 44 to 14 git calls; every figure carries an observed date and method.
decisions.why: SC-007 requires the cost re-measured by the command that measured it before, and lower; it is.

decisions.summary: Two residual git costs are reported and left: every question page's base read by one cat-file (about 180 ms) even on an empty delta, and moved_only's whole-tree ls-tree kept as its own call.
decisions.why: The GM asked to proceed with the candidate 'record-owed's git calls' as a time saving, and FR-012/SC-007 require the cost cut and measured lower, not every call removed. Nothing is excluded from the outputs or from the families the change covers; the residue is disclosed, not carved out of any requirement.

decisions.summary: template_build makes the fixture topology once; topology() copies it with cp -a and points both origins at the copy's own github.git
decisions.why: Removes per-case fixture rebuilding, the suite's own time FR-012 names; every case and assertion is kept (138 checks), as FR-012/SC-007 require.

decisions.summary: the template's clone runs the id stamp once so every copy's id cache is filled; the stamps that run wrote are deleted so each case starts as before
decisions.why: Cuts stamp_hooks' repeated first-id cost while restoring each case's starting state; held to every case's outputs and verdicts per FR-012.

decisions.summary: the two fixed sleep 0.3 become a wait for the lock to be held (lock_held)
decisions.why: Replaces a fixed delay with the condition it stood in for; no case or assertion changed.

decisions.summary: before and after measured by the same command (the suite timed alone), alternated on the same clone, before 23.4/24.5 s, after 19.1/19.5 s
decisions.why: Exactly SC-007: same command before and after, lower.

decisions.summary: the goal is set as the suite's own fixtures; the script under test (about four fifths of the suite's time), including push-checks re-running its Rust self-tests on every fixture push (about 0.4 s a push), is left and reported as what remains
decisions.why: The GM's candidate was the suite's time as the full hook run's critical path, so stopping at the fixtures narrows it. The plan's stated reason (the code is the gate's push.rs, not the suite) is a where-the-code-lives argument and is NOT accepted. The ground that holds: the named remedy, a skip in push-checks, would change what the gate does on every real push, not only in fixtures - new gate behavior the request to cut the suite's time does not reach, and which FR-012's hold on every output and verdict would have to be checked as its own piece of work. The request was to cut the time (done, measured lower per SC-007), not to exhaust it, and the plan surfaces the remainder for the GM's next measure-and-choose round rather than hiding it.

decisions.summary: A passed Rust self-test is kept against the scripts/ version and the gate binary's identity, and runs again when either changes
decisions.why: The GM approved 'let push-checks skip its Rust self-tests when nothing they test changed' (2026-11-11, 'the last two time savings of the round'). The block bases the key on what the six self-tests read: the binary, whose fixtures are compiled in, and, for gate-stamp, codeid.py under scripts/. That is the condition the GM approved, with nothing added and nothing left out.

decisions.summary: The binary is identified by path, inode, size and nanosecond mtime, not by a content hash
decisions.why: A rebuild writes a new file and the wrapper touches it, so every rebuild changes the identity. Keying on metadata errs toward running again (a same-bytes rebuild reruns the self-tests). It does not skip a changed binary in any case the block describes, so 'nothing they test changed' still holds.

decisions.summary: The binary keyed is the running process's own (current_exe), the one the wrapper's $BIN runs
decisions.why: The key names the binary that actually runs the self-tests, which is the thing they test.

decisions.summary: A binary whose file cannot be read keeps nothing, and a failed self-test is never kept
decisions.why: Both run the self-tests in every case where the keep condition cannot be shown to hold, so the gate loosens only as far as approved.

decisions.summary: The sync-with-main suite's template clone runs push-checks once, so each copied case starts with the self-tests kept
decisions.why: The GM's request names 'roughly 14 s of the sync-with-main suite's serial run' as part of the saving he approved. The fixture now matches a real clone after its first push. The suite's cases test sync-with-main, not the self-tests, and the block narrows none of its cases.

decisions.summary: Before and after measured by alternated push-checks runs and suite runs, all 138 checks passing
decisions.why: SC-007 requires the same command before and after, lower, with verdicts held. The block's figures each carry a date and method label. The saving is smaller than the 0.4 s estimate, which is a fact about the measurement and not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: A test pins that the self-tests are kept on a second push and rerun on a rewritten binary, a moved scripts/, the cache off, and an unreadable binary
decisions.why: It enforces the requested behavior and its limits. With that behavior deleted, nothing is left for it to check.

decisions.summary: money-candidates (2.2 s of a 3.7 s push) is reported to the GM as a candidate and not acted on
decisions.why: It reports the next candidate rather than widening this task's scope, which follows the GM's 'then we will stop and measure again' pattern.

decisions.summary: Before T108; exits green on make static, rust-test, hooks-test and land, red recorded and ruled through make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: Ordering and exits within the two tasks the GM approved together.

decisions.summary: Each crate's coverage run gets a report directory of its own (a hard link to its test binary, its own profiles), and its tests run straight from the binary from the crate's directory with CARGO, CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR and CARGO_PKG_NAME set, instead of through cargo test holding the build directory's lock.
decisions.why: This is the mechanism of the GM's 2026-11-11 'run a core edit's coverage tests side by side' (FR-012 T108); the runs could not overlap while llvm-cov report read the whole shared build directory. Coverage equivalence is checked under D5.

decisions.summary: The family's one together build names each test binary in its JSON, so the per-crate builds, the deletion of stale libraries and the moves aside go; a failed multi-crate build is asked again a crate at a time so the failure names the crate; show-env once a family.
decisions.why: Removes work the side-by-side runs no longer need, and the crate-by-crate retry keeps the failure output attributable as before (FR-012 'held to every output and verdict'). Nothing the GM asked for is cut.

decisions.summary: Runs go a quarter of the cores at once (side_by_side, 5 on this 22-core machine), because all at once drove the load to 31 and failed two timing tests.
decisions.why: A concurrency level is how 'side by side' is done; it does not narrow the request, and the bound exists to keep every verdict held (SC-007).

decisions.summary: The depiction bundle test's own crop timeout raised from 300 ms to 1 s (still under its slow page's 5 s sleep), because at five at a time it failed one of two core-edit passes under load.
decisions.why: Adjudicated as a relaxation of a check, since SC-007 holds every check it touches to its earlier verdicts. It is a test's own constant, not product behavior, and the property the test discriminates - a crop on a page that sleeps 5 s is cut off by the timeout - is unchanged: 1 s < 5 s, so the test still fails if the timeout mechanism is absent. Holding 300 ms literally would make the test flake under the load the requested change brings, which defeats SC-007's own purpose (verdicts held) rather than serving it. Cost about 0.7 s in a crate not on the critical path.

decisions.summary: Coverage equivalence is judged on the set of unreached lines and never-called functions, not identical bytes; core's only difference is four closures of the guard's sweep_dead outside core's own files, reached or not depending on the temp directory's contents.
decisions.why: Byte identity is physically unobtainable: two runs of the old path already differ in hit counts (cmp, observed 2026-11-11). The floor (FR-004) and the verdict read each crate's own files, which are 100% covered both ways with identical zero sets for claims and checks; the sweep_dead closures lie outside core's files and their reach is state-dependent in either path. The verdict and the floor's output are held, which is what FR-012/SC-007 ask.

decisions.summary: Starting the slowest crate first was tried and taken out, the checks crate already starting in the first five.
decisions.why: A design choice not shipped; no scope effect.

decisions.summary: SC-007 before/after by make static on a scratch clone of main and this clone, back to back, one-line edits: core 49.7-52.0 s before vs 40.2 s after; claims 26.7-34.7 s before vs 23.4/25.0 s after.
decisions.why: Same command as the T105-T107 report's make static figure; the cost is lower, as SC-007 requires. Figures carry one-shot labels with date and method.

decisions.summary: Tests pin the floor reading a report directory holding the crate's binary alone, removed after the run, tests run from the crate's directory with cargo's variables, and the together build with crate-by-crate retry (tests/cover.rs); every cargo call still runs from the tree root.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested behavior and of its held verdicts; serves the request.

decisions.summary: The checks crate's tests remain the step's floor; two coverage runs on one clone at once still share its report directories, as they shared its build directory before.
decisions.why: States the residue, not a carve-out: concurrent runs on one clone collided before (the moves aside of T92/T105), so this preserves rather than narrows prior behavior, and the GM did not ask for same-clone concurrent runs.

decisions.summary: States the measured cost being cut: rustfmt kept nothing, so every make static formatted all 19 crates (2.1 s of 29.1 s).
decisions.why: Descriptive grounding for the GM's 'rustfmt keeping its result per crate' (request.md, make static's own caching); decides no scope.

decisions.summary: The kept key is the crate's own files, the workspace manifests and toolchain files, rustfmt configuration and compiler version, not dependency crates; a nested crate's files belong to the nested crate, so the enclosing binary's key does not move on them.
decisions.why: This is what 'kept per crate' means: rustfmt reads only a crate's own sources and its configuration, so excluding dependencies loses no verdict, and the nested crate's own key moves on its edit, so that edit is still checked. FR-012/SC-007's 'every verdict held' is kept, and the tests named pin the key's movement.

decisions.summary: Only a green format check is kept; make format (the rewrite) records nothing, but still skips a crate whose check key stands.
decisions.why: Recording a rewrite's pre-rewrite key would mark unformatted text green, which would break FR-012's held verdicts; refusing it serves the request. Skipping a clean crate in a rewrite changes no output (rustfmt on already-clean text is a no-op), so the tooling's outputs are held.

decisions.summary: Before/after measured by the same command (rust format --check 2.32 s to 0.16-0.17 s unchanged, 0.78 s after a core edit; make static unchanged 1.36-1.39 s).
decisions.why: SC-007 requires each task re-measured by the same command and lower; figures carry observed-date and method labels.

decisions.summary: Two tests pin the key and the check-versus-rewrite rule; kept-result tests move to rustc/tests/kept.rs under the 1,000-line bar.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the requested caching and its held verdicts (FR-012, SC-007); a file move for the project's line bar adds no behavior.

decisions.summary: When l7r-gate rust cover passes a crate whose cargo test is its unit tests alone, the crate's test key is kept green, so make rust-test does not rerun what the coverage run ran.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 'a passing coverage run recording the test result' (2026-11-11, 'Yes to all 4 of those') and his 2026-11-11 'the results of tests which have already run so that we don't have to run them again'. The equivalence premise (no code reads cfg(coverage)) is measured, with a one-shot label, not assumed.

decisions.summary: A crate whose cargo test also runs binaries, integration tests, examples, benches or doctests (today rust/guard, rust/gate, rust/phases, rust/gate/crates/rustc) keeps no test result from a coverage pass.
decisions.why: In those crates the coverage run does not run all the tests cargo test runs, so keeping the crate's whole test key green would record a result for tests that never ran. That breaks FR-012/SC-007's 'held to every output and verdict', and it is outside the GM's own purpose: reuse the results of tests 'which have already run'. On a crate-level key, the literal rule cannot be honored without a false verdict. Each class was checked separately: binaries, integration tests, examples, benches and doctests are all cases the coverage run does not execute, so one argument covers all of them. Which crates fall out is decided by inspecting each crate (unit_tests_only), not by a fixed list. The measured result (18 of 19 crates standing after a core edit, against 11 before) shows the purpose is served, not gutted. The lib tests of the excluded crates still run twice. Recording them separately would be a further saving, not something the request requires.

decisions.summary: Only the test key make rust-test asks first is kept. The second key, over the plain test binaries, is not, because asking it would build them.
decisions.why: This is a mechanism choice inside the requested saving. It narrows nothing the GM asked for. The key is computed from the same inputs, so a later change still moves it.

decisions.summary: SC-007 is measured by the same command before and after (make rust-test after a one-line core edit and a green make static), with all 19 results standing after the revert.
decisions.why: SC-007 requires the cost re-measured by the same command and the verdicts held. Both are met. The figures carry a one-shot label.

decisions.summary: Tests: which crates count as unit-tests-only, and that a coverage pass keeps the tests of such a crate but not of a crate with a binary.
decisions.why: These tests enforce the requested behavior and its verdict-holding bound. They serve the request and are not added scope.

decisions.summary: Order after T110, exits, one-landing budget, no engine code or maps moved.
decisions.why: These are procedural decisions. None changes what was asked.

decisions.summary: Only the lint, test and coverage keys read a file's code without plain comments; rustfmt's (format) and the dead check's keys keep the whole text.
decisions.why: The GM's 'comment-insensitive keys' is unqualified, so carving out two keys narrows it. It is legitimate because applying it literally would defeat the request's own stated constraint (FR-012/SC-007: every output and verdict held): rustfmt formats comments and the dead check counts a word in a comment as a use, so a key blind to comments would reuse a verdict a comment can change. The literal rule is impossible to apply to those two without breaking verdicts, not merely awkward.

decisions.summary: Doc comments (///, //!, /** */, /*! */) stay in the code text the keys read.
decisions.why: Clippy lints doc comments and rustdoc runs doctests, so stripping them would break the verdict-hold FR-012 requires; keeping them is the request applied correctly.

decisions.summary: Line structure: blank lines still move a key; the claim that plain comments cannot change clippy's, the tests' or the coverage floor's verdict rests on a too_many_lines experiment and a search for line!(), include_str! of a .rs and include!.
decisions.why: Conservative choices that keep FR-012's verdict hold; the measured 18-of-19 crates kept after a one-line comment edit shows the purpose is reached. Unverified premise (repository not read, per the bundle): the stated search space does not name column!(), #[track_caller]/Location::caller(), or clippy's undocumented_unsafe_blocks / unnecessary_safety_comment, which read plain // SAFETY: comments. If any is in use or enabled, the lint or test key must keep those comments; the landing's verdict-hold test and SC-007's re-measure are what must cover it. Not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: A file a crate's tests declare they read keeps its whole text; the checks crate (reads = ['.']) still reruns its tests and coverage on any comment edit, that cost left to T116.
decisions.why: A declared read may be read for its comments, so keying it on code alone would risk a verdict (FR-012). Deferring the checks crate's coverage cost to T116 is not dropping it: T116 is the GM's own filed task for that crate's coverage tests (request.md, 'make static's own caching').

decisions.summary: A small lexer that honors string/raw/byte/char literals and lifetimes and nests block comments; code ids 'code:' + sha read once a run from the work tree; every crate's keys move once at the first run after landing.
decisions.why: Implementation of the requested keys; a one-time key move is the unavoidable cost of changing a key's definition and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Before/after measured by one back-to-back run of the same script on a scratch clone of main and this clone, on a loaded host with load recorded (37.5 s -> 17.5 s after a one-line comment edit).
decisions.why: SC-007 asks for the cost re-measured by the same command before and after, lower, verdicts held; the A/B uses one command on both trees and is labeled with date and method. The 29.1 s quiet-machine figure is a separately labeled observation, not the SC-007 pair.

decisions.summary: A dependency's interface is its T112 code with the bodies of non-const, non-async fns whose signature holds no impl and whose body holds no impl block or macro_rules! replaced by {}; docs, attributes, items outside bodies, macro_rules! whole kept.
decisions.why: This is the design of the interface key the GM approved ('the dependents' lint keyed on a crate's public interface', 'Yes to all 4 of those') and asked to have reviewed first. The kept cases (const fn, async fn, returned impl Trait, impl/macro_rules! inside a body) are the ones a dependent's check build can see through.

decisions.summary: Applies to the lint key alone, and only to the files of crates a crate builds from; the crate's own files stay on T112 code ids; test, coverage, format and dead keys unchanged.
decisions.why: Matches the request's item exactly: 'the dependents' lint'. Nothing beyond the lint of dependents is loosened.

decisions.summary: Not exact: (a) a dependent lint that reads a dependency's body through the compiler (nursery/restriction, none enabled) and (b) a body the rules misread as private would go unrun after a body-only edit, failing open until the dependent's files or the dependency's interface move.
decisions.why: Narrows FR-012/SC-007 as written ('held to every output and verdict the tooling gives today', with no exemption for T113). Ruled against request.md: the GM said 'Yes to all 4 of those' to an item described as 'the dependents' lint keyed on a crate's public interface - not exact, a design reviewed first', so the exception is in the GM's own words. Case (a) is inherent to any interface keying and is squarely the approved inexactness. Case (b) is this design's approximation error; it is the same class of inexactness the GM accepted and is bounded by the rules reviewed here, so it is also LEGITIMATE. Note for the caller: the accepted spec text (FR-012, SC-007) does not carry this exception; recording it there is a spec-amendment matter, not a plan ruling.

decisions.summary: A file the lexer cannot read to its end keeps its whole code.
decisions.why: Fails closed: such a file's lint key behaves as before.

decisions.summary: syn full-parser interface and rustc .rmeta rejected.
decisions.why: Design choice between ways of doing the requested thing; narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A lint key stops reading a crate's declared test reads ([package.metadata.l7r] reads); test and coverage keys keep them.
decisions.why: Not one of the four named items, so checked for exactness: per the block a declared read only ever chose a .rs file's full id over its code id in a lint key and never added an input, and a lint runs no test, so the only effect is that comment-only edits stop re-linting the checks crate, which is T112's already-approved behavior. The block's own after-run shows the declared read defeating T113 for the checks crate, so this makes the approved item take effect: enforcement, not new scope.

decisions.summary: Test and coverage keys now read every file their Rust sources include (include_str!/include_bytes!); lint, format and dead keys do not.
decisions.why: Adds inputs, so caching moves toward SC-007's 'giving the verdicts and outputs it gave before' (a kept test result had stood over a changed table). Lint, format and dead keys are left as they were. Narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: SC-007 measured by make static after a body-only core edit, before and after; plus l7r-gate.sh rust lint after the declared-read fix.
decisions.why: The same command before and after is what SC-007 asks. Not adjudicated by re-running (bundle-only review). Two notes for the landing: (1) the 10.6 s 'before' lint figure is given two different methods (l7r-gate.sh rust lint per crate in the first decision, 'the timestamped make static' in the measurement decision): it was measured one way and stated another; (2) the 30.1 s 'after' make static was taken before the declared-read and include fixes, and the only post-fix figure (1.95 s, l7r-gate.sh rust lint) is compared against a make static lint step, a different command. SC-007 is a landing condition: make static must be re-run on the landed tree, the same way as the 37.5 s before.

decisions.id: T114-D1 side by side rather than skipped
decisions.summary: Cut the push's money-candidates check by scanning the record's question pages in parallel across cores instead of adding a cache/skip keyed on its inputs.
decisions.why: FR-012 names 'the push's money-candidates check (T114)' as a cost to cut, by the GM's 2026-11-11 'The three things you suggested also seem good to work on too'; the choice of mechanism is open, and parallelism performs the same scans on every push, so no case is skipped and no verdict loosened.

decisions.id: T114-D2 same output by restoring page order
decisions.summary: Pages dealt round-robin to cores (page i to core i mod n) and their amounts restored to page order before the existing stable sort, so the listing sees the same sequence.
decisions.why: Serves FR-012's 'held to every output and verdict the tooling gives today' and SC-007's identical outputs; it preserves behavior, it carves nothing out.

decisions.summary: money-candidates with --all --context, with --check and with no flags compared byte for byte (stdout, stderr, exit) before and after; existing money tests kept unchanged and green, every changed line covered.
decisions.why: Enforces the output-identity half of FR-012/SC-007; it is verification of what was asked, not new scope.

decisions.id: T114-D4 timing measured before and after by the same commands
decisions.summary: The check alone timed with date around it, and the push's row via l7r-gate measure push-check-times, before and after, with load recorded.
decisions.why: SC-007 requires the cost re-measured by the command that measured it before, and lower; the same two commands are used on both sides and the figures carry one-shot labels (date and method).

decisions.summary: The record's pages are parsed across the cores before Record::of reads them (warm in record/units.rs); the parse table's lock is taken only to look up and to keep; the record is then read in the same order from the same parses.
decisions.why: A means to the GM's 'the full hook run's two longest suites' (FR-012, T115). FR-012's 'held to every output and verdict' is carried by the block's own evidence: record-owed with no flags, --unanswered and --slugs, on an empty delta and with a page edited, byte-identical between the old and new binaries (cmp). Nothing narrowed.

decisions.summary: push-checks' rows start at once; each row's output is shown in the table's order; the first refusal ends the run with the shell's line as before.
decisions.why: Table order, verdict and the refusal's shell line are held as FR-012 requires, and the test the_runner_stops_at_the_first_refusal_with_the_shell_s_line pins the verdict. The one output that moves is split out as T115-D3 and ruled there.

decisions.summary: Within one row, the row's stdout is shown before its stderr, so where a row wrote to both the cross-stream interleave can differ from today's.
decisions.why: Narrows FR-012's 'held to every output'. Legitimate on the impossibility bar, scoped tightly: when rows run at once their output has to be captured, and two captured pipes carry no shared order; a single merged capture (pipe or pty) keeps the order but moves stderr bytes onto stdout, which is itself an output change. So every concurrent design changes one of the two, and only a serial run changes neither. A serial run would give sync-with-main, one of the two suites the GM named for T115, nothing from this task, since push-checks is the block's only lever on that suite; so the literal rule would defeat half the request. The ruling covers ONLY the stdout/stderr interleave within a single row, replayed after that row ends. Each stream's bytes and their order within the stream, the table order, the refusal line and the verdict are not excepted and must stay as they are today. Any wider output difference is not approved here.

decisions.summary: Rows after a refusal now run (today they do not), but show nothing and keep nothing; a self-test after a refusal is not kept.
decisions.why: If 'keeps nothing' holds, no output or verdict moves; running wasted work is cost, not fidelity. A seam the block should close in its text: it says the two memo presets and the ledger check each keep a file of their own by atomic rename, and its parenthetical says only how a self-test after a refusal is withheld. Nothing says how a memo or ledger row that has already run is stopped from renaming its file into place. The block should name that mechanism, or say that such a file is kept. Not blocking: a kept memo records a true pass for that tree state, so a later verdict is unchanged.

decisions.summary: The full hook run's wall time is left as it is (measured unchanged, 64.8/64.4 s before vs 64.6/64.2 s after, bound by contention the suites share in the kernel); it is offered to the GM as a candidate, not changed here.
decisions.why: The GM's words for T115 name 'the full hook run's two longest suites', not the full run's wall time. The block measures the suites lower inside the full run (sync-with-main 51.9/52.9 to 49.1/48.5 s, entry-gate 47.8/47.0 to 43.0/44.3 s), reports openly that the full run did not move, and leaves the kernel-bound cause to the GM instead of quietly widening scope. That is the right way to handle it.

decisions.summary: The hook run stays at eight suites at a time (HOOKS_JOBS 8).
decisions.why: No constant moved; 12 and 16 were measured slower (72.8 s, 76.3 s vs 64.1 s), so the existing value is kept. Nothing narrowed.

decisions.summary: The whole-tree test every_pointer_in_the_repository_resolves_to_a_fragment is left out of the coverage build (#[cfg(not(coverage))]) and runs only in the plain make rust-test run.
decisions.why: The GM asked for the checks crate's coverage tests to cost less (request.md 2026-11-11 'make static's own caching', T116; FR-012). FR-012/SC-007 require the cost lower and every verdict held, not that every test run under instrumentation: the test still runs and gives its verdict in the plain run, and the crate's coverage stays 100% (FR-004's floor), so no verdict or floor is given up.

decisions.summary: alternation takes a Vec (one instantiation) and the fixture test the_alternation_puts_a_longer_name_first reaches the sort line only the whole-tree test reached.
decisions.why: A code change whose only purpose is to keep FR-004's 100% line coverage once the whole-tree test leaves the coverage build; enforcement of the existing floor, not new behavior, and the function's output is unchanged.

decisions.summary: The plain run stays owed after every coverage pass because T111 records no test result from a coverage pass for a crate that reads cfg(coverage); the workspace declares cfg(coverage) in check-cfg so the unexpected_cfgs lint accepts it.
decisions.why: Read as invoking T111's existing rule, not carving the checks crate out of it. The CLEAR depends on that premise: if a coverage pass recorded the crate green, the plain run would be skipped and the whole-tree test would never run, a verdict lost under SC-007. The premise is stated in the plan, not pinned by anything in the bundle; the exits (make rust-test, make land green) must show it holds.

decisions.summary: The checks crate's declared reads stay the whole tree (reads = ["."]).
decisions.why: Status quo kept; it keeps any edit re-running the crate's tree-reading tests, so no verdict is skipped under FR-011's reuse.

decisions.summary: Before/after measured back to back on a scratch clone of main and this clone with the T108/T113 scratch scripts around make static, after comment and body edits of core and claims.
decisions.why: SC-007 asks for the cost re-measured by the same command before and after and lower; every figure carries a one-shot label (date and method). Measurement of what was asked, not added scope.

decisions.summary: The lint and the cost live in the guard crate (shared/ledger.rs, ledger/cost.rs), the commands and owed rows in the gate's reviews crate; passes.rs reads the shared code.
decisions.why: FR-003 one implementation: the guard already held a copy of review_cost's arithmetic and ledger_lint.CHECKS, and the guard cannot depend on the gate. Placement of a port, not a narrowing of FR-001/FR-002 or ask:449-T83-scope.

decisions.summary: iso.rs and py_text::repr move into the guard, core re-exporting both.
decisions.why: Forced by the same build direction; callers unchanged. Internal structure only.

decisions.summary: ledger_hooks and escalation_hooks call the lint and cost in-process; ledger_hooks runs `reviews ledger-owed` by command through the gate wrapper.
decisions.why: Replaces a by-path Python run with Rust (FR-001). FR-007's one process per tool call for guard dispatch is kept; a child on one branch is what the guard already did with Python. The hook-time build is a cost the plan discloses, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: Unported Python importers (coord.py, review_census.py, feature_report.py until T119, land.py until T121, page_session_runner.py) run the Rust commands (ledger-lint, review-cost --last, ledger-rows, ledger-passes) instead of importing.
decisions.why: ask:449-T83-scope itself orders the ledger at T117 and land.py at T121 'calling the ledger ... in-process', so the ruling requires Python callers to reach the Rust ledger by command in between; 'no door' refers to a Python bridge module, and none is added. FR-003 one implementation holds (the three .py are deleted), and the 21-case before/after differential of the importers shows no difference.

decisions.summary: Two corrections toward the Python inside the guard: a pass's cost computed as review_cost.py did (integer microseconds, int()), and verdict_of reading the first line with Python's strip()/splitlines().
decisions.why: FR-002 same outputs as the Python and FR-003 one implementation; moves the Rust toward the reference, all 54 hook suites green.

decisions.summary: Differential normalizations N1 traceback stderr, N2 argparse usage text, N3 the usage line's utc, N4 no bytecode.
decisions.why: N1 and N2 are exactly what ask:449-usage-text rules unbound (exit status and stdout still held); N3 is a timestamp and N4 a Python run artifact, neither an output of the tool.

decisions.summary: Known divergences no case reaches: --help exits 2, Unicode \w/\b and non-ASCII digits, NaN or lone-surrogate log lines skipped, glob characters in an agent id, which undecodable page raises first.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds every case the tests and suites hold, and --help is bound only where a kept test holds it (ask:449-usage-text); no case is excluded or changed, the differential ran over the real ledger, pass log and transcripts, and the divergences are disclosed rather than hidden.

decisions.summary: The three .py are deleted in the same cut, every caller repointed (Makefile recipes, sync-with-main.sh, land-tooling.sh defaults with the suite contract kept, push.rs's row now a gate row).
decisions.why: FR-001 and FR-003; the GM's standing approval of 2026-11-10 to delete Python once its port lands; one error text kept byte for byte for FR-002.

decisions.summary: turn_time.py left to T120 (its one importer is stepback_bundle.py), land.py to T121, feature_report.py to T119.
decisions.why: Exactly ask:449-T83-scope's slice order; ledger_owed does not import turn_time per the plan's census, so nothing it reads is left behind a door.

decisions.summary: speckit-todo's rules in the guard crate (shared/speckit.rs), its command line and report in cohort as l7r-gate speckit-todo
decisions.why: Crate placement is design the spec leaves open; two guards read the rules and the guard cannot build on the gate. Nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: ci/features.rs, reviews/glyph.rs, set_down_hooks and feature_approval_hooks call the rules in-process; glyph's run-by-command cache and features' unused python parameter go; feature_approval_hooks keeps its own at_rev
decisions.why: This is ask:449-T83-scope's 'its Rust callers calling it in-process' carried out. at_rev is the revision reader reused under ask:449-T89-reviews, not speckit-todo's state, so keeping it changes nothing. The dropped cache only held the results of a process that no longer runs.

decisions.summary: The push's speckit-todo check stays a gate row run by command (l7r-gate speckit-todo --root --check), keeping the row runner, refusal text, kept key and usage line, as T117's ledger-owed row did
decisions.why: The push is a Rust caller and the ruling says Rust callers go in-process, so this departs from the ruling's words. It is legitimate because FR-002 binds the push's own outputs: its row, refusal text, kept key and usage line, and the push table that m:push-checks-rust re-measures. Moving the push in-process would change those outputs. Keeping the row by command changes none of them. The ruling exists so that no Python and no door is left, and that purpose is met: the row starts the Rust binary the push already is, with no Python and no door.

decisions.summary: The Python importers close_check.py, plan_hold.py, research_claims.py and tick-task.py, plus the Makefile, sync-with-main.sh and land.py, reach the port by command, the importers through one new flag --each-state DIR... (one process for all their directories, no usage line)
decisions.why: The ruling requires by-command callers to switch in the same cut and forbids a door. A flag on the Rust binary is not a door. One process a caller serves FR-006. The flag is new surface with no Python counterpart, so FR-002 does not bind it. The callers it serves were compared before and after (855 cases, 0 differing).

decisions.summary: The command records its usage line as usage_log.exited did; the in-process calls record none, where features.rs and set_down_hooks used to leave a speckit-todo line through their runs by command
decisions.why: This changes a file the differential compares, so it narrows FR-002's 'same outputs' for two callers. It is implied by the accepted ruling ask:449-T83-scope, which makes these calls in-process. With no process there is no exit to record, and a line written anyway would record a command run that never happened. The ruling's words carry the decision; the block's 'by-product of the process' description does not. The Python importers' imports also recorded no line, so the Rust follows the same rule the Python already did.

decisions.summary: work_budget_view.py's lines() and moved() are ported for the report in T118 while the .py stays for land.py until T121: two copies for one slice, each naming the other, the .py deleted with land.py in T121
decisions.why: This bears on FR-003 ('no piece runs both') and on the ruling placing work_budget_view at T121. It is legitimate because the ruling's own words require it. 'The modules each importer reads port with it, no door' covers both importers: speckit-todo lands in T118 and land.py in T121. The speckit-todo port therefore has to carry what it reads now and cannot reach the .py through a door, while land.py needs the .py until its own port. No piece runs both: the report runs only the Rust functions and land.py only the Python. The overlap is limited to two named functions, cross-referenced, deleted in T121 as the ruling places it, with the Rust side covered by the differential.

decisions.summary: -h exits 2 against the Python's 0, the one difference in 1,317 command cases, accepted as in T82 (N7) and T117
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text: --help is bound only where a kept test or suite case holds it. The block says no kept case holds it but does not show this; FR-001b deleted the Python tests, so a hook suite is the only place one could be.

decisions.summary: N1 traceback text, N2 argparse usage text, N3 the usage line's utc, N4 a raise compared as a raise and not by its type; four named divergences no case reaches (non-ASCII isdigit in F=, NaN in JSON, an alias given as a number or tags not an object, a lone --)
decisions.why: Traceback and argparse text are unbound under ask:449-usage-text, while the exit status and stdout are still held. A timestamp is not a verdict. FR-002 binds 'every case its tests and its suites hold', and these four inputs are held by no case. They are listed here so the record shows they were seen.

decisions.summary: A broken .specify/affects.json fails where the Python raised: --state exits 1, --each-state prints error: lines and exits 1, the importers that let the import raise now raise on the nonzero exit, research_claims keeps its old handling, glyph reads the error as not closed, an absent file still reads as none
decisions.why: Each case keeps the Python's verdict and exit (FR-002), and the differential compares both sides failing. The --each-state error form has no Python side. Nothing changes what was asked.

decisions.summary: The command of 375-a1-speckit-todo-clones is retired to <retired: ...> with its values kept as history, so make figures does not run it
decisions.why: The accepted spec carries this exact ruling (ask:449-T118-retire-375-a1). It rests on the GM's 2026-11-09 rule on unused past harnesses: the comparison measured a mode the port does not keep, so nothing could re-run it.

decisions.summary: speckit-todo.py deleted in the same cut after a census of callers; test stubs replaced by real .git/active-task files and status lines
decisions.why: FR-001, FR-003 and the GM's standing approval to delete ported Python. Note: the census names the kinds of files it searched but not the pattern it grepped, and file kinds outside the listed ones and directories (*.toml, *.yml, .specify/ non-shell non-md files) are not searched. This is not a narrowing, but the search space is not fully stated.

decisions.summary: The event-log reader lives in the guard beside its writer (read_jsonl, from_transcript, reversals), reusing its helpers; the arbiter bundle's own read_jsonl/reversals now call these; py_str and value_repr move into the guard's pyjson with core re-exporting them.
decisions.why: ask:449-T83-scope places event_log.py in T119 'reusing the event-log reader the Rust already has'; one reader is what the ruling asks, and consolidating the arbiter's duplicate serves it. No output changes.

decisions.summary: feature_report reads the review passes in-process (ledger_passes::passes) instead of running `reviews ledger-passes` by command; the command stays for its other readers.
decisions.why: Both sides are Rust after T117; ask:449-T83-scope and FR-003 prefer no door between ported modules, and no piece runs both implementations. Keeping the command for its other callers removes nothing.

decisions.summary: Both event_log.py verbs (hook, from-transcript) are ported though nothing runs them; hook writes through a new guard function `record`, so a hook payload that is no JSON object writes no line, as the Python wrote none, where the guard's writer had written one.
decisions.why: FR-001 replaces every Python file, so porting both verbs rather than dropping one is the literal reading. The no-line behavior on a non-object payload moves the Rust TO the Python's behavior, which is what FR-002 requires; it carries no exception. Read either way the block's 'the hook's own path' may mean (a new function for the ported verb, or the live hook's path), the change is parity with the Python, and the block reports make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 green on 54 suites, so no held guard-suite case was changed.

decisions.summary: The callers repointed are the Makefile's feature-report and where-time recipes ('##' text and F= checks unchanged); no inline python3 -c recipe calls these modules, so none of T83's make-audit recipes goes with this slice.
decisions.why: ask:449-T83-scope: every by-command caller switches in the same cut, and each make-audit recipe goes with the slice whose module it calls or with T121. The census at the cut (git grep of the four names, observed 2026-11-12) finds only comments, docs and measurement prose, so no caller is left on the Python.

decisions.summary: specs/385-approach-checklist/where_time.py, which imported feature_report, is deleted unported as a past harness.
decisions.why: FR-001 already settles it: a file under specs/ 'that nothing runs is deleted and not ported, the GM 2026-11-09: "I don't think we need to port the past feature harnesses if those are not still used."' The 'nothing runs it' premise is measured (git grep over Makefile, scripts/, rust/, .claude/ and every specs/*/measurements*.json command, observed 2026-11-12) and corroborated by the repo-wide census of the name at the cut. Were it classed narrowing it would be LEGITIMATE on the GM's own words.

decisions.summary: Wherever the Python raised, the Rust fails too, pinned by 40 differential cases with both sides failing.
decisions.why: FR-002 parity of verdict and exit; ask:449-usage-text leaves an uncaught traceback's text unbound while holding exit status and stdout, which is what these cases compare.

decisions.summary: Differential normalizations N1 (stderr from 'Traceback' on) and N2 (argparse usage text).
decisions.why: Both are exactly what ask:449-usage-text unbinds: an uncaught traceback's text, and the stderr argparse itself generates on a malformed invocation (exit 2 and empty stdout still held). Premise recorded: the 8 usage-error cases are taken to be argparse-generated, not a hand-written parser.error message or a usage line a caller reads, which the ruling keeps bound; the block does not say so explicitly.

decisions.summary: Normalizations N3 (the line 'This report took X s') and N5 (the hook's own time in a written line).
decisions.why: Byte equality on a wall-clock time is physically impossible: two runs of the Python itself do not match there. Only the time value is normalized; the line's presence and every other byte stay compared, so FR-002's purpose (the port gives the same answers) is intact.

decisions.summary: Normalization N4: the order of where-time rows that tie on their sort key; the Python left it to its string hash (two PYTHONHASHSEED values gave two orders), the Rust keeps the order first booked.
decisions.why: There is no single Python output to hold the Rust to: the Python's order was observed to move with the hash seed, so matching it byte for byte is physically impossible. The rows themselves stay compared; only the order among rows equal on the sort key is normalized, which carries no information the report's reader relies on. A deterministic order is the only way to have one output at all.

decisions.summary: Normalization N6: the Makefile's path in make's own error line.
decisions.why: An artifact of the harness comparing HEAD's Makefile at one path with this clone's at another; it is make's text, not an output of the ported tool.

decisions.summary: Disclosed divergences no case reaches: non-ASCII digits in an int or float, NaN in JSON, unhashable or mixed-type event fields, a list-valued t on a lone event, which agent wins when one tool id is in two subagents' transcripts, non-UTF-8 git output (both fail, at different points), and -h exiting 2.
decisions.why: Adjudicated by item. (a) -h exiting 2: ask:449-usage-text binds --help only where a kept test or suite case holds it, and none is reported to. (b) Which agent wins on a duplicated tool id: the Python's answer is its set order, nondeterministic, so no single Python output exists to match. (c) Non-UTF-8 git output: both fail, so the verdict is held. (d) Non-ASCII digits, NaN, unhashable or mixed-type fields, a list-valued t: inputs no held case and none of the real features, logs and transcripts in the 182-case differential produced; FR-002 binds 'every case its tests and its suites hold', and the list is disclosed rather than excluded from a held case. None of the four guts FR-002's purpose on the logs this tooling actually reads.

decisions.summary: No recorded measurement is rewritten: the feature-report entries of specs/374 and specs/375 run make feature-report and match the differential; sc005-372, cascade-threshold and sc006-replay fail alike before and after on a transcript no longer on disk; event-hook-cost's command runs nothing since T012, only its method naming event_log.py.
decisions.why: FR-001's rewrite clause binds a measurement's command that runs a .py, python3 -c/-m, or describes a python3 run in prose; these commands go through make and name no deleted file, and event-hook-cost's mention is in its method, history. The three entries that fail on a missing transcript fail identically before and after, so this cut changes nothing about them (measured: git grep of the four names over every specs/*/measurements*.json, observed 2026-11-12).

decisions.summary: event_log.py, task_phases.py, feature_report.py and where_time.py are ported and deleted in one cut, after the differential, with the callers repointed.
decisions.why: ask:449-T83-scope names T119 as one slice holding the measure chain; its 'then ... then' orders the work inside that slice, the five slices being the separate tasks. Deletion after the port passes is FR-003 and the GM's standing approval to delete ported Python; the differential was re-run after the deletion, 0 differing.

decisions.summary: The step-back is ported into the measure crate beside fix_yield and calls reviews' git, gitdir and checkpoint::state in-process. reviews_door.py, reviews/door.rs and the reviews-door dispatch are removed. Bundle files are written in the Python's order.
decisions.why: ask:449-T83-scope assigns stepback_bundle.py to T120 with no door and says T120 removes reviews_door.py's three verbs. ask:449-T89-reviews says the door leaves when T83 lands. FR-002 requires the same written files, which is why the write order is kept.

decisions.summary: The ruling assumed checks/tool_signals.rs ran tool_yield.py by command. It actually held its own copy of the inventory. That copy is replaced by one implementation in core, read in-process by checks and measure. check tool-signals now fails on a broken settings file, Makefile or registry, or a non-UTF-8 gate script, where T068's copy read them leniently.
decisions.why: The plan names the ruling's wrong premise openly. What it does instead serves the ruling's purpose: one implementation and no piece running both (FR-003; FR-001c's one-implementation condition). Making the check stricter on broken inputs does not refuse correct work (constitution XIV runs the other way). The plan pins it with a test and the check passes on the real tree. The plan says this restores check-tool-signals.py's behavior through its import of tool_yield. No differential reaches that deleted check directly. The support in the bundle is the tool-yield differential's 31 broken scratch trees, which both the Python and the Rust fail on.

decisions.summary: turn_time stays a command with no make recipe.
decisions.why: The Python had no recipe, so nothing changes. T119's rule that no command vanishes unannounced applies.

decisions.summary: tool-yield's default --root is the working tree the command runs in. The Python defaulted to the tree its own script sat in.
decisions.why: This is a real behavior difference, recorded here. No reachable output changes: FR-005 makes make the one entry point, the make-only guard covers the binary, and make tool-yield always passes --root. A compiled binary also has no source-tree location to inherit.

decisions.summary: fix_yield checks that a fix's commit exists with git rev-parse --verify --quiet <sha>^{commit} instead of git cat-file -e.
decisions.why: This is an implementation choice through the one git reader. The two commands differ only on a sha that names a non-commit object, which cat-file -e accepts and ^{commit} rejects. A ruled fix's recorded commit cannot be such an object, so no case reaches the difference.

decisions.summary: The Makefile's fix-yield, tool-yield and both step-back forms are repointed. The five .py files are deleted in the same cut.
decisions.why: ask:449-T83-scope says every by-command caller switches in the same cut. The GM gave standing approval on 2026-11-10: "Yes please delete Python files once their Rust ports land."

decisions.summary: specs/375-enforced-wave-process/measurements.json entry 375-a7-turn-time ran python3 scripts/measure/turn_time.py on a transcript that is no longer on disk. Its command is retired and its values are kept as history, so make figures no longer runs it.
decisions.why: This narrows FR-001's rule that a recorded measurement running Python is rewritten to the port and re-run as the proof. Here the rule is physically impossible: the input is gone, and the command fails both before and after the cut, so no rewrite could be re-run as proof. The GM's 2026-11-09 words, "I don't think we need to port the past feature harnesses if those are not still used", cover a measurement that nothing can run. The values stay as history, and the arbiter ruled it as ask:449-T120-retire-375-a7, on the same pattern as T79, T89 and T118.

decisions.summary: The differential normalizes N1 to N8: N1 stderr from Traceback on, N2 argparse usage text, N3/N5/N8 clock-derived values, N4 bytecode, N6 the Makefile path in make's own error line, N7 the scratch fixtures' .git internals.
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text rules N1 and N2: a traceback's text and argparse's own usage text are not bound, while exit status and stdout stay held. N3, N5 and N8 come from the wall clock, which differs between any two runs. N4 and N7 are artifacts of the interpreter and of git, not outputs of the tool. N6 is make's own text naming the changed Makefile, the same shape as ask:449-T92-messages. No output that the tool itself writes is relaxed.

decisions.summary: make step-back with no TRIGGER is not run end to end because it writes a real bundle's name. Its two halves are run separately.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds the cases that the piece's tests and suites hold. The differential's Makefile forms are the session's own extra coverage, and the plan states this exclusion openly. If a kept test or suite case held this form, it would be owed. The bundle names none.

decisions.summary: These divergences are declared but no case reaches them: Unicode isalnum in the trigger's escape, glob characters in a session id or F=, NaN or a lone surrogate in JSON, integers past 64 bits, -h exiting 2, a lone --, and a registry kind that is not text.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds the cases that tests and suites hold, and none of these is held. -h exiting 2 is ruled directly by ask:449-usage-text: --help is bound only where a kept case holds it. The most reachable item is a non-ASCII letter in a real trigger, which would change a bundle's filename only. It is recorded, not reproduced, and it does not change the class.

decisions.summary: Cut the full hook run (make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1) under the GM's 2026-11-12 pre-approval: a concrete target (the full run's wall time) with a measured saving, 43 s to 29 s from a cool start.
decisions.why: The GM pre-approved efficiency work with 'concrete targets with significant measured expected savings' and then asked that 'the performance bits of the tests and landing' be prioritized; the full hook run is the tests' time, and a one-third measured cut is the condition he set.

decisions.summary: The idle-tests guard's real-time waits shortened through fixture seams IDLE_WAIT_S / IDLE_DEFER_S, honored inside a fixture alone; the suite's cases kept.
decisions.why: Removes waiting a test asked for without changing any case or the guard's production behavior; no clause of the request or FR-002 is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The entry-gate suite's fixture answers notes a question at a time, other subjects by kind and the three modal units as one answer - three record-owed calls in place of eleven - the same units answered and case 4 still proving the gate falls quiet.
decisions.why: Every case and assertion is kept (FR-002's 'every case its tests and its suites hold'); only the fixture's route to the same answered state changes, matching how a session records answers.

decisions.summary: The Makefile's missing-program self-test starts beside the suites instead of after them; its pass, failure and stamp are read after the suites as before, and a plain make hooks-test still skips it when unchanged.
decisions.why: Moves no check out of the run and changes no verdict or skip rule; only its start time moves.

decisions.summary: The next bound (sync-with-main, with entry-gate and l7r-gate within 4 s of it) and its candidate cuts are recorded and not cut in this task.
decisions.why: The pre-approval permits identified, measured improvements; it does not oblige every candidate to be cut in one task, and recording the next bound with its candidates serves the GM's 'stop and measure again ... what the next most low-hanging fruit is'. Nothing asked is dropped.

decisions.summary: The ledger, speckit-todo --holding and the claims are called in process; the stamp, coverage-exempt, arbiter gate-held, cohort, the *-gate.sh scripts, make, sync-with-main, make-docs and ruff stay commands, as the Python ran them

decisions.summary: tick-task.py stays Python, run by path; it gains a --land-check flag so the first pass asks it about every task in one process, its rows report box_open, and the Rust makes the _box_flag choice; the refusal is asked in the first pass instead of just before each tick
decisions.why: ask:449-T83-scope keeps tick-task.py as Python behind the Rust land, run by path under the T065 clause. One process per run is what FR-006 asks for, the boxes are still read by the one boxes_refusal (FR-003), and the _box_flag choice stays in Rust, so no landing logic moves into Python. The block rests on an unmeasured premise: that nothing between the first pass and a tick changes that tick's refusal, because 'each of its own task'. The case that would break this is a land-batch where a later task's refusal reads an earlier task's tick in the same landing, for example a closing tick after a sibling. The block's list of 53 command cases names 'a closing tick refused and reverted', but it does not say a batch with an earlier sibling tick was among them. If the refusal does read sibling state, this becomes an FR-002 difference. That is a gap in the differential, not a narrowing of the request.

decisions.summary: The engine-path question the land asked codeid.py is answered by the cohort crate's identical regex, is_landing_engine, in process
decisions.why: ask:449-T062-py-id keeps codeid.py for the .py id (ast.dump), not for a path regex. Rust already holds an identical regex, so this adds no second implementation of anything the Python still owns, and the outputs are covered by the differential.

decisions.summary: land.py's file_left branch (no caller sets it) and the start_cover branches (None since FR-001b deleted the Python tests) are not ported
decisions.why: Code that nothing can reach produces no verdict or output, so FR-002 has nothing to bind there. start_cover went dead through FR-001b itself. Both are backed by a dated git grep census.

decisions.summary: The claims door verbs only land.py asks (scope_split, file_left, flight_live, CLAIMS_FEATURE_DIR) and seam::file_left stay through this commit and are removed in T124
decisions.why: ask:449-T82-claims has land.py on claims_door until T83. Keeping these verbs past T121 is a narrowing, but the ruling's own words force it: this commit has to be landed by the Python land.py, which calls these verbs during the run. Removing them in the same commit cannot work. The removal is now owed to T124. This bundle does not show that T124 is filed or what it holds, so I have not confirmed it. The session must make sure it exists.

decisions.summary: GATE_MACHINERY: scripts/land.py replaced by rust/gate/crates/land/
decisions.why: The existing rule (a change to the land runs the tooling tests) follows the code to its new home. This keeps what is already enforced rather than adding anything.

decisions.summary: The land registers its stop step on the guard's single TERM handler (l7r_guard::shared::tempdir::before_exit), pinned by tests
decisions.why: This fixes a Rust-side defect the differential found, where a stopped landing exited 143 with its gate still running. The fix makes the port behave as the Python did, which is what FR-002 asks for.

decisions.summary: The usage text naming land.py, -h exiting 2, and INT cleaning only the scratch and exiting 130 are kept; make land-stop finds an l7r-gate land process
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text holds the exit status and the hand-written text, and keeping more than that ruling binds narrows nothing. land-stop has to look for the process that is now the land, and its cases are in the differential.

decisions.summary: The commit deletes land.py and points make land at l7r-gate land (the LAND_DRIVER switch collapsed); it is landed by HEAD's land.py saved outside the tree and run through make land ... LAND_RUN="python3 <saved runner>"
decisions.why: This carries out ask:449-T83-scope's 'its own commit the last the Python land.py lands and the one that deletes it'. The block does not say whether the LAND_RUN override stays in the Makefile after this commit. If it stays, it is a permanent knob that can put any command in place of the land. Nobody asked for that and no escape records its use, so it would be unrequested behavior owing either a ruling or a removal (for example in T124). It is not a narrowing of what was asked, so it does not block this verdict.

decisions.summary: FR-002 proof: a verdict replay of 104 runs with 0 differing; 53 command cases with 1 differing (push-failed, a same-second bypass-record name); 14 replay-owing cases and 50 audit cases with 0 differing; failure parity; normalizations for tracebacks, argparse usage, record file names, utc and commit, same-second add-or-modify, JOBS and memory figures, and commit ids
decisions.why: This is the replay over recorded landings that the ruling asks for. Each normalization is either a ruled case (ask:449-usage-text covers traceback and argparse text) or a clock, id or machine artifact. The one remaining difference comes from naming records by the second inside the harness, not from Python and Rust behaving differently.

decisions.summary: specs/375's sc001-replay is left as it is (prose that make cannot parse, listed NOT RE-MEASURED before and after); the 14 replay-owing cases stand as its proof of sameness
decisions.why: FR-001's rewrite clause covers commands that run Python in its three named forms. ask:449-T83-scope itself says this entry records make replay-owing, which stays. Aside for the arbiter or the GM: the ruling assumed make figures re-runs this entry, and the block measured that it does not, before the cut or after. The entry stays permanently NOT RE-MEASURED under a rule that figures are re-run, never read. Fixing that is not part of this task.

decisions.summary: Provenance comments, rust/gate/CLAUDE.md, scripts/CLAUDE.md and docs/guards.md repointed by a git grep census; make static, rust-test and hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 green
decisions.why: The census at the cut is what ask:449-T83-scope asks for, and its search space is stated (the three names and LAND_DRIVER, outside specs/ and dev/).

decisions.summary: Remove the claims door's scope_split, file_left, flight_live and CLAIMS_FEATURE_DIR verbs from Rust door.rs and scripts/claims_door.py, with their tests, once the Rust land is make land.
decisions.why: ask:449-T82-claims put these verbs on scripts/claims_door.py for the Python that stays Python - land.py and replay_owing.py until T83 - on the plan_door pattern, whose door holds no logic and whose verbs leave with their callers; ask:449-T83-scope has T121 delete land.py in its own last landing. A verb only land.py asked has no caller left once T121 landed, so removing it completes the ruled lifecycle and narrows nothing the GM asked (make this a Rust codebase; delete Python once its Rust port lands). FR-003 is kept: the door stays for its remaining callers (impl_check.py and the verbs they use), and nothing still running is switched off. The task stays a follow-up of T121 rather than part of T121 for the reason the ruling gives (the Python land.py had to land its own deletion through these verbs).

decisions.summary: Remove the Rust seam::file_left and its constant, with their tests.
decisions.why: The Rust half that served only the door verb file_left; the Rust land asks scope_split and flight_live in process (kept), and file_left/its constant have no other asker per the recorded census. Removing dead Rust that only served a removed door verb is inside the port; it changes no verdict or output of a live command (FR-002).

decisions.summary: Apply the removal patch kept from T121's landing commit rather than re-deriving it.
decisions.why: A method choice; it decides nothing the spec or request leaves open about scope.

decisions.summary: Premise and done-check: git grep -n of the four names over scripts and rust finds them only in provenance comments and the door's tests (observed 2026-11-12); exits make static, make rust-test, make land green, red set down or ruled through make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Enforcement of the removal, not new scope; the figure carries a one-shot label (date and method). Non-blocking note: the stated search space is scripts and rust only - it does not reach the Makefile, tests/, l7r/, .specify/ or specs/, where a name can be held as a string (feature 185); a door caller there would be switched off contrary to FR-003. Running the same git grep over the whole tree before deleting closes that, and does not change this decision's class. ask:449-T82-claims names three Python callers of this door: land.py, replay_owing.py and impl_check.py; the block accounts for the first two and not impl_check.py, which stays a door caller to the phase-3 close. Precondition on the deletion: the census re-run with no pathspec, showing impl_check.py and the Makefile ask none of the four names.

decisions.summary: File T125 under the GM's 2026-11-12 pre-approval: target the full hook run's end (idle-tests, the longest suite, started 19.6 s in by roster order), expected saving about 8 s, measured 52.5 s against 59.4 s mean alternated three a side; ordered after T124.
decisions.why: The pre-approval's conditions are a concrete target and a significant measured expected saving, and the task names both and quotes the words, as request.md's 2026-11-12 entry requires; the GM's later priority puts the tests' and landing's time first after T121, and the full hook run is the landing's longest phase. The measured gain is the removal of the baseline's 62-63 s tail (treatment 51.0-54.9 s against 52.4-63.3 s), not a shift of the floor; that is still a concrete measured saving the GM's words cover.

decisions.summary: make hooks-test dispatches its suites to its eight slots longest first by each suite's seconds at its last run, kept beside its stamp (.git/hooks-test/<suite>.s, pass or fail); a never-timed suite first; the general rule rather than naming idle-tests.
decisions.why: A reordering of the same work to cut the run's wall time, the target the pre-approval covers; the general rule was A/B'd equal to the single-suite move and nothing in the request or spec fixes the roster order.

decisions.summary: A suite's kept seconds is a hint to the order alone; a missing or stale one only moves a suite in the queue.
decisions.why: Keeps the new state from touching any verdict; narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: T98's measurement that longest first was slower, on an earlier roster, is superseded by today's measurement.
decisions.why: T98's ordering finding was a session measurement, not a GM requirement; FR-012's T98 asks only that the suites run in parallel, which stays.

decisions.summary: The engine-freeze suite's two roll fixtures wait (5 s bound) for the roll to appear in /proc by name instead of a fixed 0.5 s sleep, so the cases test a running roll and the other-tree case no longer passes vacuously.
decisions.why: A flake the requested reorder exposed (three engine-freeze cases failed in one longest-first run); the block's own 'Kept as it was: every suite, its cases and its checks' pins the cases, and the change removes the other-tree case's vacuous pass rather than altering what it expects. Needed for the requested speed-up to land green, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: Raising PARTS_MAX above two not done: measured no gain (52.8 s at four, 53.4 s at eight against 50.9 s at two).
decisions.why: Declining an unrequested alternative on measurement; the pre-approval licenses only targets with significant measured savings, which this lacked.

decisions.summary: Every suite, its cases and checks, the stamps, HOOKS_JOBS and PARTS_MAX kept as they were.
decisions.why: Preserves all verdicts and the existing parallelism; removes nothing the GM asked to keep.

decisions.summary: T126 is filed under the GM's 2026-11-12 pre-approval: target l7r-gate.sh's per-call cost, expected saving about 12 ms a call, measured saving on the full hook run 46.6 s against 51.5 s mean over twelve alternated runs.
decisions.why: The pre-approval's conditions are a concrete target and a significant measured saving, the task naming both and quoting the GM's words; the block does all three, and the GM's later words put the tests' and the landing's time first. About 10% of the full hook run, five of six pairs favoring the change by 5 to 9 s, re-read from wrap.txt and wrap2.txt (the twelve numbers and both means match the block). The one HEAD run faster than every new run is reported by the block itself. Soft spot, not a finding: performance item 3's 'many hundreds of calls a full hook run' carries a method that does not count calls; the measured A/B, not that estimate, is what the significance rests on. No FR codifies the 2026-11-12 round (FR-012 and SC-007 stop at T116); the request's own sentence on how such a task is filed is the rule, and the block meets it.

decisions.summary: The wrapper reads the account's home from /etc/passwd in its own shell, matching the shell's UID, with getent kept as the fallback where no line matches.
decisions.why: An implementation choice inside the approved target that keeps the same answer (the same account's home); narrows nothing the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: The stale-binary test becomes one find -newer ... -quit over the same sources in place of a bash glob walk with -nt.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds Python-to-Rust ports; this is shell to shell, so FR-002 is cited by analogy rather than as the operative constraint. The change only widens the rebuild trigger (dot files now seen, strictly newer kept), never skips a rebuild the old test asked for, and the block records a touched source still rebuilding. Nothing asked for is narrowed.

decisions.id: D4 l7r-guard.sh left as it is
decisions.summary: The guards' wrapper is not changed, its rust/guard walk measured at 1.6 ms.
decisions.why: The request asks for concrete targets with significant measured savings, not every wrapper; leaving one below that bar applies the GM's condition rather than narrowing it. Recorded precisely: the 1.6 ms covers the walk only, and the bundle does not say whether l7r-guard.sh also runs the getent/id/cut chain (4.7 ms in the gate wrapper), so that part is unmeasured; it is a possible later target, not a narrowing of this one.

decisions.summary: After T125; green is make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 and make land, red recorded and a claim of impossibility ruled through make arbiter-ask; one landing.
decisions.why: Follows the GM's priority on the tests' and the landing's time after the in-progress work; the exits check the requested saving and the unchanged outputs.

decisions.why: Placement is design; the one-writer result is what ask:449-T82-claims requires, and the census names its search space.

decisions.why: FR-003: no piece runs both; the fixture stood in for the inline Python that no longer runs.

decisions.why: FR-002 and ask:449-usage-text: hand-written usage stays bound; keeping it is the strict reading.

decisions.summary: close_check.py stays Python, run by path from reviewed only on the branch where the GM's box is a feature's last open box, under the T065 clause, gaining a new --reasons-json DIR SPECS mode that writes no usage-log line; T127 filed for its port, the by-path run going when it lands
decisions.why: Adding a mode changes a Python file the GM said is no longer being changed except to delete it. Legitimate because the spec's own placement requires it: ask:449-T067-scope puts close_check.py in phase 3 carrying the T065 clause until ported, and gm_review.py reached it by import, which a Rust caller cannot do (FR-003: a name a command can carry goes by command); the mode only emits, as JSON, what the import returned and keeps the import's no-usage-log behavior, adding no logic, and its run is on a rare branch, never a plain Bash call or Edit. Should the mode compute anything the import did not, this ruling does not cover it. The alternative, porting close_check in the same cut, is phase-3 work the spec allows but does not require of T91, and T127 holds it.

decisions.summary: the arbiter's failure message 'python3 said: <traceback>' becomes 'gm-review said: <why>', two Rust tests in arbiter/tests.rs changed to expect it
decisions.why: The arbiter is not the replaced piece and the fixed words are the Rust arbiter's own; keeping 'python3 said' would name a subprocess that no longer exists after the port. Ruled precedent T87-arbiter-test-message (LEGITIMATE) on the same message pattern. Exit status and verdict unchanged.

decisions.summary: claims-known on a gm-review write failure prints 'gm-review: <why>' where it printed the runner's traceback; exit status unchanged through the same ? of the same function
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text: an uncaught Python traceback's text is not bound for any port, its exit status and stdout held; the block records the exit path compared at HEAD and in the working tree. Not resting on T87.

decisions.summary: differential of 1,272 cases accepts 8 differences (7 rows holding NaN, 1 integer past 64 bits) and lists divergences no case reaches; in-process callers 55 cases with none
decisions.why: FR-002 binds every case the piece's tests and suites hold: the kept suites (make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1, 54 suites) are green and the real queues of all 47 features as stored and reopened match; the 8 are constructed row values no writer produces, and the only writer after the cut is the port. The differential reaches beyond FR-002's bound set rather than excluding a bound case.

decisions.summary: lands after T126
decisions.why: The GM 2026-11-12 put the tests' and landing's performance ahead of remaining ports only where a concrete target with a significant measured saving is identified, otherwise 'keep working on the port of the tooling'. The block names no open target; the bundle holds no task list, so that is the reach of this finding.

decisions.summary: census at the cut by stated pathspecs; docs/guards.md pointer to a nonexistent test repointed to the Rust tests; no measurements.json command runs the file
decisions.why: FR-001's rewrite-measurements and census requirements; the pointer fix serves the cut.
