decisions.why: Every caller repointed in the same cut and the .py deleted, as FR-001 and FR-003 require (no piece runs both); tick-task.py staying Python and reaching ported code by command is ask:449-T89-reviews' ruled pattern. The deletion rests on the GM's standing approval quoted in the spec (2026-11-10).

decisions.summary: impl_check.py stays Python (phase 3, its own later port); the Rust runs impl_check.py --missing-json DIR... by path, one process a run and none when no non-grandfathered research-record directory needs it, no usage line; the new mode prints only what missing() returned; stderr carried inside the error on failure, passed through or dropped on success as before.
decisions.why: FR-001 places impl_check.py in phase 3 and the T065 clause governs a ported piece reaching unported Python by path; the starts are the push, gm-review's last box and tick-task's last tick, none a plain Bash call, a plain Edit or a make done. A logic-free JSON verb on the Python side is the door pattern the spec uses throughout (codeid.py --debug-free-equal, bundle_door, claims_door); impl_check runs in one implementation, so FR-003 holds. The mode leaves with impl_check's own port by that pattern.

decisions.summary: Every form ported (--carries and --write-grandfathered included); --reasons-json kept for tick-task.py with no usage line (T118 --each-state precedent); passed/refused recording, exit 2 as refused, a raise recording nothing; usage text byte for byte; measurements.json read as Python's json reads it, NaN and Infinity as values.
decisions.why: FR-002 parity; the differential compares every file written (the usage log included, utc normalized), and the tick and gm groups (9 and 8 cases) show no difference.

decisions.summary: Accept 2 of 117 scratch cases differing: a directory named '٣-x', whose non-ASCII digit Python's int() reads as 3 (pointing the user at make feature-report F=3, a different feature) and the Rust refuses. Re-derived from results-scratch.json: 'differ': 2, both this name; results-real/push/tick/gm/impl all 'differ': 0, seen totals 1,469+22+9+8+117+20 = 1,645.
decisions.why: Ruled here on FR-002's own scope, not on its written exception (which covers a port that stops refusing correct work, not one that starts refusing a mis-parse) and not on the T91/T118 precedent, which the block cites without an ask: id. FR-002 binds 'every case its tests and its suites hold'; this input is one the session's harness constructed, held by no kept test or suite case, and every real feature directory in the clone (1,469 cases, both forms, real and empty grandfathered lists) and every real push range (22) match. The request's purpose - a Rust codebase that decides as the Python did on the work it actually does - is intact; the divergence is disclosed in the plan.

decisions.summary: Known divergences no case reaches: a lone surrogate, nesting past 128 or 1e400 in a measurements.json, a directory name not UTF-8; plus the normalizations (stderr from the first Traceback, the usage line's utc, each side's scratch path).
decisions.why: Adjudicated apart from the '٣-x' case: none is a case any kept test or suite holds, and the real tree reaches none (every real directory's measurements.json is read in the 1,469 real cases with no difference), so FR-002's binding set is untouched. The traceback normalization is ask:449-usage-text's ruling that a traceback's text is not bound; utc and scratch paths are run-specific, not outputs.

decisions.summary: usage_log, hm_escape and hm_shape ported onto the guard crate's shared/ (shared::usage the one writer, shared::escape, shared::shape/wait); gate commands under `log usage|goals` and a new `escape reason-ok` verb
decisions.why: FR-001 places these libraries in phase 3 and ask:449-phase3-remainder names T129 the hook libraries; where the port lives and how its commands are named is design inside the request.

decisions.summary: every caller repointed: Makefile LOGESCAPE/idle-tests/goals line, the gate shells, sync-with-main, land-tooling by command; clone_sync_hooks in process; memo_check, phase_sources, check-entry-headings, tick-task and escape_log stay Python and run the gate command
decisions.why: FR-003 (one implementation runs once the port passes); the Python callers keep their ruled placements (memo_check T140, check-entry-headings phase 4, phase_sources T066/phase 3, tick-task T131) and reach the port by command, which no ruling forbids.

decisions.summary: guardlog.sh's escape_or_refuse and guard_cmd deleted rather than repointed
decisions.why: nothing calls either once every guard is Rust (observed 2026-11-12 by git grep of both names, search space stated); removing dead code changes no output FR-002 binds.

decisions.summary: hm_tree.py deleted unported
decisions.why: its port is shared::tree since T010; the census (git grep over Makefile, *.mk, *.sh, *.py, *.rs, .claude/, tests/) shows only comments and one recorded refusal naming it; GM 2026-11-10 'Yes please delete Python files once their Rust ports land' and GM 2026-11-09 on not porting what nothing runs.

decisions.summary: hm_shape gets no command; its one outside caller, a no-poll suite case, becomes a unit test of shared::wait checking the same condition
decisions.why: hm_shape's port landed at T003/T009 with its FR-002 comparison; the case keeps its assertion (the escaped wait it builds parses under bash -n), moving with the piece it tests as FR-001 moves surviving tests; no case is dropped.

decisions.summary: the usage writer appends one line in one append-mode write and takes no flock, where the Python took an exclusive lock
decisions.why: FR-002 binds verdicts and outputs, and a lock is neither; a single O_APPEND write of a short line on a local file is not interleaved, so the log's contents are the same, and the landed, reviewed Rust writers (stamp.rs, checks/passes.rs) already write this way. Not ruled on cost grounds.

decisions.summary: escape::enough splits words on Python's whitespace (x1c-x1f included) for every guard; reason-ok reads stdin with surrogateescape as the C.UTF-8 Python did
decisions.why: moves landed Rust toward the Python it replaced at the one edge the floor could differ, which is FR-002's direction, not a departure from it.

decisions.summary: check tool-signals reads `log usage` as a record marker, skips Rust test files, and names the command in its fix
decisions.why: the check now reads less (Rust test files). Its purpose is that every registered tool records its usage; a test file is not a tool and holds no tool's record marker, while read literally the check would refuse the port itself on fixture scratch names. The block measured every registered tool still found (exit 0, suite green), and old-form markers are still accepted, so the purpose is intact.

decisions.summary: test-gate-write-hooks.sh no longer copies the deleted preflight.py; clone-sync context drops the python field nothing read once the run is in process
decisions.why: removing a dangling copy and an unread field changes no verdict or output; both follow from the port itself.

decisions.summary: FR-002 differential (7,854 cases, none differing) normalizes utc, the guard-log entry's file name, argparse's own text where both exit 2, and a traceback's text
decisions.why: timestamps and generated file names are not comparable outputs; argparse text and traceback text are exactly what ask:449-usage-text rules unbound, exit status and stdout held.

decisions.summary: the differential normalizes --help output
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text binds --help only where a kept test or suite case holds it or a caller reads it; make hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 is green on 54 suites with the Rust in place, so no kept case binds --help text that differs, and the plan names no caller reading it. The narrowing sits inside the ruling's own condition.

decisions.summary: the Makefile's parse-time goals line runs the gate wrapper with L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1 (runs the binary present, builds only when none exists; a failed build records nothing for that run)
decisions.why: FR-011 requires the loop not drift back to slow commands, and before the cut make rust-test never built l7r-gate; a stale binary writes the same line. The failed-build case is outside every case FR-002 binds ('every case its tests and its suites hold'), so not recording there is no departure from it.

decisions.summary: About 70 failing make-figures commands that run no file (35 greps of old skill paths in 261, greps/ls on moved text or untracked SVGs, prose with shell syntax, 375's three make feature-report on transcripts no longer on disk, one prose entry in 449's own file) are reported and not retired

It is legitimate on purpose, not by completing anyone's thought: the GM's request is a Python-to-Rust port and the 2026-11-09 words are about not porting unused past-feature harnesses; FR-001's rewrite duty covers only recorded measurements that RUN Python. A failing grep, ls or prose entry runs no Python and no file, imposes no port, and retiring it serves no clause of the GM's request - it would be unrequested cleanup. The ruling's own words bound its subject to files: the consequence is 'its file deleted unported', the counterpart is 'the measurement scripts that run and work are ported (T139)', and the census it rules on is of tracked .py files. Adjudicated separately, the three make feature-report commands run feature_report, which T119 placed on the port and which is reached through make, so no port-or-delete decision rides on them either way (unlike ask:449-T120-retire-375-a7, whose command ran python3 turn_time.py and so was a Python-running measurement FR-001 had to rewrite). decisions.summary: --land-check and --resolve kept as commands of the binary; Path.glob and fnmatch empty ranges ported in glob.rs.
decisions.why: Implementation choices that keep FR-002 parity; decide nothing the spec left to the GM.

decisions.summary: The land's message 'tick-task.py raised on <task>' becomes 'the tick raised on <task> (above)'.
decisions.why: FR-002 binds the land's own hand-written words, and this changes them. The ruling rests on the purpose test alone. The cut deletes tick-task.py and runs the tick in process, so keeping the string byte for byte would make the land report that a program no longer in the tree raised. That would be a false output, and it would work against the request's purpose: "making this a Rust codebase instead of a Python codebase". What a reader acts on is unchanged: the task named, the failure, the verdict and the exit. The plan names T87 and T91 as precedent. The bundle does not carry them, so this ruling takes the plan's word for them and does not rest on them. Neither ask:449-usage-text nor ask:449-T92-messages supports the change: both keep a tool's hand-written words bound.

decisions.summary: The first pass's 'tick-task.py --land-check exited N' becomes a raise carrying the crate's own error.
decisions.why: This one is physically impossible to keep: the check now runs in process, so there is no child process and no exit status N to report. The verdict, a raise in the first pass, is kept.

decisions.summary: FR-002 proof: 274 command-line cases and 31 land/task-add cases, none differing, under named normalizations (traceback past its first line, bypass record file name and same-second record split, phase-read clock, the renamed message, AUTO_MERGE, stamps, commit ids); five divergences named that no case reaches.
decisions.why: Each normalization is a ruled one (traceback, ask:449-usage-text), clock or identity noise, or the message ruled above. The one raw difference was a same-second timing collision, and it went away on three reruns. The five named divergences are inputs that no test or suite holds, and FR-002 binds only 'every case its tests and its suites hold'. Naming them is disclosure, not an exclusion.

On record: the block derives all four forms from two Python mechanisms (`if d is not None and task`, the raise on bad JSON), so the 'failed run' form's equivalence rests on a failed gate run printing non-JSON stdout; a nonzero exit with valid JSON on stdout is neither named nor pinned. FR-002 binds the cases the tests hold, so this does not block.

decisions.why: Enforcement of FR-002 (same verdicts) and FR-004 (coverage floor) for the requested port; a check whose only effect is that the ported behavior holds is in scope.

decisions.summary: No other python3 snippet of the guard asks the gate, from `git grep -n "subprocess.run" -- rust/guard/src`; the checks make hooks-test, make static, make rust-test.
decisions.why: Excludes nothing requested: the task claims only this hop, and FR-001 phase 1 still owes any other Python start in the guard. Finding on the search space (not a narrowing): the stated goal is 'a spec-fidelity dispatch starts no Python in the guard', but the grep searches a Python API name inside snippets, not the mechanism. It misses `subprocess.check_output`, `Popen`, `os.system` and any snippet that does not shell out. The waist is the Rust side that starts the interpreter, e.g. `git grep -nE 'python3?\b' -- rust/guard/src`, read hit by hit. The census as a done criterion should use that search.

decisions.summary: 829 cases, 11 differing: 6 are make's own '*** [...Makefile:685]' line naming the Makefile each side ran with -f; 5 are raises with identical exit, stdout and files whose traceback text above the shared last line differs. The stamps and bytecode are harness hygiene. Being non-zero, the task is not straight under FR-001c, which is why this review is owed.

'No case reaches' is a statement about the 829 harness cases and the held suites, as the block says; it is not a claim that live data cannot contain them, and I did not verify it beyond the block.

decisions.summary: spec.rs is the one writer of the three scripts' measurements.json writes, and one inventory parser serves both 238 and 242, as 238's script already loaded 242's by path.
decisions.why: This is an internal shape inside FR-002's same-outputs rule, and it keeps one implementation where the Python already shared one. Nothing that was asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: The recorded commands of 238, 239, 242, 261, 430 and 432 are rewritten to the gate commands and re-run, and the values of 238, 239, 242's inventory_census, 430 and 432 reproduce.
decisions.why: FR-001: a recorded command is rewritten in the commit that ports what it runs, and the rewritten command is re-run as the proof. Note: the Approach line says 29 commands, but this decision's per-feature list adds up to 28 (4+2+12+8+1+1), so one command is unaccounted for. That is a count to reconcile, not a narrowing.

decisions.summary: 261's eight commands are ported even though they no longer reproduce their recorded figures (the maps they read have since been re-laid). They write nothing, so make figures compares nothing for them, and both sides give the same output.
decisions.why: The retire test in ask:449-phase3-remainder is 'a command make figures runs that fails when run today, or that invokes deleted code'. Neither half fires here: make figures does not fail on these commands, and they read live maps. FR-002 allows maps to change. Python and Rust print the same thing, so FR-002 holds. This is the same test that retires note_census, applied the same way.

decisions.summary: specs/242/measure/note_census.py is retired here instead of ported: its four commands become <retired: ...> with their values kept, and the script is deleted.
decisions.why: Both halves of the ruling's own retire test are met as stated. make figures fails on the script before and after the cut (all four values move to 0), and it reads .claude/skills/diagram/research/citations/*.html, which feature 258 deleted (3e2fe218b), so no port could reproduce 995/260/2/120. The ground is the arbiter's class test, not the GM's 'not still used' line; make figures does run the script, so that line would be the weaker ground. The retire class was assigned to T130, but the ruling defines the class by a test and not by a list, so a member T130 missed is still in the class. The retirement keeps the values as history, the fr005_probe pattern, so no recorded figure is lost.

decisions.summary: The census's tier-share sum check is not carried into the Rust (a commented omission): it cannot fail once no tier is stray, and the stray-tier check runs first.
decisions.why: The Approach line says the scripts are 'ported whole', which contradicts this omission. The plan should say 'whole but two unreached branches'. Ruled on its merits: FR-002 binds outputs on cases, and no input reaches this branch because it follows logically from the stray-tier check before it. A literal carry would be a Rust line that no test can reach, which conflicts with FR-004's floor of every line reached (measure is held at 100%). Applying the rule literally is therefore impossible, not just awkward.

decisions.summary: Triage's unpacking-error branch is not carried into the Rust (a commented omission), on the premise that git prints no empty line in the output it parses.
decisions.why: This is judged separately from the tier-share branch because it is a different kind of claim. The tier-share branch is dead by logic; this one is dead only if a fact about git's output format holds. The block gives that fact without its own method label. The differential's 574 cases over the real claims history are taken as the measurement of it: a branch no case reaches is a branch with no output for FR-002 to bind. The FR-004 conflict is the same as for the tier-share branch. The premise is recorded here so that if git ever prints an empty line, this ruling falls with it.

decisions.summary: Three defects in the shared Rust are fixed for every crate: serde_json float_roundtrip turned on, math.hypot following CPython's algorithm, and py_float printing inf as inf.0.
decisions.why: Each fix makes a Rust port give the outputs of the Python it replaces, which FR-002 demands of every crate and not only of this task's. The before and after counts are recorded (509 to 0 of 6,000; 1,760 to 0 of 300,000). No behavior beyond FR-002 is added.

decisions.summary: The differential normalizes away a failing run's stderr (argparse's own text or a traceback; none of the nine writes stderr by hand, checked by grep of five forms) and swaps the old python3 command for the new one in written measurements.json files.
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text: argparse-generated stderr and an uncaught traceback's text are not outputs FR-002 binds, and exit status and stdout stay compared. The grep shows nothing hand-written is hidden by this. The command swap is FR-001's required rewrite. Neither hides a bound output.

decisions.summary: fixtures-and-board takes its arguments and ignores them, as the Python did.
decisions.why: FR-002: this reproduces the Python's behavior.

decisions.summary: triage-price reads git objects through one streaming git cat-file --batch.
decisions.why: This is an implementation shape with the same outputs (FR-002), in line with FR-006's one-process fixes. Nothing that was asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: claim, trial-start, trial-review and patch in a new gate crate `author` on `core`; make-docs in `cohort`; task-add and set-down in `task`; task-add calls the tick's repo_root/spec_dir in process, `tick --resolve` keeping its command form
decisions.why: Where a port lives is a design choice the spec leaves open; FR-001 places these phase-3 files and ask:449-phase3-remainder files T135. No output or scope changes.

decisions.summary: Every caller (Makefile targets, make static's page check, create-new-feature.sh, land-tooling.sh's default page check, test-set-down-hooks.sh, docs/efficiency-tooling.md) repointed and the seven .py files deleted in the same cut, no door
decisions.why: FR-003 (one implementation, none run both) and the GM's standing approval of 2026-11-10, 'Yes please delete Python files once their Rust ports land'.

decisions.summary: The push row's make-docs becomes an in-process kind under the same name and timing key; the land's first pass checks and writes in process, a failed write ignored as the command's exit was; neither is diffed against HEAD's binary, covered by the make-docs cases and their own tests
decisions.why: Preserves the existing behavior (same name, same key, same ignore-on-failure) with one implementation (FR-003); they call the same function the 45 make-docs differential cases cover.

decisions.summary: The task template moves to plan/src/plan/template.rs, read by task-add, sections.rs and lint.rs; the polled lock and mirror_of into core::record::repo (used by make download-add); fmt_g into the guard's py_text
decisions.why: FR-003: one copy, no second implementation; sections.rs previously read task-add.py's source, which this cut deletes. No output changes.

decisions.summary: make-docs' unknown-category line spells 'Unrecognized' where the Python wrote 'Unrecognised'
decisions.why: Already a ruled case in the accepted spec, FR-002's ask:449-T135-spelling (the round arbiter, 2026-11-14).

decisions.summary: docs/make-targets.html's three generator lines name the Rust port instead of scripts/make-docs.py, on 'the T87 and T91 precedent', and the differential normalizes those three lines away
decisions.why: FR-002 requires the same outputs as the Python. The arbiter's ruling on THIS port today, ask:449-T135-spelling, changes one word and says 'every other output, verdict and exit status stays byte for byte'; ask:449-T92-messages adds that 'a path the Python wrote by hand stays bound', which a generator line naming scripts/make-docs.py is. The 'T87 and T91 precedent' is not a ruled case anywhere in the spec (spec-cited.md and spec-index.md hold none), and a prior task's plan is not the GM's words. None of the legitimating tests holds: writing the old path is not impossible; the GM's approval to delete Python files says nothing about what a generated page says about its generator; and keeping the string does not defeat the request's purpose, it satisfies FR-002 literally. 'The page would name a deleted file' is an accuracy ground, which does not legitimate an exception. The normalization also means '344 cases, 1 differing' counts one difference only after these lines were taken out (FR-001c: no case excluded or changed). Remedy: get a second FR-002 ruled case through make arbiter-ask, the route the spelling took, or keep the three lines byte for byte and drop them from the normalizations.

decisions.summary: --help exits 2 where the Python exited 0, the one differing case of the 344
decisions.why: ask:449-usage-text: '--help is bound only where a kept test or suite case holds it, and a port whose usage text is read by a caller or asserted by a kept suite case keeps it.' Within ONLY on that condition. The block does not say a search was made that no kept test, suite case or caller holds --help for these seven tools; the record should state that search.

decisions.summary: Normalized: stderr from Traceback on, argparse errors as exit 2 with empty stdout and a usage: opening, rows' utc, a guard-edit record's file name
decisions.why: Traceback text and argparse's generated stderr are unbound under ask:449-usage-text (exit and stdout held); utc and a generated record file name are run-dependent, not compared outputs.

decisions.summary: Divergences no case reaches: JSON NaN and lone surrogates, non-ASCII digits, integers past i128, isalnum on a session id, float vs whole seconds at the week's reset, a NaN lock timeout
decisions.why: FR-002 binds 'every case its tests and its suites hold'; these are outside every held case, and the plan names them openly rather than excluding a case.

decisions.summary: make-docs keeps its handling of nine [docs]-tagged targets as unrecognized categories, which --check has always passed
decisions.why: Keeps the Python's behavior, as FR-002 requires.

decisions.summary: After T139, one landing; exits green on make static, rust-test, hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 and make land, red set down or ruled through make arbiter-ask
decisions.why: Sequencing and the exits, nothing the spec settles differently.

decisions.summary: The five page-session tools are ported whole, with no door, into a new gate crate `pages` built on core, reviews and the guard; the ledger rows, append's lint and cost cells are called in process; the guard log's file naming and rename move into one helper, shared::log::place, which the guards' own writer also uses.
decisions.why: Where the port lives is a design choice. FR-001 asks for the port and ask:449-phase3-remainder assigns these files to T137. Having one log helper with two users follows FR-003's one implementation. Nothing that was asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: In the same cut, the Makefile's lines/append/research-claim/research-claims, page-session.sh and the runner's setsid self-restart are repointed to the gate commands and the five .py files are deleted.
decisions.why: This repoints callers in the cut that ports them, as FR-003 requires, and deletes the Python under the GM's standing approval of 2026-11-10. The environment variables are still read as before.

decisions.summary: reserve-prefix.py stays Python and reaches the Rust escape by command (`escape take`, exit 0/1/3, 2 for usage). If the gate cannot start, it refuses without the 'blocked' guard-log entry that the in-process call used to write.
decisions.why: The spec already places reserve-prefix.py in phase 4 (ask:449-T81-slices), and a by-command call from staying Python follows the door pattern the spec rules elsewhere. The gate-cannot-start case is a failure mode the by-command call creates. The verdict there is the same (it refuses) and only a log line is lost. FR-002 binds the cases the tests and suites hold, and none holds this one. The statement that nothing reaches it at the cut is asserted, not measured, so it is noted here but does not block.

decisions.summary: The stall watchdog recognizes a page-session queue by the Rust runner's exact argv. Its unit and suite tests check that the old Python form is no longer exempt, and a Python queue still running across the cut loses its retry-wait exemption until it ends.
decisions.why: The exemption is for page-session queues, and that rule is unchanged. The argv that identifies such a queue changes because the runner is ported and the Python deleted (FR-003, the GM's 2026-11-10 approval to delete). The changed suite case repoints the recognized name and leaves the verdict on a page-session queue as it was. Neither the request nor the spec promises in-flight Python processes a grace period across a cut, so keeping the old form exempt would preserve behavior nobody asked to preserve. This is not FR-002's 'refuses correct work' exception and does not need it.

decisions.summary: make lines translates Python's \Z to the Rust regex's \z. The claims sheet's lock is a blocking flock -x on <sheet>.lock, which works together with the old Python's fcntl.flock.
decisions.why: Both serve FR-002: the differential found a \Z mismatch and this removes it, and the lock keeps the Python's blocking semantics across both implementations during the cut.

decisions.summary: brief-load, research-claims sweep and speckit-todo --each-state are kept as command forms that have no caller (T119's rule).
decisions.why: This ports the tools whole under the plan's existing T119 rule. It adds a little and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: The one differing case: `research-claims -h` prints help and exits 0 in Python, and exits 2 in Rust, under ask:449-usage-text.
decisions.why: This applies a case the accepted spec already rules: ask:449-usage-text binds --help only where a kept test or suite case holds it or a caller reads its usage text. The block does not state that condition outright. Its nearest evidence is the census (git grep of each name over the Makefile, tests/, .claude/, the shell scripts and the measurements files, which finds only provenance comments and history) and green hook suites. The difference is ruled, so the task is not straight under FR-001c and gets this review, which it is getting.

decisions.summary: The differential normalizes: Traceback stderr; argparse's exit-2 usage text; the quoted regex-library text after 'KEY is not a regular expression - '; session ids and run-log names; the guard-log file name, utc and command; a goals line's utc; the stub's environment keys; the case path in the long cases. It lists unreached divergences (non-ASCII digits, isdigit vs is_numeric, re syntax beyond \Z, a non-UTF-8 environment value, a moved-303.json that is not an object, -p with no prompt, ties in claim times).
decisions.why: Each normalization is covered by a ruled case or is nondeterminism or a harness artifact. Traceback text and argparse's text fall under ask:449-usage-text. The quoted library error text falls under ask:449-T066-json-message, which keeps the fixed words bound. Ids, timestamps and pid-based file names are nondeterministic. The harness (diff.py's NORMALIZED list) says the runner's guard-log 'command' is the process's own argv: the generator naming itself, deleted in this cut, which ask:449-T135-generator rules, though the block does not cite it. Reserve's 'command' differs only by the harness's old/ directory. The listed divergences lie outside the cases FR-002 binds (the cases its tests and suites hold).

decisions.summary: specs/274-leaner-research-sessions/measure/probe.sh, which nothing runs, is deleted unported in this cut.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 2026-11-09 rule ('I don't think we need to port the past feature harnesses if those are not still used') and FR-001's phase-3 clause. ask:449-phase3-remainder's deletion class holds it. Deleting it with the files it runs, rather than in T130, changes the timing and not the outcome.

decisions.summary: The task runs after T135 in one landing. It exits on make static, rust-test, hooks-test HOOKS_ALL=1 and land, and a claim that it cannot be done goes to make arbiter-ask.
decisions.why: Procedure inside the plan's own process. Nothing that was asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Every ticked task with an id (lowercase `- [x] Tnn`) and its indented lines moves to tasks-done.md, unless it holds an open box; the GM-review box, headings, Occasions and prose stay; no recent ticked tasks kept; blocks byte for byte in id order; one pointer line, no per-block marker.
decisions.why: The GM asked for tooling that moves completed tasks out of tasks.md so it stops eating tokens. A ticked task that still holds an open box is not completed work (it holds a landing), and the GM box is an open review state, not a finished task, so keeping them is not a carve-out from the request. The tick itself treats only lowercase [x] as ticked and writes it that way, so every task finished through the tooling moves. Moving all finished tasks instead of keeping a few recent ones reads 'old completed tasks' at its widest and serves the token purpose.

decisions.summary: Every tick archives all of its feature's ticked tasks, plan section or not; make plan-archive and `tick --archive` move them by hand; 449 archived in the cut; closed features are not backfilled; the tick-archive usage line is recorded on every tick.
decisions.why: 'Automatically move' is carried by the tick. The purpose is long-running features worked on now, and each open feature clears at its next tick. The request asks for the mechanism, not a migration of closed features, so not backfilling does not take any case away from it, and the manual command stays available for any feature. The tool-yield shift is a side effect, not new behavior.

decisions.summary: One reader/mover in the guard's shared::speckit::tasks; the readers that need ticked tasks (state, approval at_rev, plan checks, next id, already-ticked, spec lint, report) read both files; readers of open tasks only keep reading tasks.md, from a stated grep census.
decisions.why: Without this, the archive would break readers: a feature would read as reopened, an archived id could be handed out again, and so on. Wiring the readers to the moved file is what makes the requested move correct (FR-003, one implementation). The enumeration states its search space.

decisions.summary: The tick's block end becomes any heading (it was only `## `, so a `###` heading got swallowed and 449's T001/T005/T070 were misplaced, repaired before the archive; closed 383/417 left as history); a refused land batch removes the tasks-done.md/plan-done.md its tick created.
decisions.why: The archive moves blocks by the tick's own block boundary, so a boundary that swallows a heading would carry that heading into tasks-done.md. A refused landing that leaves the new archive file untracked would leave the tree half-moved. Both fixes exist only so that the requested move is correct. Leaving closed features' history alone is not a narrowing of anything the GM asked for.

decisions.summary: A before/after comparison over every feature archived in a copy (1,001 outputs, none differing); the archived lookup reads lowercase [x] alone to match the tick's rule; an end-to-end make run; 449's sizes; static, rust-test and hooks-test green.
decisions.why: These are checks that only fail if the requested archive changes what any reader answers, or if it does not happen. That is enforcement of the request and FR-002, not a property the GM never mentioned. The lowercase rule keeps the archived lookup consistent with the tick, so it is not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Done before the phase-4 slices, which file their tasks into the archived tasks.md; budget one landing.
decisions.why: This is sequencing within the feature. It takes nothing out of the request.

decisions.summary: guard_log reaches the Rust through the gate binary (l7r-gate log guard), not the guard binary through l7r-guard.sh; the one hook-time caller runs under L7R_GATE_STALE_OK=1 and a new L7R_GATE_NO_BUILD=1 seam so it never waits on a build
decisions.why: A choice of route for the port FR-001 and ask:449-phase4-slices Q12 require; it keeps no Python and changes no output. The loop through l7r-guard.sh's no-binary path is the stated reason. The no-build seam keeps hook-time cost off a compile, which serves the request's own purpose (hook latency, the GM 2026-11-07).

decisions.summary: On l7r-guard.sh's no-binary path, when the gate has no binary either, the failed-open entry is written by a new shell writer, scripts/hooks/lib/failed-open-log.sh (jq, or printf without jq), byte for byte HEAD's Python entry; every other entry goes through the one Rust writer
decisions.why: FR-001 says the Python is replaced by Rust, and this one path is replaced by shell instead. Running Rust there is physically impossible: the path exists because no binary is built. The only other choices are keeping Python (the request refuses that) or dropping the entry (an FR-002 output lost, and the only record that the guards did not run). The request's purpose is no Python, and that holds on this path too. The writer is confined to that one path, and the differential's 1,028 no-binary cases match HEAD.

decisions.summary: Two disclosed edges of the shell writer: a lower-case float literal (nan) that jq reads and Python's JSON rejects, and, without iconv, a non-UTF-8 input that also holds a real U+FFFD
decisions.why: FR-002 binds every case the tests and suites hold. Neither edge is a held case: upper-case NaN and the payload shapes are held, run on the no-binary path, and match (nogate-payload 125/0 in results.json). No held case is excluded or changed. The edges are disclosed in the file header, on a path reached only when nothing is built, and on input Claude Code's JSON serializer does not emit. If a held case is ever found among them, this becomes a narrowing.

decisions.summary: pyjson::loads keeps integers past u64, NaN, Infinity and floats past a double's range as Python's JSON did, written back bare by pyjson::dumps; serde_json arbitrary_precision is rejected because it would change every crate's numbers
decisions.why: This serves FR-002 (the Python's outputs). It is kept local so that no other crate's output moves (FR-002 for every other piece). Wording only: the decision says 'scoped to the door' while the approach says 'no door'. That is an inconsistency in the text, not a decision.

decisions.summary: pyjson::ascii_string escapes 0x7f as ensure_ascii does, changing log run, log bypass, escape take and the guard log for that character; the guards' entries share the shell's writer; the shared resolver (also read by clone-sync routing) takes clone-resolve.sh's real-path, dot-file, whitespace and empty-variable semantics
decisions.why: Each change moves an already-ported Rust writer or resolver toward the Python it replaced. Python's ensure_ascii escapes 0x7f: its ESCAPE_ASCII class is everything outside space to tilde. So the old core test pinned an FR-002 divergence. One writer and one resolver serve FR-003 and FR-001c's one implementation. No held case of any suite or crate moves (54 suites and 23 crates green), and live routing does not move because /diagram and the clone are not symlinks.

decisions.summary: l7r-gate takes its arguments as bytes: log guard decodes them as Python's surrogateescape did; any other subcommand given non-UTF-8 exits 101 with a message where it panicked
decisions.why: For log guard this is FR-002 fidelity to the shell's Python. For the other subcommands the exit status stays 101, and only a Rust panic's text becomes a message. That text is no output FR-002 binds (by analogy with ask:449-usage-text's traceback ruling), and no held case changes.

decisions.summary: The FR-002 proof is HEAD's shell against the new one: exit, stdout, stderr and every file written compared, normalizing an entry's utc, its file name and a bypass record's name and utc
decisions.why: Carries FR-002. The normalizations remove time values only. HEAD's guardlog.sh named entries with date -u +%Y%m%dT%H%M%S%6N (microseconds), and the new Rust writer's header gives microseconds too, so the shell's entries keep the Python's name form and only the unreproducible timestamp digits are normalized. FIGURE FINDING (not a narrowing): the block's '2,194 cases' with 'the guard log 1,167 (... 8 log-directory cases ...)' and 'the spec-kit functions 364' does not reconcile with its own run. results.json gives 2,194 = 1,166 guard-log cases (logdir 7, not 8) + 1,028 no-binary cases, and the 364 spec-kit cases are a separate run (results-speckit.json, 364/0). All differ in none, but the block's figures must be corrected: 1,166 and 7, and 2,194 stated as excluding the 364 (2,558 in all).

decisions.summary: clone-resolve.sh (one caller, guardlog.sh) and common.sh's resolve_template_content (no caller) are deleted unported; test-clone-sync-hooks.sh's one clone-resolve.sh case now checks the name through guard_log
decisions.why: FR-001 places clone-resolve.sh with guardlog.sh in phase 3, and Q12 names both files' Python. Code nothing runs is deleted rather than ported (the GM 2026-11-09). The census names its git grep and its search space (scripts/, .specify/, rust/, tests/, the Makefile, .claude/). The rerouted test case keeps its assertion and expected verdict, only its entry point moves.

decisions.summary: The inline-census-sites figure (57 recorded, 41 now) is left to the arbiter to retire or re-record; speckit.manifest.json's stale hash of common.sh is left; measure audit's load() defect on a lone \udcXX is named as not this task's
decisions.why: These are deferred or out of task, not decided in a way that narrows the request. The figure goes to the arbiter. The reader defect belongs to an already-landed port and no entry triggers it today. The manifest hash rests on an unmeasured 'nothing reads it' but decides nothing within T143's scope.

decisions.summary: guard_log costs 47 ms against 8 ms (no hook input) and 67 ms against 8 ms (with one), paid only where a guard or gate refuses or is escaped
decisions.why: This is a measurement report with a one-shot label (date and method). It decides nothing.

decisions.summary: Port the record core (17 record modules, sources.py, content.py) as the gate crate `research` with no production caller; the Python stays the implementation and is not deleted here
decisions.why: FR-003 (the Python remains the one that runs until its replacement passes; no piece runs both) and FR-002 ('before that Python is deleted') carry this without the ruling. ask:449-phase4-slices Q1 was cited but its text was not in the bundle, so the plan's paraphrase of it was not relied on. Module count and slice assignment checked against the phase-4 census (17 record/ rows plus sources.py and content.py, all slice S1).

decisions.summary: Reuse the Rust already present and fold duplicated helpers (cited-URL cleaning and url id, blocked list, html.escape, trailing-punctuation trim) into one copy; keep units::restored and the raw readers of five checks apart because they port different Python or refuse less
decisions.why: FR-003's one implementation. Keeping the near-duplicates apart is done expressly so no check's verdict moves (FR-002); that is fidelity, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: Eleven Python functions nothing calls are not ported and go with their files
decisions.why: Narrows FR-001's 'every Python file replaced' at function level, but the GM's own words (2026-11-09: 'I don't think we need to port the past feature harnesses if those are not still used') imply not porting unused code, and an uncalled function has no verdict or output FR-002 could bind. The census states its search space (git grep of each name over the whole tree, which reaches Makefiles, shell and registries holding a name as a string). The eleven are not named in the block; the ruling rests on the stated method, not on a checked list.

decisions.summary: archive_first_hooks (six entities decoded) and blocked_fetch_hooks (none) both now call the shared url_id, which decodes every entity as the Python hm_fetch.archived did
decisions.why: Changes two landed guards on live input, but toward the Python they replaced, which is FR-002's direction, and removes a duplicate (FR-003). Suites unmoved means no suite case holds the affected URL form; that is acceptable here because the change restores the Python's behavior rather than departing from it.

decisions.summary: No process cache: the Python's per-file memo, @cache readers and clear_caches left to each caller; sources::Reader holds a loaded record for its lifetime; notes as ordered pairs, sections as owned trees matched by id
decisions.why: FR-002 binds verdicts and outputs, not memoization or object identity; the replay shows no output differing on the real record. clear_caches' two recorded calls are the replay's skips, consistent with this decision. ask:449-T81-slices was cited but not supplied in the bundle.

decisions.summary: make static's dead check counts pub fn names over every .rs including tests, so the uncalled library passes it; no caller added for the check
decisions.why: An observation of an existing check; nothing is relaxed or added.

decisions.summary: Recorded-run differential over every public function: 378,360 calls, 118 functions, none differing; byte offsets compared as character offsets (the refusal still printing the character offset); a library's own words compared up to them; 336 calls inside a load covered by the load's output
decisions.why: Re-read replay.out: TOTAL 378360, 0 differing, 119 functions listed of which 118 called (clear_caches 0); split_originals 163 files same bytes. Offsets are comparison-side only; library words are ask:449-T066-json-message, inside FR-002. Two comparison details the block does not state: the replay skips 339 calls, not 336 (the other three are clear_caches' 2, covered by T144-no-cache, and one split.heading_id call with offset -1 from the driver's own sweep input bad.find('<h2'), which no caller passes), and its same_error treats any two OS-error kinds (OSError, FileNotFoundError, IsADirectoryError, NotADirectoryError) as equal without comparing their messages. Neither touches a case a test or suite holds, so FR-002 still holds; both should be stated in the record rather than left in the harness.

decisions.summary: A KeyError's message compared with its quotes stripped
decisions.why: This is a case changed in comparison, which FR-001c names. Legitimate for this slice only: the library has no caller, so no bound output moves, and a KeyError the Python left uncaught is a traceback FR-002 does not bind. The plan does not say whether any Python caller prints str(e) of these KeyErrors; where one does, that caller's wiring slice (S5, S11 or S12) must reproduce the quotes, and this ruling does not release it.

decisions.summary: host neither drops tabs nor applies urlsplit's NFKC check
decisions.why: Ruled apart from NaN. A known departure from the Python, legitimate for the unwired library only: no production caller exists (FR-003), and FR-002 binds the cases tests and suites hold, which none of these is. 'No real case reaches' was measured against the record's cited and attempted URLs, not against the live fetch URLs the blocked-fetch guard reads, and this host sits beside the blocked-domain list. S5, which wires blocked.py, owes its own decision on closing the divergence or ruling on it, and this ruling does not decide that.

decisions.summary: JSON NaN, which Python's json accepts, is not accepted

decisions.summary: The eight tools are ported, wired to every make, Rust and suite caller, and five are deleted. bundle_door's run/passages/save_cached verbs, owed_door's mb and record_door's americanize_json/moved_only retire with their callers.

The earlier rulings already put the switch at this cut: T80-order ('Rust downloads running reserve-prefix.py by path until T81 lands'), T81-slices (quote_verbatim's Rust callers 'by command until then'), T88-bundles ('each verb leaves the runner when its owner ports'), and T81-hm-record / T87 (a door is deleted with its last caller). FR-003's one writer is kept by bullet 3.

decisions.summary: sources.py, attempts.py and reserve-prefix.py become thin forwarders to the Rust writers. Their command lines, ledger writers, seed, import_saves, CachedPages and key cap are removed. attempts.write refuses the attempts log. Each shared file gets one named writer, and 'escape take' retires.
decisions.why: This is FR-003 and ask:449-T86-door applied as written (a name a command can carry goes by command). The refusal in attempts.write only enforces the one-writer rule. No importer passes it the attempts log (the importers' calls were read). The uncited lists keep the Python as their one writer.

decisions.summary: A CPython HTML parser port, decoder and case-fold tables generated from CPython, unicode-normalization pinned to match Python 3.14.4's NFKC, and curl as an external transport. ParseCache is not carried. An edit to the kept Python makes the same change in the Rust.

decisions.why: Both restore FR-002 parity with the Python that existed before the port. Neither changes an expected verdict away from the Python.

decisions.summary: FR-002 difference: reserve on a source-tags.json that is not JSON quotes the Rust parser's words inside the Python's fixed message.
decisions.why: This is exactly ask:449-T066-json-message's class. The harness record shows exit 2 on both sides and 'reserve: source-tags.json: not JSON (' ... ')' identical, with only serde's text inside the parentheses differing.

decisions.summary: FR-002 difference: make apply-edits with a missing reply has the same exit and exception kind (FileNotFoundError), and only its message text differs.
decisions.why: In the Python this was an uncaught exception. ask:449-usage-text says an uncaught traceback's text is not bound for any port, while exit status and stdout stay held, and the block holds both.

decisions.summary: Normalization (216 cases): the text inside '<urlopen error ...>' is curl's where Python gave its errno text. Exit, stderr frame, JSON report and the UNFETCHABLE verdict are the same.
decisions.why: T066-json-message binds verdict, exit status, location and fixed words, and lets through a library's own error text quoted inside a fixed message. curl is the transport in the role the Python's socket library had. The harness regex replaces only the text after '<urlopen error ', and the dead-host run done raw on both sides showed everything else equal, so no output the tool writes itself is hidden.

decisions.summary: Normalization: argparse's exit-2 text and an uncaught traceback's text are compared by refusal and by exception kind.
decisions.why: This is ask:449-usage-text. The harness's exit-2 rule is broader than the ruling, since it would also collapse a hand-written parser.error(). I checked HEAD's eight files in the harness's ref copy: none calls parser.error or exits 2 by hand, and their hand-written stderr lines start with the tool's name, which neither branch of the normalizer collapses. So it hides only unbound text.

decisions.summary: The key-cap escape's guard-log 'command' field names 'l7r-gate record reserve' where it named reserve-prefix.py.
decisions.why: The Python wrote the field as ' '.join(sys.argv), its own invocation (reserve-prefix.py:59 in the harness's HEAD copy). The Rust records its own invocation by the same definition, so the field's meaning is unchanged. T135-generator's condition holds for the code that writes the entry, since the key cap is removed from the Python in this cut. Keeping 'reserve-prefix.py' would name a process that no longer writes the entry.

decisions.summary: Timestamps and the guard-log entry's file name (UTC-microsecond plus pid) are normalized.

decisions.summary: Timings are recorded and not held. quote-verbatim is faster, while the prepass/style sweeps (230 s vs 337 s) and the archive sweep (41 s vs 88 s) are slower.
decisions.why: The spec binds timing per phase (FR-010, SC-001..003), not per port, and FR-002 binds outputs. Recording the figures does not narrow a requirement.

decisions.summary: No measurements.json command runs the eight. 375's two one-shot rows that name three of them as timing keys keep their values as that day's record.

decisions.summary: This slice wires the Rust into production callers (Makefile archive recipes, record::reserve in process, depiction.rs's crop, tree's stamp, Python writes forwarded) rather than landing a library with no production caller
decisions.why: ask:449-phase4-slices' default slice shape (library, Python staying the implementation) yields here to the more specific ask:449-T80-order (4), which phase4-slices itself invokes for S3a's order and which moves the Chromium install off the Python package in the same cut, with T145's precedent under ask:449-T88-bundles. It ports more, not less, of what the GM asked ('all be ported to Rust'), and the purpose of the slice shape, one wired implementation (FR-003, FR-001c), holds: each file has one live writer, the Rust, with the 13 importer cases in the differential. Nothing the request or spec asked for is narrowed.

The salt keeps cache keys correct.

decisions.summary: The plain GET runs curl, sharing the page context's cookies as Playwright's request context did
decisions.why: Implementation of the port, T145's fetch precedent; the 109-case differential (cookies, redirects, PDFs, binary, 404s) holds the outputs (FR-002).

decisions.summary: Node's words kept for the failures the Python's reports name (refused, not found, timeout, redirect cap); other fetch failures carry curl's own error text
decisions.why: An FR-002 output not held byte for byte, so narrowing. ask:449-T066-json-message is a general ruled case - where a message quotes a library's own error text inside a fixed message, verdict, exit, location and fixed words match and the quoted text is the replacement's - with the spec lint as its instance, not its limit. The plan holds more than the ruling requires (the named failures keep Node's words) and lets only the quoted library text of unnamed failures change. curl is a program rather than a Rust library, but the ruling's purpose - a port cannot reproduce another fetch library's own error strings - applies unchanged. No case in the 109 surfaced such a difference.

decisions.summary: The archive's working copy and manifest rows written by the Rust alone; archive.py's ensure, push, place_gm, archive_url, _lane, settle, sync_gm_copies, write_row, Browser, fetch and wayback forward to door verbs; reads, the lock and Archive's git reads stay Python; a Rust verb run by a Python caller under that lock takes no lock itself
decisions.why: FR-003 and ask:449-T86-door (one implementation writing each file, door verbs, no logic in the door); ask:449-T81-slices allows the reads to stay half-ported. Not re-taking the caller's lock prevents self-deadlock without opening a second writer.

decisions.summary: One seam (Reach, cli_with) replaces store, browser and credential in the crates' tests; one kept end-to-end case in tests/hooks/test-l7r-gate.sh drives record archive url, backfill and gm-copies through the real launcher on the pinned Chromium, a local bare remote, empty secrets and a dead proxy
decisions.why: ask:449-T80-order (4): 'behind one seam, one end-to-end test'; FR-008 exempts the one end-to-end test from the tenth-of-a-second bar; ask:449-T146-browser's 'its one end-to-end test'.

decisions.summary: The production wiring that hands in the real store, browser and credential (cli, production_store, start_browser, token, Process::start) is #[cfg(not(test))], so it is outside the unit-test coverage instrument and reached only by the end-to-end case
decisions.why: FR-004 read strictly asks every line reached by a test; these lines leave the unit-test instrument's denominator, so narrowing. Legitimate on the spec's own words: ask:449-T80-order (4) and ask:449-T146-browser put the browser behind one seam with one end-to-end test, its lines owing FR-004 'with its one end-to-end test', and FR-008 bars any other test from starting the real browser and process. The ruling holds only while the excluded set is the named hand-in of real store, browser, credential and process (cli, production_store, start_browser, token, Process::start); any logic behind cfg(not(test)) beyond that is not covered. Evidence gap: the block's label for 'executes every line of those blocks' (run, and run with no Chromium) shows the case depends on Chromium, not line reach, so line reach is asserted rather than shown.

decisions.summary: make archive-find, dead on AttributeError since T145 cut attempts.report, restored by a forwarder
decisions.why: Restores behavior FR-002 bound T145 to keep; the forwarder reaches the Rust, so FR-003's one implementation holds.

decisions.summary: The Rust archive-sources deadlock (stdout lock held while lanes printed) fixed
