decisions.summary: Kuwabata's glyph-check declared under Occasions and deferred while the port switch stands at rust-only
decisions.why: Feature 444 FR-023 (GM-approved amendment 8/10) states a glyph-check the review gate owes for a pool hamlet a Rust stage moves is not owed while the switch stands, owed when it is thrown back; declaring it keeps it owed rather than dropped.

decisions.summary: Found and left: the reed strip covering the dike's corners and sluice cuts filed as T236, and reviews-owed owing no review for an undeclared Rust drawing change filed as T237, both landing before T158
decisions.why: Both defects are filed as their own tasks and land before the next step (T158), which is what the GM's 2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on' asks; neither is carried into the next step.

decisions.summary: The page's sluice name not drawn, since the hamlet maps draw no element captions
decisions.why: A difference from the page's own drawing, not a wrong outcome: no map reads wrong and no research finding is contradicted (constitution XIV v2.36.0, the GM 2026-11-19); no defect is left.

decisions.summary: Ordered after T226 and before T158; exits, budget of one gated landing, and done measured as Kuwabata's two sluices drawn as frames across their channels
decisions.why: Sequencing and exits inside the feature's process; the done measure is the fix's own goal.

decisions.summary: reviews owed compares the Rust engines' drawing code item by item, base against now; an item whose comment-free tokens differ is changed and owes the glyph-check of each element it redraws, on the first map of its engine's kind that draws it, merged with the declared route's unit
decisions.why: This fixes the defect T234 found: a redrawn glyph shipped without a judgment unless someone declared it, a check passing bad work (constitution XIV; the GM 2026-11-18: 'fix all known bugs in each step'). The declared route is kept and the two routes share a slug.

decisions.summary: a detected drawing change owes the glyph-check only, with no size-audit
decisions.why: The block cites docs/reviews.md as owing a glyph-check when an element's glyph is redrawn. That text is not in the bundle, so this ruling rests on the block's own quote of the rule. Nothing in 449's request or spec index asks for a size-audit on this occasion.

decisions.summary: draw functions in the hamlet driver are read by line (the last svg.kind above each changed line); Mode A marks are read whole, with their callees' kinds; writer methods, helpers and constants owe what their uses redraw (a free function's call is never a method's of the same name); a roll is read line by line; a type, import or test owes nothing
decisions.why: This is the mechanism for 'owes the glyph-check of each element it redraws'. On T234's commit it owes the sluice gate alone, and 48 of the 55 non-drawing functions owe nothing (dated one-shot labels). It is a design choice inside the fix.

decisions.summary: where the elements cannot be told (a kind chosen at run time, a line above a draw function's first kind, a mark past a draw call), each engine map's whole legend is owed, and the occasion says so
decisions.why: This owes more checks than the change redraws, never fewer, so no bad work passes.

decisions.summary: a map's legend is read from its drawing now, else from its drawing at the base
decisions.why: The unit still stands when the change left a hamlet not current. This keeps the fix from missing a case.

decisions.summary: the drawing code is the hamlet driver (rust/phases/src/driver.rs, driver/) and the Mode A compound engine (compound.rs, emit.rs, emit_parts.rs); hand sheets stay under CODE
decisions.why: This is measured (a grep of the writer and kind calls over rust/, dated). The stages outside the driver name no kind and touch no writer, so this list is the set of Rust code that redraws a glyph.

decisions.summary: an element drawn by several maps is judged on the first map that draws it, which may not be the map the change touched
decisions.why: This is the declared route's existing choice. The glyph-check judges the element's glyph, which is the same on every map that draws it. Today the one such case (the polder's ditches) is not told and falls to the whole legend.

decisions.summary: a Rust stage's placement change (rust/phases/src outside the driver) owes nothing and is not refused undeclared, where a Python one is refused under CODE; not filed by this task
decisions.why: Today this produces no wrong outcome. FR-023 (spec-cited.md): 'a settlement-review FR-019 owes, or a glyph-check the review gate owes, for a pool hamlet a Rust stage moves, is not owed while the switch stands - each is owed, for every pool hamlet the port moved, when it is thrown back.' The Rust stages draw the live (pool) hamlets, so while the switch stands at rust-only no review is owed for such a change, and failing to detect one passes nothing bad. The gap is live from the moment the switch is thrown back, so it has to be filed before then.

decisions.summary: the declared route resolves its map from the drawings now only, so with a hamlet not current it owes a unit on no map, with a problem line; left as is
decisions.why: This is a behavior of the existing declared route. The review gate redraws before it reads the route, so the case produces no wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: Mode A marks are read whole, so a one-line change to parts owes all ten kinds that parts and well tag
decisions.why: This owes more checks than the change redraws, never fewer. It is a cost and not a wrong outcome, so it is not a defect.

decisions.summary: a file that was only moved owes what its items redraw, where CODE's refusal sets a moved file aside
decisions.why: This errs toward owing a check. It narrows nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: edits docs/reviews.md and rust/gate/CLAUDE.md to say what is owed
decisions.why: This documents the behavior the fix enforces.

decisions.summary: the rust-only set-aside of the detected hamlet units is read from the gate's rule (pool find on the slug's last part), not run
decisions.why: This is a verification choice, not a narrowing. The detected units carry the declared route's slug form, which ends in the hamlet, so FR-023's set-aside reaches them by the same rule. The block's runs exercise the lookup only, never the gate's set-aside on a hamlet unit that has no declared line.

decisions.summary: the item reader repeats the claims crate's item_end rather than sharing it, because claims builds on this crate
decisions.why: An internal design choice that touches nothing that was asked.

decisions.summary: The strip is laid from the dike's outer face itself (its corners nearest the flank, in axis order, carried round the corner to the box's corner); the notch step-in, the 32 bins, BINS and STRIP_CUT_HW go.
decisions.why: Fixes a defect (reeds drawn on the dike and over its corners, a wrong outcome against pages 0019/0027) found by T234; fix-as-we-go within the step is what the GM asked (2026-11-18). The corner meeting at the diagonal is labeled GUESS where no page speaks.

decisions.summary: Each straight reach of the feeder and outfall has its bed (drawn width, carried half a width past each end) taken out of the strip along its own four sides by a Weiler-Atherton difference, replacing the axis-boxed cut.
decisions.why: Fixes the defect of reeds over the channels the sluices shut and the bare ground beside slanting banks (0074: reeds to the water's edge and out of the water); a defect fix, not a difference-from-expected.

decisions.summary: A bed reaching an end of the strip's span ends the run past the dike's end square across at its nearest point; a piece wholly past the dike's extent (cut off by a channel past a corner) is dropped, leaving the outfall's west bank past Kuwabata's south-west corner bare.
decisions.why: No page places reeds on a channel's far bank past the dike's corner (labeled GUESS at the unit); past the flank's own extent the strip is the run-past, so a bare far bank there contradicts no research finding and is not a wrong outcome.

decisions.summary: Part 2: roll_polder's choice of the field outline as the seat's ring, its lines, pond and strip ordering get a claim (0019, 0081, and GUESSes recording cost); no code change.
decisions.why: Answers the impl-drift finding on T234 by claiming the existing decision; claims are the project's standing rule (FR-021 unchanged) and add no behavior.

decisions.summary: The settlement's reserved ground drawn over Kuwabata's north dike and head canal is a seat placement change filed as T239, landing before T158, the step's close.
decisions.why: A known defect, but fixed within the same step before the next step's port begins, which is what the GM's 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on' asks; it is a placement change of a different stage, not this task's mechanism.

decisions.summary: The marsh glyph-check on Kuwabata is declared under 449's Occasions, named by reviews owed, set aside at rust-only and recorded under feature 444 FR-023; its undetected-without-declaration gap is T238, before T158.
decisions.why: FR-023 (accepted, GM amendment 8) states a glyph-check for a pool hamlet a Rust stage moves is not owed while the switch stands rust-only; the detection gap is a tooling defect fixed within the step (T238 before T158).

decisions.summary: A reach starting inside a strip with no earlier bed from the dike, and a fold at a corner zigzagging the face, are left; no map draws either.
decisions.why: Neither is a wrong outcome on any map (every sluice channel reaches the strip from the dike; no fold on Kuwabata or R); under constitution XIV v2.36.0 a case no map draws is not a defect owed.

decisions.summary: waterward.polder's counted work rises to 3,929 and 5,501 (about 0.14 and 0.15 of budget, exponent 0.49 against 0.464 + 0.05 allowance); the ratchet refusal is routed through a MODE AUDIT and budget-accept by the caller.
decisions.why: Arithmetic re-derived: 3929/27296=0.144, 5501/37653=0.146, log2(5501/3929)=0.486; within the derived budget and its allowance, and the work budgets (FR-022) are kept, not bypassed; whether a re-accept needs the GM's words is left open to the gate, not waived.

decisions.summary: roll_polder hands the seat a ring off the dike's outer face (each side pushed straight out to the outer face at its widest on that side, corners re-met) where it handed the plots' edge
decisions.why: Fixes a defect in the sense the GM set (2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs in each step', 2026-11-19 what a defect is): the settlement's ground drawn over the dike and head canal contradicts page 0019's village on dry ground off the dike, a wrong outcome a reader sees. Holding each side straight at the dike's widest is a labeled GUESS that keeps the ground off the dike everywhere; it narrows nothing asked.

decisions.summary: T236's proposal (hand the outer face itself, 82-89 candidates against 2) priced and not taken
decisions.why: A design choice between two ways to the same outcome; T236's proposal is a session finding, not the GM's request, and the chosen ring reaches 0 ft2 over the dike and canal on all five polders measured. Cost and design are not fidelity findings.

decisions.summary: roll_polder's and off_the_dike's comments restate the claim to page 0019
decisions.why: Keeps the research claim matching the corrected behavior (FR-002: the research claims a piece carries hold).

decisions.summary: No settlement-review or glyph-check owed: only the driver's placeholder ground ('-', no registry element) and its label move on Kuwabata, ink census unchanged; declared as a none: line under Occasions
decisions.why: FR-023 (feature 444) already suspends a settlement-review or glyph-check for a pool hamlet a Rust stage moves while the switch stands at rust-only; the block's own reason (no unit can name '-') reaches the same result. Nothing asked is narrowed.

decisions.summary: Exits (red-first test, make quick/static/counters-inert, 48-seed cohort per polder form) and budget (seat.polder rises 1,682/2,089 to 2,185/2,875; the stage has no accepted budget)
decisions.why: Verification of the requested fix and the work-budget record FR-022 keeps; the cohort is run voluntarily though FR-023 does not require it. No case excluded.

decisions.summary: Found and left: polder_checks asks only whether the seat's middle is inside the plots' edge, so it passes ground over the dike; a check against the outer face not written here
decisions.why: This is a defect (a check that passes bad work), so leaving it in T239 narrows 'fix all known bugs in each step'. But the GM's rule is per step ('before moving on to porting the next step'), and the dispatch states it is carried by filed task T240 before T158, the next step's port; deferral within the step to a filed task keeps the rule's purpose. Legitimate only so long as T240 lands before T158.

decisions.summary: Found and left: a malformed Occasions declaration '- placement-changed: - on kuwabata' is read as a unit glyph-check-- with no map rather than refused
decisions.why: A tool answering wrongly is a defect; it is outside this task's subject (the seat's ring) and is carried by filed task T238 before T158, which satisfies the GM's per-step rule. Legitimate on that filing.

decisions.summary: Found and left: 0019 draws the village on the landward (east) shore; the seat picks its side by wind and fall (north on Kuwabata) and nothing ties it to a shore
decisions.why: Whether the village stands on the landward side is a research-claim question (a possible defect, not a mere difference from the page's drawn orientation; 'east' itself is not owed). Left here and carried by filed task T240 before T158, inside the step, which is what the GM's 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on' asks. Legitimate on that filing; if T240 finds the side reads fine and matches 0019's claim it closes by restating the claim, per the GM's 2026-11-19 rule.

decisions.summary: A .rs under rust/phases/src/ or rust/mode_a/src/compound/ (no drawing or test file; 45 files, now carrying its find) whose non-test items' comment-free tokens changed, and a drawing file's change that redraws no element, refuse undeclared; a change that redraws owes its glyph-check from the change
decisions.why: Restores for the Rust placers the refusal the deleted Python's CODE pattern held (FR-002: a ported check must still do its job); T237 found the Rust stages refused nothing, a check passing the bad. Fixed as found per the GM 2026-11-18 ('fix all known bugs in each step'). The count now names its search space (find, less the tests, drawing files and driver), as asked last round.

decisions.id: D2 comments, tests, imports, types, moves do not refuse
decisions.summary: Narrower than the old file-level pattern; a type alone is no placement (the first version refused T234's SluiceFrame)
decisions.why: FR-002's exception: a check refusing correct work is fixed in its port. A comment-only or type-only change re-places nothing, and refusing T234's type was measured as refusing correct work. No known instance of a type alone moving an element; a difference with no wrong outcome is no defect (XIV, T196).

decisions.id: D3 a tasks.md declaration naming nothing, or no known occasion, refused with its form
decisions.summary: Refused by --check-declared whatever code the delta touches; the check reads no legend
decisions.why: Fixes a found defect (T239: a declaration naming no element became a unit on no map). Unknown kinds are the same defect. GM 2026-11-18, fix as we go.

decisions.id: D4 a tweak's misformed Occasion: commit line is a problem line, never refused
decisions.summary: Owes no unit and is never refused, since a pushed commit message cannot be rewritten (also for --check-drawn's undrawn element)
decisions.why: No defect is left: a misformed commit line owes no unrunnable unit and answers no undeclared code (D7), and the one form --check-declared cannot see before the redraw, an element its map's current drawing does not hold, answers nothing at --check-drawn (D9c), so the delta's code is refused while the line itself, which cannot be rewritten, is not.

decisions.id: D5 only the started task's own line answers
decisions.summary: An active feature's Occasions line answers only when it owns the started task (.git/active-task), not ticked at the base, in one of three owning forms; a mention answers nothing; wrapped lines joined
decisions.why: Fixes the round-1 defect measured on T236's delta (other tasks' and features' sections passed undeclared placement code). Every existing task-naming line still answers its own task. GM 2026-11-18, fix as we go.

decisions.id: D6 a line already on main still answers its unticked task
decisions.summary: A declaration pushed with the spec, before the code, names the task all the same
decisions.why: The declaration's unit is the task (docs/reviews.md); a stale line is excluded by the tick test. Nothing asked for a per-push declaration.

decisions.id: D7 a misformed commit line answers no undeclared code
decisions.summary: Only a commit Occasion: line that owes a runnable review answers the delta
decisions.why: Fixes a found defect (Occasion: bogus: x answered undeclared code), red first. GM 2026-11-18, fix as we go.

decisions.id: D8 a map or sheet the pool does not hold refused with its form, closest names offered
decisions.summary: Every kind with a map or sheet slot; the pool walk runs only when an unlanded line names a map; a commit line so formed is a problem line owing no unit
decisions.why: Fixes a found defect (well on nowhere became a unit on no map); each slotted kind is the same defect. GM 2026-11-18, fix as we go.

decisions.id: D9 an element the named map's current drawing does not hold refused after the redraw (--check-drawn)
decisions.summary: review-gate.sh asks reviews owed --check-drawn right after redrawing maps not current and before --landing; a tasks.md glyph line whose element the named map's legend (current drawing only) does not hold is refused with its form and closest drawn kinds; with no map named, refused once every live legend is known and none holds it; such a line owes no unit
decisions.why: Option (a) of the first round's NOT LEGITIMATE ruling, built for tasks.md lines, red first (a_declared_element_its_current_drawing_does_not_hold_is_refused, review-gate r12): fixes a found defect (a declared line shipping a unit on no map) as we go (GM 2026-11-18). A stale engine's drawing is not current (the currency question reads an engine older than its sources as no engine) and falls to D9r; make map rebuilds the hamlet driver from the tree's sources (measured in a scratch clone), and a_drawing_by_an_older_engine_refuses_no_declared_new_element pins that a correctly declared new element is not refused. Item 4's scratch run's prebuilt engine is now reconciled by reading: review-gate.sh redraws by the same make map launcher that builds (Launcher build: true), the prebuilt binary a scratch set-up artifact of timestamps; stated as read, not measured end to end. That claim reads the unit from the code's change and needs no element from the drawing, so nothing in this decision turns on it.

decisions.id: D9r residual: a map whose redraw failed keeps the old behavior
decisions.summary: A map still not current after the redraw (a failed draw at rust-only, or a drawing by an engine older than its sources), or an unmapped element while any live legend is unknown, is left a unit on no map plus a problem line, not refused; a commit line on such a map still answers
decisions.why: Physically impossible to decide, not merely awkward: with no current drawing there is nothing to tell a misnamed element from one new to the map, so a refusal there would refuse correct work (a check refusing good work is itself a defect, XIV T196 and FR-002's exception). Option (b) of last round's ruling is met for this residual: no current drawing exists at any point the gate could refuse. The two cases (named map not current; no map named while some live legend is unknown) are adjudicated separately and each fails on the same ground: the drawing that would decide does not exist. The same ground covers a commit line on a not-current map answering at --check-drawn (D9c): no drawing exists that could tell its element wrong from new.

decisions.id: D9c a commit line naming an element its map's current drawing does not hold answers nothing at --check-drawn
decisions.summary: At --check-drawn a well-formed commit Occasion: line answers the delta only if it is no glyph line, its map is not current, or its current drawing holds the element (answers_drawn); placement code only such lines answered is refused there as undeclared; the line itself is never refused; D9r unchanged - the mapped case only; see D9c-nomap
decisions.why: Last round's NOT LEGITIMATE ruling met by the option it named: an undrawn-element commit line answers no undeclared code at --check-drawn, red first (1 of 161 crate tests and review-gate r13, 2 of 111, failing before answers_drawn), so placement code with only a commit line naming an element its named map does not draw no longer ships unreviewed - the check-passing-the-bad defect is fixed in this step (GM 2026-11-18). Refusing the code, not the line, keeps D7's reason: a later commit can carry a line that answers. The not-current case it leaves is D9r's residual, ruled LEGITIMATE.

decisions.id: D9c-nomap a commit glyph line naming no map, whose element no current drawing holds
decisions.summary: At --check-drawn a no-map commit glyph line is decided as the tasks.md side decides one (undrawn for both): it answers nothing once every live legend is known and none holds the element, answers when some legend holds it, and while any live legend is unknown it is D9r and answers; pinned by a_commit_line_naming_no_map_is_decided_by_every_legend (a pin, green on the D9c code as written, said so) and in the D9c table row
decisions.why: Last round's NOT LEGITIMATE ruling met exactly as it asked: the rule is now stated for the no-map case in all three branches, and the pin is named and labeled as a pin rather than red-first. Placement code answered only by a no-map commit line naming an element no current legend holds is refused at --check-drawn, so the check-passing-the-bad sibling of D9c is closed in this step (GM 2026-11-18, fix all known bugs in each step). The residual while a legend is unknown is D9r's, already ruled LEGITIMATE on the same ground (no drawing exists to tell a wrong name from a new element).

decisions.id: D10 a two-task landing answered by the started task's line
decisions.summary: Another task's placement code in the same landing rides on the started task's declaration; no known instance (T236's --stat, its 451 T26 files no placement code); not filed
decisions.why: The refusal's per-delta grain, as the old pattern had; the started task's line is written by the session landing the whole delta. Nothing asks per-task attribution inside a landing. Now worded as no known instance, with its method, as asked.

decisions.id: D11 docs/guards.md's stale review-gate row left
decisions.summary: Names the deleted review_owed.py, not placed.rs; outside this task's files; rust/gate/CLAUDE.md and review-gate.sh's comment updated
decisions.why: A stale documentation row is no wrong outcome under XIV (T196): no map reads wrong, no check passes the bad or refuses the good, no tool fails.

decisions.id: D12 Mode A caption placers not stage code
decisions.summary: caption_place.rs and place.rs place captions, no element
decisions.why: docs/reviews.md's occasion is the re-placement of an element; captions are no census element, so nothing the occasion covers is narrowed.

decisions.id: D13 detected hamlet units set aside at rust-only and recorded
decisions.summary: The scratch gate run sets glyph-check--field-grave--inashiro aside into dev/deferred-reviews.jsonl
decisions.why: Settled by feature 444 FR-023, cited in full: a glyph-check owed for a pool hamlet a Rust stage moves is not owed while the switch stands, and is owed when it is thrown back.

decisions.id: D14 sheet placeholder marks are no element
decisions.summary: sheet_kinds leaves out data-kind '-' and the compound's title, as ink_classes does
decisions.why: Fixes a found defect (a sheet with an unreadable base drawing owed glyph-check----county-magistracy-example), red first. GM 2026-11-18, fix as we go.

decisions.id: D15 --check-declared slower after round 2; --check-drawn adds 56-59 ms
decisions.summary: The cost is the delta's code read that 449's section had let the check skip, and the new legend check after the redraw
decisions.why: The old speed came from the defect; no timing target in the request or spec reaches these checks, and restoring a check's job is FR-002's requirement. Each figure carries a dated method label.

decisions.id: T242-1 recorders write in the house style
decisions.summary: Every recorder that writes a reviewer's words into the repository applies the house-style correction the push's delta check enforces, so a recorded verdict never turns make quick red or refuses a landing.
decisions.why: A defect by constitution XIV's definition: a tool writes what its own check refuses and blocks landings, observed three times on 2026-11-20. The GM 2026-11-18: 'we want to use this port to fix broken things as we find them ... fix all known bugs in each step'. Nothing a map reader sees changes.

decisions.id: T242-2 the decision id styled too
decisions.summary: plan-verdict styles each decision's id and nested lists, not only its free text; the id was earlier kept as given.
decisions.why: The plan states, from an observed grep over rust/ and scripts/, that nothing compares an id (status.rs names it, the arbiter bundle prints it, plan_rounds reads blocks alone), so styling it changes no caller's behavior (FR-002: a caller still finds what it reads). The id was the incident's own carrier.

decisions.summary: New guard functions hold only what the delta check holds in a non-prose file (code spans, corner brackets, curly quotes, q, blockquote), not straight quotes, and walk every JSON string, keys as written.
decisions.why: Matches the correction to the check it must satisfy; the measured scratch run (2 findings: plain and straight-quoted word) shows straight quotes are not held in JSON. Keys are schema names, not prose. Quotations the record can hold keep their words, per CLAUDE.md's quotation rule.

decisions.summary: The same correction applied to arbiter-ruled, claims-checked, gm-escalated, gm_review::question, record-checked's found.jsonl, and the ledger row from ledger-owed WRITE (americanize, Markdown, before the 110-character cut).
decisions.why: The same defect in each, measured, not assumed: 7 assertions failing across 5 crates before the change. Fixing a known defect class where it was found is what the GM asked for on 2026-11-18. The tests are enforcement, not unrequested scope.

decisions.id: T242-5 names and the GM's words left as written
decisions.summary: found.jsonl's file and block fields kept as given (they name things); the GM's own words (WORDS=, GM_WORDS) never styled.
decisions.why: Neither narrows anything the GM asked for. A name is not prose, and restyling it would break what it names. The house style itself stops at quotations (CLAUDE.md), and FR-002 keeps a verbatim quotation exact.

decisions.summary: Before T158, after T238 and T241; red-first tests, the changed crates' rust-test, quick, static and hooks-test green; one gated landing.
decisions.why: Sequencing and verification of the fix only; it narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A parked arm in phase_source_hooks (matcher widened to Write|Edit|MultiEdit, run before the read hold's early returns) refuses a Write/Edit/MultiEdit or a shell write (mv, cp, rsync, redirect, sed -i, git mv's destination) landing a parked stage in rust/phases/src/<stage>, or a new `mod <stage>` in rust/phases/src/lib.rs, unless the stage is resumed.
decisions.why: Enforces 'then don't actually proceed ... before you get started on that': the guard's only reach is the parked stages' source and their lib.rs declaration, so with the requested stop deleted it has nothing left to check. Enforcement of the request, not unrequested scope.

decisions.summary: make task-start refuses a parked stage's task (parked_stage) before the performance-first check and before any file is written, telling the session to stop rather than to use PERF_LATER_OK.
decisions.why: The same stop at the task's start door; ordering it before FR-013's check only makes the refusal say 'stop' instead of offering an unrelated escape. It does not change FR-013 for any non-parked task.

decisions.summary: The one escape is GM_RESUMED="<the GM's words>", recorded (guard log parked-stage, parked-resumed.jsonl), and held on a move or a task-start to words of a message the GM wrote this session; a heredoc or quoted argument naming it is no escape.
decisions.why: The GM said 'we can talk more ... before you get started on that': resumption belongs to the GM after the talk. Requiring his own words and refusing a session's own is exactly that; it widens nothing.

decisions.summary: The set-down pickers and fallback skip a held stage's task; with only those open the Stop refusal names the ruling and make set-down, and set_down's parked_stop takes that set-down with no arbiter ruling and under the usage cap, its row carrying the ruling.

Letting the stop happen is the request itself; the bypass of the arbiter ruling and the cap is confined to the case where only parked stages remain, so it reaches nothing the GM did not ask for.

decisions.summary: a rule's multiple ('past 2x', 'more than 2x', 'the 2x rule', 'the 2x raise') is a limit, not a figure
decisions.why: Parity with the lint's existing treatment of thresholds, which the block keeps for the word forms too ('at most ten keys' stays a limit, as the numeral threshold already does); a limit or rule parameter is a stated bound, not a measurement. The change only widens the check (before it, every multiple passed), and the reviewer stays the backstop for a measured multiple placed after a limit word (feature 239 FR-013), so no part of the approved T159 check's reach is narrowed.

decisions.summary: a spaced '2 x 3' is arithmetic or a size, not a multiple
decisions.why: A dimension or product is not a ratio figure; a unit-bearing size is still read by the existing unit rule. No measured multiple of the two forms that motivated the task (written close) is excluded.

decisions.summary: the word 'one' is not read as a count
decisions.why: 'one' is overwhelmingly a determiner or name in prose ('one landing', 'one crate'); the numeral '1' stays counted as before, so the exclusion keeps the word rule on figures without removing any reach the check had.

decisions.summary: a threshold's word ('at most ten keys') stays a limit
decisions.why: Same parity as the numeral thresholds the count rule already exempts; a bound is not a measurement.

decisions.summary: a count spelled as a word (two..twenty, the tens, hundred(s), thousand(s), dozen(s); never 'one') is read by the count rule where a counted noun follows, as a numeral is; count nouns gain 'captions'; a threshold's word stays a limit; the refusals' wording names both forms
decisions.why: Closes the second gap (T209's 'moved five captions a few pixels' reached review unlabeled). Extending the existing numeral count rule to the same count in words is enforcement of the T159 check; excluding 'one' (a determiner/naming word, while the numeral form stays counted) and thresholds keeps the rule on figures.

decisions.summary: item 4's any-number rule does not take spelled words (on the replay they added 45 findings, nearly all naming: 'the three checks')

decisions.summary: T258: the check-bundle guard reads the task a check serves (its description, else its prompt's first line; its dispatching builder's brief, every bundle member; its page session's brief) and asks the three-argument `plan decided <root> <feature> <task>`, never the clone's active-task mark first.
decisions.why: Feature 375 FR-003(a) holds a check until 'the decisions of the task they belong to' carry a verdict; judging it on whichever task started last (measured: 32 of 113 refused on another builder's section) is the defect, and reading the check's own task restores the requirement. A tool answering wrongly is a defect (XIV), fixed as we go (GM 2026-11-18).

decisions.summary: T258: a task with no plan section passes (owes no decision), where the one-argument form fell back to the plan-stage `owed` reading.
decisions.why: FR-003(a) reads 'else the plan's own plan-stage verdict'. In a per-block plan (375 amendment 11) that fallback is 'no block owed', which makes one task's check wait on any other builder's undecided section, the exact measured defect T258 fixes; the literal fallback defeats the requirement's purpose, which is that a check waits on its OWN task's decisions. It is also implied by the GM's FR-001c, under which straight port tasks carry no plan review and so no section. A task with a section still waits on that section's verdict.

decisions.summary: T258: a section with an unfiled found-and-left deferral refuses the check too.
decisions.why: Stricter, not narrower: a section `make decide` already refuses is not decided, so FR-003(a) holds its checks.

decisions.summary: T258 (round 2 change): a check naming no task falls back to the mark's one-argument answer and, where that refuses, is refused told to name its task; it never passes unjudged.
decisions.why: Round 1's finding (a no-task check passed silently) is answered: the check is still judged by decide-first, on the clone's own record of its active task, the only evidence left when the check names nothing, and the refusal steers its dispatcher to be judged on its own section thereafter. No case is passed that the pre-T258 guard refused.

decisions.summary: T258: every refusal keeps 'decide first, then check (feature 375 FR-003a)'; test-checks-hooks.sh's four dispatches name their task.
decisions.why: Keeps the suites' reading of the rule; the fixtures name their task so they exercise the new per-task reading. Enforcement of FR-003(a).

decisions.summary: Row 141's contradiction (0031's drawing page says every hamlet backs the wind; the Rust seat backs Sawada's declared fall-into-the-wind cluster to the hill) is resolved by correcting the record: 0031's 'on every map' narrowed to the rolled falls, the declared case recorded (high dry margin, back to the hill as a labeled GUESS with its absence note, houses still south-facing by 0029 with Sakamoto-Tsubaki p.114), the seat claim restated to the page's words.
decisions.why: This is the GM's rule word for word (2026-11-19, constitution XIV, T196). Where the code doesn't literally match a research claim but behaves fine, the claim is restated and the code is left alone. The 2026-11-17/18 exactness amendments say a map that differs from the Python's is fine if it holds its research. A search pass ran before the guess was called one, and on the declared case the record is silent (one survey, no page on a cluster's back when hill and wind lie opposite), so the easier route is taken and labeled under XII. The wind rule being narrowed was a project decision (an arbiter ruling), not a finding of the GM's or the record's. No live map changes: the shipped Sawada manifest is the Python seat's. None of this narrows anything the GM asked for.

decisions.id: T261-D2 the fallback only on a fall toward the wind
decisions.summary: seat.rs::seat's off-wind fallback fired on any empty first ranking, so a rolled crosswind map with every wind-facing margin refused would have been seated off the wind against the page. It now fires only on a fall toward the wind, and such a map is refused by name. Pinned red-first by seat::tests::only_a_fall_toward_the_wind_backs_the_hill; 1,000 cohort seeds, 0 refused.
decisions.why: This fixes a known defect in the step where it was found, as the GM's 2026-11-18 fix-as-we-go rule asks: a rolled map seated against the record is a wrong outcome, not merely a difference. A test that fails only when the defect is present is enforcement of the request, not added scope. The cohort run is offered as evidence that no valid rolled map is now refused.

decisions.id: T261-D3 the seat claim and SeatRefused's doc restated
decisions.summary: The seat claim stops attributing 'the high side and the windward side one side' to 0031 (no 0031 file carries it, grep 2026-11-22), and SeatRefused's doc ('never seated off the wind', false since T27) is restated.
decisions.why: Restating a claim and a doc comment that no longer describe the code or the record is the restating that T196 and FR-002 prescribe. Nothing about behavior changes.

decisions.id: T261-D4 the belt on an off-wind seat filed as T277
decisions.summary: The finding that an off-wind seat keeps 0072's windward belt ground behind its back, uphill, is not fixed in T261. It is filed as T277 (the belt is drawn in driver.rs, T240's file, and whether the belt follows the wind or the back is 0072's record question), set to land before T158.
decisions.why: Nothing is left unfixed: the finding is filed as its own task and ordered to land before T158, so the fix-as-we-go rule (fix each step's known defects before the next step's port begins) still holds. Whether it is even a defect is a record question of 0072's, which belongs to a page session of its own and does not arise from row 141. Putting work on another task's file into a separate filed task is scheduling within the step, not a narrowing of the request.

E1 (office reaches its granary only through the garden), E2 (a bare 31 x 31 ft corner) and Q1 (the shrine's door on a cart apron) are wrong outcomes a reader of the sheet sees, i.e. defects, not differences.

A labeled guess consistent with the finding is not a defect (constitution XIV), and nothing the GM asked is narrowed.

decisions.why: Follows from moving the granary out of the household's court; it served only the removed seat.

decisions.summary: T259: `make work-budget WRITE=1` writes `meta.code`, `tree`'s worktree_key of HAMLET_READS (the ratchet's key of the same reads), taken before the counting run starts; previously runs carried the Python `code_id` (114) or the Rust port's `rev-parse --short HEAD` (12).
decisions.why: The defect, measured 2026-11-22, is a wrong outcome: an audit judged counts of code other than the code it read (the waterward.polder round read a run 180 lines behind; the newest run was stale on the landed tree). decisions.id: T259-D3 newest matching run, refuse where none
decisions.summary: T259: the audit bundle takes the newest run whose key is the tree's (key text searched first, other code's runs never parsed; a run holding the key that does not read fails), and refuses where none matches, naming the newest and `make work-budget WRITE=1`; it does not re-run.
decisions.why: Refusal is what the task line asks (per the block), and it gives the audit what FR-008 owes: counts of this code or no verdict, never a stale one. decisions.summary: T259: the ledger cannot recover how often an earlier audit read a stale run (no bundle but one names its run); no retrospective re-audit is planned.

decisions.id: D1 option A, command named make maps
decisions.summary: Build the one self-scoping command as `make maps` (the name the clause already uses, free since T223), over the Rust sweeps; the clause kept.
decisions.why: This is the GM's 2026-11-22 ruling as written: build the one self-scoping command over the Rust sweeps and keep the clause. Using the name the clause already holds is how the ruling is carried out, not a narrowing of it.

decisions.summary: One record, .git/maps-state.json per checkout, drives both the scope and the verbosity. One record, not one per row: a failure in any row narrows every row's next run.
decisions.why: The block quotes the clause's one-state rule, and a per-row record would depart from it, so taking one record keeps the clause the GM kept. Bundle gap: Constitution VI's text is not in the bundle, so this is checked against the block's own quotation of the clause. The half-second-a-row cost it cites is a proxy, because pool map was not timed, but the decision rests on the clause and not on that cost.

decisions.summary: After a passed run, every row runs whole and every failure is collected. After a failed run, or with no last run, each row's reference runs, stopping at the first problem, and the same run widens once every reference is clean. SCOPE=reference|all overrides.
decisions.why: These are the clause's self-scoping and SCOPE= override, which the GM's ruling keeps. They are checked against the block's quotations of the clause (bundle gap as in D2).

decisions.summary: TIER=<row> runs a single row.
decisions.why: An extra explicit override. It removes nothing from the self-scoping default the ruling asks for, so it narrows nothing.

decisions.id: D5 tier rows now: hamlets and mode-a; larger tiers added as they land
decisions.summary: TIERS holds two rows today. Villages, towns and cities add their rows when they land.
decisions.why: The GM's question ('once we implement villages, towns, provincial cities, and capital cities') is about tiers not yet built. The ruling asks for the command over the Rust sweeps that exist, and leaves a row for each later tier. Nothing that exists is left out.

decisions.summary: Reference: Inashiro, via pool map plus hamlet --check. Whole run: pool map of every pool hamlet, hamlet --check of each, and hamlet --cohort 1 48.
decisions.why: A reference and a whole run for the existing hamlet sweep. Inashiro is called the clause's canonical hamlet. Nothing in request.md or the spec names a different reference.

decisions.summary: county-magistracy-example, a generated compound, is the Mode A reference.
decisions.why: Choosing the reference a tier row needs is part of building the command. Neither request.md nor the spec names another Mode A reference (spec-index grep for reference/tier/shrine/magistr finds none). The plan's 'the session approved it' carries no authority and is not relied on; the choice is within either way.

decisions.id: D8 one mode-a row for magistracies and country-shrines
decisions.summary: Every Mode A building type with a pool folder shares one row and one reference. Its whole run is pool map of every live Mode A map and then the mode_a crate tests, the pool sweep among them.
decisions.why: Purpose walk for a change that breaks only a country shrine. After a passed run, the whole run's pool sweep judges every live Mode A map, so it is caught. After a failed run or with no run, the magistracy reference is clean, the same run widens, and the whole run catches it. No state ends a bare `make maps` without judging the shrine, so only the early stop is lost and nothing goes unchecked. In words, the GM asked for the command 'over the Rust sweeps', and Mode A is one sweep (`make rust-test CRATE=rust/mode_a`). The tiers the GM named are settlement sizes, not Mode A building types. The spec carries no per-building-type reference requirement. Bundle gap: whether the clause's 'reference per tier' reaches Mode A building types is judged from the block's quotation only.

decisions.id: D9 ordering: reference first, narrow run a prefix of a wide one
decisions.summary: Each whole run starts with its reference, and widening re-runs the references inside the whole runs.
decisions.why: An implementation of the clause's narrowing and widening, with no change of scope.

decisions.summary: Add l7r-mode-a sweep <map> (the pool sweep's compose, with_context and judge moved out of cfg(test)) and hamlet --check <spec> (a new spec_check.rs), because a draw judges no rule.
decisions.why: Without a judge the reference step would prove nothing, since a draw passes a hamlet with refusals and a cached map runs nothing. So these serve the command the GM asked for. Both are read-only and add no behavior beyond judging what is already judged.

decisions.id: D11 Launch trait and fake in tests
decisions.summary: Steps run through a Launch trait, so the tests drive a fake and meet the line-coverage floor without cargo or a map.
decisions.why: A test design that serves FR-004's coverage floor. It is not a scope decision.

decisions.id: D12 make map MAP= and make rust-test CRATE=rust/mode_a stay callable
decisions.summary: The two existing commands remain beside make maps, and make maps calls their underlying launcher steps.
decisions.why: The ruling asks for the one self-scoping command to exist 'over the Rust sweeps'. It does not ask for the sweeps it runs to be removed, and make maps is built over them. The pair guard's assertion (no gate) stands unchanged.

decisions.summary: VI's tier-table sentence names maps.rs where it named mapcheck.py. T228's note says the clause was kept and the command rebuilt. The efficiency-tooling row and the make-docs prose are updated, and make-targets.html is regenerated. The pair-guard comment is updated. The 1.12.0 and 1.12.1 history entries keep their words.
decisions.why: The GM's ruling says to put the new command's name in as upkeep, and the plan does exactly that. Leaving the historical entries untouched is right: they are records, not operative text.

decisions.id: D14 pool map untimed; end-to-end make maps run after the commit
decisions.summary: pool map is not timed, because it rewrites tracked pool files while other builders edit them. Done is shown by make maps SCOPE=reference running clean and a bare make maps then going wide.
decisions.why: A verification-timing choice that leaves out nothing the GM asked for. The end-to-end run is still owed and named in item 9.

decisions.id: D15 make cohort's slower cargo-run path left
decisions.summary: make cohort takes 4.4-4.8 s against the launcher's 0.59 s for the same seeds. It is not filed.
decisions.why: Same outcome and slower time, so not a wrong outcome and not a defect under constitution XIV. The whole run uses the launcher's binary anyway.

decisions.why: The research pass found the sources silent on both points, so there is no wrong outcome to fix: under constitution XIV and the GM 2026-11-19 ('don't spend a lot of time fixing things which are not actually wrong'), a silence is fixed by stating it in the record, not by changing the drawing. Not a defect left, so no narrowing.

decisions.summary: T275: the record gains the room order, the silences, and a mislabel fix (0097's 'prefectural designation' corrected to the national historic-site text) via a page session on 0093, 0097, 0123
decisions.why: A wrong statement in the record is a defect and gets fixed as found, as the GM asked 2026-11-18 ('fix broken things as we find them').

decisions.summary: T276: 'optional' dropped from the armory item in types.json so program_complete refuses a seat with no armory; red first on exactly the four sheets that drew none
decisions.why: Knob 4 says every seat keeps an armory and four sheets drew none, so the research claim was contradicted and the check was passing bad work. Both are defects under XIV. The changed check only fails when the armory is absent, so it enforces the fix rather than adding scope (GM 2026-09-20).

decisions.summary: T276: each seat's armory placed by knob 4 and its gate form: one-bay-gate seats (Ochiba, the round-trip) take the hall's west end; gate-range seats (Hayakawa, Ubame) roll the armory-site knob from the map's seed (Hayakawa office hall, Ubame gate range's west room, formerly a gate-keepers' room whose use was a guess); every size inside the types.json band
decisions.why: This applies knob 4 as written: a gate range where one stands is a knob, the hall's west end where none does. decisions.summary: belt_off measures the canvas room on the band's swept windward fringe (margins::belt_swept, 36-146 ft, BELT_ACROSS, cut to the margin's dry side) in place of the rectangle off the band's windward-most corner; BELT_BAND.1 lead unchanged
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome (a seat refused or scored for room its belt does not need: 0.442 off the canvas where the fringe's belt stands wholly on it); no constant moved, no requirement or research finding narrowed; fix-as-we-go (GM 2026-11-18).

decisions.summary: the belt's planting target is 0072's 'each cluster carries its own band along its windward edge', the band hugging it, which the deleted placer's fringe_profile also drew; belt_swept is the band and its copy carried along the wind, their hull, cut by the Rust constants BELT_BAND, BELT_ACROSS and the margin
decisions.why: Tied to 0072's quoted sentence and derived geometrically from existing Rust constants, not a port of the Python's per-column walk (2026-11-19, rebuilding from derivations); the Python is cited only as the earlier drawing of the same finding.

decisions.summary: no Rust belt planter is built; the bundle corrects the seat's canvas room (driver::roll, belt_off) and the kept ground (settlement_ground) in already-ported code
decisions.why: Builds no parked hamlet stage (2026-11-21, stop before the parked hamlet stages): the block states no Rust belt planter exists and none is added; only room and kept-ground readings of ported code change.

decisions.summary: settlement_ground(frame, wind) becomes the hull of the old strip and the belt's swept ground to BELT_FAR_FT, widened never narrowed; the hem, dry_on_settlement and seat_on_dike read it
decisions.why: Fixes a wrong outcome (the dashed kept ground leaving the belt's end out, the hem able to lay 3-8 percent of the belt's ground at Sawada's 240-250 degree falls); widens what is kept, narrows nothing asked; maps may change (XIII, GM 2026-11-17).

decisions.summary: a polder seat's belt follows the map's wind on the windward side the polder leaves dry (SeatIn::belt_wind), the village kept off the dike (0019), labeled GUESS where the research pass found the choice silent; Kuwabata's dashed ground reaches 103 ft north, never toward the dike
decisions.why: Fixes the polder seat's belt room being asked of the shore's way; the research pass is recorded (between houses and dike SILENT, dry windward side ATTESTED ONLY FOR the northwest as the wind rule, dike trees NOT ATTESTED), the record silent on the choice, and the route taken is labeled a GUESS (the algorithmically easier one) on 0019's and 0072's pages; it contradicts no finding and narrows no clause of the request.

decisions.summary: windbreak_default prints no card for a regional wind outside REGIONAL_QUARTERS (NW, N, W), per 0072; no live writer pairs regional with SE today
decisions.why: A cheap guard keeping a card from contradicting a research finding (0072: belts on the north and west or one of the two), which is a wrong outcome were it reached; it narrows no requirement, refuses only an input no live writer produces, and is not time spent re-fixing a working difference (XIV).

decisions.summary: County main gate moved 140 -> 191.5 ft onto the genkan door's line (0104); senior retainers' long-house 24 x 50 -> 22 x 60 ft in karo-rank bays (a GUESS, T320 Q5).

decisions.summary: 22 x 25.5 ft of dead ground left before the servants' doors (39 ft before), labeled a GUESS, not filled further.

Filling the ground would break a size band, and so contradict research. The remainder is a labeled bare yard, not a wrong outcome.

The placements (the free run, the 12x24 dwelling, three men a dwelling, the cell's join) are labeled GUESS or SILENT where no page settles them. Room was measured before packing (the 47 ft run).

decisions.summary: four rowhouse dwellings of 12x24 ft; the servants' dwellings 15 -> 12 ft and the stables 12 ft west to make room
decisions.why: About 59 sq ft a man, below the barracks' 88, is a defect a review found. Eight options were measured on trial specs before drawing. The servants' 15 ft was a GUESS no page sizes, so changing it narrows nothing the GM or a page asked for.

decisions.summary: emit.rs cell draws a bar beside a court-face door that holds none, pinned by a_cells_bars_show_beside_its_door
decisions.why: This carries out ask:cell-lattice-hidden-449-T351 (CONTINUE): the north door is kept, the fewest sheets change (the round trip's svg sha256 is unchanged), legibility is judged on the PNG and the fix is pinned by a test. The cell's round-two glyph-check PASS covers F1 and F2.

decisions.summary: ochiba practice ground turned to the west wall; ubame's cart lane and parley path in one group; notes and docs claims brought to the drawing; the off-topic day-office paragraph cut; the writing-rooms Depiction restated for mirrored rows
decisions.why: Notes and claims untrue of the drawing are defects under XIV, and fixing them is fix-as-we-go.

decisions.summary: ask:glyph-occasions-emit-449-T351's discharge of 48 units restated to the landing drawing, re-measured per data-kind with data-id stripped
decisions.why: This answers round one's condition. The ruling's own last clause governs: a kind whose marks change after it is 'owed again under the rule', and the rule owes a check for a new element, a redrawn glyph or a substantially changed placement rule. After 07:30Z only the county's spec (E1) and emit.rs fn cell changed (ask:glyph-pass-carried-cell-fix-449-T351's diff), so no placement rule changed. That makes the stables and wells, displaced with their shapes kept, class C by the ruling's own wording ('the same glyphs displaced'), though the ruling's named C list did not carry them. The fourth dwelling's door is class C ('doors and tubs following their buildings'). The latrines' leaders are caption-only, a class the ruling discharged. Every kind whose shape changed has a PASS on a drawing at or after its last change: the servants' quarters (owed and checked PASS), the cell (round two PASS at the landing key), and the retainers' quarters, granary and gatehouse (PASS at cef72b9db8d3, carried). Every other kind's marks are unchanged.

decisions.summary: four glyph PASSes from cef72b9db8d3 carried to landing key 0e6a69cceff6
decisions.why: ask:glyph-pass-carried-cell-fix-449-T351 grants exactly this carry, bound to the 9bd9e35ca4..7e08b45d82 diff in which only fn cell, a test and the county's notes changed. The round trip's svg sha256 is unchanged, and nothing since reaches beyond fn cell.

decisions.summary: hayakawa, ochiba, ubame and the round trip keep their PASS at the new engine key
decisions.why: ask:reowed-reviews-unchanged-449-T351 binds each to its content key, and the block re-measured them as unchanged in the clone (l7r-gate reviews prereq content-key, 2026-11-23). The county's own review was run as owed and passed.

decisions.summary: the push reads no arbiter accept on a glyph unit or a carried review, so the lander cites the rulings; T377 builds the route with the whole-legend fallback's fix
decisions.why: This answers round one's condition: the route is named. ask:glyph-occasions-emit-449-T351 says the discharge is 'cited by its trigger id' at this landing, and that where the push has no route, 'that route is built with the fix and its test'. The fix is the whole-legend fallback, which T377 owns. Building the route with it is what the ruling orders, not a carve-out.

decisions.summary: T369, T371-T373, T377, T380-T384, T386-T391 filed, each landing before T158
decisions.why: Each is outside this bundle's files (research pages, tooling, rows of types.json this bundle did not change), or is a nitpick or outside finding on a PASS sheet whose fix would re-owe its review. Taken separately, the county's two latrine leaders are this bundle's own change on a sheet that was NEEDS-WORK at the time, not a PASS sheet. They still stay within: the landing-key county building-review PASSed and raised nothing on the change, and the latrines' marks are discharged as caption-only, so no reader-visible wrong outcome is left. Premise not verifiable from the bundle: that T158 is the next step's port, which would make 'lands before T158' the GM's 'fix all known bugs in each step before moving on' (2026-11-18). The 0104 porch and 0113 back-row items are differences between a page's wording and a drawing, not defects in the drawing.

decisions.summary: the review prerequisite attributed to feature 240's FR-003; 14 verifying records and 31 review-accepts dispose its 45 findings
decisions.why: This answers round one's condition and decides nothing new.

decisions.summary: cart_route's granary refusal points at an office-court flank column's head (0123's drawing page), pinned by a test
decisions.why: A refusal pointing at a seat 0123 rejects is a wrong outcome (XIV); fixing it is the GM's fix-as-we-go (2026-11-18).

decisions.summary: hearing court mats keyed to the dais axis; the round trip's '102 ft' claim restated to the 94 ft drawn
decisions.why: The accused kneeling 8 ft off the magistrate contradicts 0099. Restating the 102 ft claim, not the code, is the GM's 2026-11-19 rule.

decisions.summary: an open-shed interior (hatched roof, six posts, no door) for the cinnabar workshop
decisions.why: The workshop drawn as a shrine with a door is a map that reads wrong; this is a defect fix.

decisions.summary: knob 4's second roll, armory end bay [west, east], taken only under the hall site; armory.rs claims restated to ask:armory-store-ubame route (a)'s reach, with the end bay given a claim of its own
decisions.why: Judged against the ruling's own why: (b) was refused because it put a nested 1-in-3 roll behind a GUESSED knob that turns one site into another, and (a) adds no new GUESS and no rule a source lacks. The end-bay roll turns no site into another. It chooses between two forms 0123 attests (Pingyao, Jiexiu, Zhenping) under the one site route (a) picks, and a knob of several attested forms is the project's rule. Every hall armory drawn on the west contradicts 0123's varied side, which is a defect. The ruling's 'what' already allows an armory to move under a later engine change as no reversal, provided its pop-up says what it draws, and the pop-up is confirmed to name no fixed end (hayakawa x 638-680 px, round trip 549-591 px, observed 2026-11-23).

decisions.summary: types.json drops optional on magistrates_dais; a magistracy drawn without its dais is refused
decisions.why: A hall without a dais passing is a check that passes bad work, a defect under XIV.

decisions.why: The finding (a reader hovering li in 0093's notes told only a mile) is fixed, not left: the fix is carried by another task's landing. Folding a fix into the bundle that already carries it removes nothing the GM asked for; the 2026-11-22 'finish the remaining fixes' and 2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs' are honored. The red exit (record what failed, rule a cannot-be-done claim through make arbiter-ask) keeps it from being quietly dropped.

decisions.summary: 3760-li.json's definition gives the three senses the record uses (the ward of 110 households, the li of distance, the li of silver) and the term is cased; Kang Pil-li gets its own term file so the name's li does not resolve to the glossary li
decisions.why: A wrong outcome a reader would see (a ward glossed as a mile) fixed from the record's own text per the research glossary rule; the second file is the direct means of not mis-glossing a personal name. No scope beyond the defect.

decisions.summary: Done measured by the built glossary.js carrying the definition and cased flag, make record-owed and make claims-owed owing nothing new, and a dated whole-word search for li over fragments, notes, registry and pop-ups
decisions.why: Verification that the requested fix happened and broke nothing; enforcement of the fix, not unrequested scope. Figures are dated one-shot observations (2026-11-23) with their method.

decisions.summary: Where redrawn.rs cannot tell which kinds a change redraws (a kind chosen at run time, emit.rs building; a line of the sheet's roll, compound.rs sheet), each compound map's drawing is compared kind by kind with its drawing at the base in a new owed/marks.rs, and a kind is owed only where its marks differ.
decisions.why: This is the tooling fix the arbiter's accept on ask:glyph-occasions-emit-449-T351 calls for: (2) rules the whole-legend fallback a tool fault, and the why says it sends checks to byte-identical marks. Owing a kind where its marks differ applies the glyph-check occasion rule (new, redrawn, placement changed) to what was actually drawn. It is also what the GM asked for on 2026-11-16 (process time) and 2026-11-22 (finish the remaining fixes).

decisions.summary: Each token goes to its own data-kind or data-part-of, else to the enclosing element's. data-id is stripped. A changed <defs> entry owes every kind that uses it, transitively.
decisions.why: Data-id stripped and per-kind attribution are the method the ruling measured with ('data-id stripped, each line attributed to its kind'). The transitive defs rule makes sure a glyph redrawn through a shared definition is still owed, so it enforces the occasion rule and narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: A kind whose marks differ is owed on the first map where they differ, which moves the office hall's back-row kinds from the county (unchanged there) to the round trip (changed there).
decisions.why: A kind is owed once across the maps both before and after (the before row: the county's legend plus only the round-trip kinds the county does not draw). The plan now picks the first map where the marks differ, which matches the ruling's 'each on the map where its change shows'. No unit whose marks differ is dropped.

decisions.summary: The base text is the base commit's blob, else the mirror's copy, read as base_legends reads it.
decisions.why: This is how the comparison is implemented. It decides nothing about scope.

decisions.summary: Where the marks cannot be compared, the whole legend is still owed: the hamlet driver (its marks are not read by kind), a drawing that is not current, a drawing the base does not hold, or a difference no kind owns. The occasion says which.
decisions.why: The ruling calls the whole-legend fallback a tool fault in general, and the fix leaves it in these cases, so I treat this as a narrowing. It is legitimate because per-kind comparison is physically impossible in each case: no attribution by kind (the hamlet driver), no current drawing, no base drawing, or a difference with no owning kind. In every one the fallback owes more checks, never fewer, so a glyph the occasion rule owes is never missed. The ruling measured only compound maps, so no defect is measured or known in these cases, and nothing a reader sees on a map is wrong. Each such occasion is named, so the fallback stays visible.

decisions.summary: What the code itself tells (a literal data-kind in a changed mark, or a writer method whose uses reach one) stays owed as before (T237, T289). This is pinned by the_compound_engines_marks_owe_their_kinds_on_the_compound.
decisions.why: It keeps the existing reading of the code and owes more, never less. The ruling does not ask for code-told units to be dropped: it lets the caption-only and kneeling units 'still be listed' and discharges them itself.

decisions.summary: New verb l7r-gate reviews discharge --root R --ruling TRIGGER UNIT... (owed/discharged.rs; make review-discharge RULING= UNITS=). It records an arbiter accept against each owed glyph unit, bound to the digest of that kind's current marks, all or none. all_owed drops a unit only while its ruling still reads accept and its marks keep the digest. reviews owed --why names each discharged unit and its ruling.
decisions.why: The ruling asks for this route in its own words: 'If the push has no route that reads an arbiter accept as a glyph unit's discharge, that route is built with the fix and its test.' Binding to the marks digest implements 'If a sheet changes again before the push, any kind whose marks change is owed again under the rule.' The make target keeps make as the one entry point (FR-005).

decisions.summary: Before it writes anything, the verb refuses a ruling that is not an accept in some specs/*/arbiter.jsonl, a unit not owed now, a unit that is not a glyph check, and a unit on a map that draws no mark of its kind.
decisions.why: These refusals keep the route inside what the ruling authorizes, an arbiter accept discharging glyph units bound to marks. They block nothing the GM or the ruling asked to happen.

decisions.summary: The verb cannot tell which units a ruling discharged, or whether the marks are the ones the ruling measured. So a push names only the units the cited ruling discharged, by name or by a class the ruling states, and only where that kind's marks are unchanged (marks.rs rule) between the drawing the ruling measured and the drawing being recorded. The push states both, unit by unit, in its own plan section. Units the ruling kept owed, units an unrelated accept does not name, and units whose marks differ stay owed.
decisions.why: It holds the discharge to exactly the ruling's scope ('the 48 units named above', 'bound to the drawn sheets as measured') where the tool cannot check it, and it keeps owed everything the ruling keeps owed. A digest taken at record time could otherwise bind to marks that changed after the ruling, and this closes that gap. It widens nothing.

decisions.summary: The T351 bundle's landing carries its three arbiter rulings at its own push and records no discharge through this verb, so the unit list such a discharge would have named is moot and dropped from this section.
decisions.why: The ruling requires the route to exist, and D7 builds it. It does not require T377 to use the route for T351. How T351's push carries its rulings belongs to T351's own landing, and not using the verb leaves units owed rather than unowed. None of the ruling's five owed units, and no unit whose marks changed, is discharged by this choice.

decisions.summary: A make target review-discharge was added (Makefile block after review-verdict, row in docs/make-targets.html) so a landing reaches the verb without calling the gate binary directly.
decisions.why: It serves FR-005 (make the one entry point) and only exposes the route the ruling asked for.

decisions.summary: the round arbiter accepted T383 and T384 and T388 and T391's section as it stands

T383: aligned_gaps' blocked set counts a drawn practice ground (plan.fills rect of kind PRACTICE_GROUND) as laid-out ground, so the pack audit stops listing it as a vacancy; only report.rs calls it, no sheet moves.
decisions.why: Fixes a listing that named a vacancy where ground is drawn (a check answering wrongly, a defect under XIV); the GM's 2026-11-18 'fix all known bugs in each step' and 2026-11-22 'please finish the remaining fixes'. Pinned by a red test.

decisions.summary: T384: block_pair meets a shared span at its middle (span_middle, nearer()) instead of the first candidate, a CONVENTION where 0330 leaves the end open; leader_span returns the span's Slide.
decisions.why: Fixes the county's privy leader running from the privy's corner along the stables' wall (a leader that reads as wall, a wrong outcome). Inside the fixes the GM asked be finished; the convention fills a point research leaves open.

decisions.summary: T384: Placer::led keeps the middle unless it meets other ink, else draws the middle of the least-ink run along the span; the slide is applied only to the drawn leader in seat(), not inside the sweep, because inside the sweep it moved Ochiba's latrine caption under a wall.
decisions.why: A choice of mechanism measured on the pool (Ubame's altar leader clears the post with it; the in-sweep variant produced a worse map). Narrows nothing the GM asked; the goal (leaders read clear) is served.

decisions.summary: T384: stroke_end carries its span's slide, held on a dashed stroke to its dash (dash_part); a dash's end takes the butt flat-end rule (segment_at), fixing an end up to half a stroke into the gap on main since T202.
decisions.why: Fixes impl-drift's rounds 1 and 2 code findings with red tests; the arbiter (ask:449-t383-claims-round3) accepted the bundle on exactly this code. Fixing a pre-existing defect found on the way is the GM's fix-as-we-go.

decisions.summary: T384: stables_well is seated within its court face's span, its GUESS claim restated; a court-door stable whose face leaves no room for the well is refused its well aloud (no pool sheet draws one).
decisions.why: Fixes a well standing off its stable (wrong outcome). The loud refusal replaces a wrong drawing on a case no pool sheet reaches (constitution: fail loudly rather than draw wrong); not a defect left, so no ruling.

decisions.summary: T384 table: a leader no slide clears keeps the middle and is filed.
decisions.why: A fallback that files rather than hides any leader the rules cannot clear; consistent with fixing every known defect in the step through a filed task.

decisions.summary: T388: a stables interior with no declared door opens on its west gable (north where the court face runs north-south) at the passage's middle, per 0108's gable-entered warrior's stable; which gable and the depths are GUESSES.
decisions.why: Fixes horses led through the grooms' lodging (a map that reads wrong); research-grounded, guesses labeled as knobs.

decisions.summary: T388: room for the lane made by drawing the guessed gatehouse 37.5 ft (inside its kind's band; spec's sizes line, notes and a dated entry restated) after trials; a 3 ft wider envelope priced and refused for growing the outer court's west-column vacancy.
decisions.why: Constitution XII room-before-packing, a GUESS constant moved inside its band with its source restated; the docs/pop-up 'about 40 ft' still describes it. No narrowing of what was asked.

decisions.summary: T388: CART_LANE (a GUESS on 0082's cart lane past the tub) and door_lane seat a granary or stable whose door is on an end with the lane on that end; seat_one keeps FIRE_GAP - CLEAR off the row's end on the door's side in every branch; CART_KINDS names granary (0082) and stables (GUESS).
decisions.why: Fixes a tub leaving a cart 2.73 ft of a 6 ft lane, and the row-end case impl-drift round 1 found, each pinned by red tests; the arbiter ruled the lane widened to fit the cart, not packed.

decisions.summary: T391: the diffrun timeout test calibrates its window from a loop of `true` runs just before the case (never under the old timeout), per CLAUDE.md's calibration convention; run.rs SECOND made pub(crate).
decisions.why: Fixes a gate test that goes red on a loaded machine with nothing wrong (a check refusing good work); measured red unfixed and green fixed under pinned load.

decisions.summary: Left: a granary or stables with doors declared on both ends holds a cart lane at one end only (door_lane's find_map); no pool sheet declares one; filed as T397, landing before T158.
decisions.why: A real but unreached defect (visible effect stated). The arbiter's ruling asks it fixed 'in this step', and the GM's rule is to fix known bugs in each step before porting the next; filing it as T397 to land before T158 keeps it inside the step, so the bundle defers it without carrying it past the step. Legitimate only on that ordering.

decisions.summary: Left: seat_one seats a gatehouse beside its gate only, where 0093 attests one behind the gate too; filed as T398 (roll the form or restate the claim), landing before T158.
decisions.why: The arbiter ruled it a choice of form, not a defect; under constitution XIV (T196) a difference that reads fine is not a defect, so leaving it is within and needs no ruling.

decisions.summary: Left: Ochiba's 'latrine' leader runs 68.7 px through the stables, the same on main, a hand sheet's crossing fallback no T384 rule moves; filed as T395, landing before T158.
decisions.why: A defect (a reader takes the latrine's name for the stables') carved out of T384's goal 'every caption's leader reads clear'. Not introduced by this bundle and needs a different mechanism from the tie-break T384 fixed; filed with its visible effect to land before T158, i.e. within the step, as the GM's fix-all-known-bugs-before-the-next-step allows. Legitimate only on that ordering.

decisions.summary: Left: make pack-audit lists the new 9.3 ft cart lane as a LOOSE aligned gap; every check OK.
decisions.why: A true measurement of deliberate unbuilt ground, not a check failing; no wrong outcome under XIV.

decisions.summary: Left: the gatehouse pop-up and docs/building-programs.md say 'about 40 ft' (a GUESS) while the county draws 37.5 ft; other builders' files left.
decisions.why: 37.5 ft is about 40 ft and the round trip still draws 40; a difference from wording, not a defect (XIV).

decisions.summary: Claims round closed after round 2 by the arbiter's accept (ask:449-t383-claims-round3); the record bundle's page-edit claims left to that bundle; occasions: layout-revised building-review on county, round trip, Ochiba, Ubame, none for T383 and T391.
decisions.why: Follows the arbiter's recorded ruling verbatim (both round-2 out-of-change findings filed as T397 and T398); review scope matches the sheets the change moves.
